title: Monetize Your Git Repositories for AI Training
description:
We are connecting with software companies, development agencies, product teams, and independent engineers that own original codebases and want to explore a new revenue stream through AI training licenses.

It is a licensing opportunity for organizations and individuals that already have valuable repositories they own and are legally able to license.

Eligible repositories can include active products, archived projects, internal tools, legacy systems, unsuccessful products, or other original codebases that still hold technical value.

How it works?

  • Connect selected Git repositories for technical review.
  • Submit only repositories you own or are authorized to license.
  • Receive an assessment of repository size, structure, and licensing potential.
  • Review the estimated value before deciding whether to proceed.
  • Receive technical feedback where a repository needs improvement before it can qualify.
  • Update and resubmit repositories where appropriate.
  • Choose which approved repositories you want to make available for AI training.
  • Receive payment when qualifying code is licensed and used.

Compensation

For standard non-exclusive licensing, current reference rates are:

  • $100 per 1M source-code tokens
  • $40 per 1M Git-history tokens

Each repository is assessed individually, and you can review the estimated value before deciding whether to move forward.

If you have repositories that are no longer generating value commercially, this can create an additional revenue stream from code you already own — without selling the IP outright. Your code remains yours under a non-exclusive licensing model, subject to the agreed licensing terms.

Requirements

  • You must own the code or have clear legal authority to license it.
  • Repositories should contain meaningful original software development work.
  • You must be authorized to connect and submit the repository for evaluation.
  • Code must not include third-party material that you are not permitted to sublicense.
  • Repositories must pass technical and quality checks before licensing.
  • Ownership or licensing rights may need to be verified.

title: Sustainability Data & Carbon Analyst
description:
Could you be Incommunities new Sustainability Data & Carbon Analyst? This is an exciting time to join us ahead of the launch of our new Sustainability strategy. You'll play a key role by collecting, validating and analysing environmental and carbon data, providing a robust evidence base for decision-making. The role will support accurate carbon, ESG and sustainability reporting, using insight to identify emissions hotspots and opportunities to drive carbon reduction across homes, assets and operations.

About us

We are a social housing landlord and one of the largest housing providers in the region with over 22,000 social and affordable homes, mainly in the Bradford district. We employ a talented workforce of nearly 1,000 people.

In 2024 we’ve launched our five-year Corporate Strategy, which runs to 2029. Our purpose is to provide high quality homes, services, and support to our customers, so we’ve worked with colleagues and customers to find out what’s important to them. Our customers sit at the heart of what we do, and our colleagues are the people who’ll help us achieve our vision, which is to create the best customer experience to improve everyday lives.

Duties include:

  • Collect, validate and maintain environmental, energy and carbon data across homes, assets and operations.
  • Support the annual calculation and update of the organisation’s carbon footprint, including Scope 1, Scope 2 and relevant Scope 3 emissions.
  • Maintain and improve carbon datasets, reporting tools and data quality processes.
  • Analyse emissions trends, identify key hotspots and highlight opportunities for carbon reduction.
  • Track the impact of sustainability, retrofit and energy efficiency projects, providing clear reporting on outcomes and benefits.
  • Aid the development of evidence-based business cases for decarbonisation and energy efficiency initiatives.
  • Work with internal teams, including assets, finance, procurement and operations, to improve data accuracy and support delivery of carbon reduction activity.
  • Translate data and insight into clear information for colleagues, managers and decision makers.
  • Collaborate with external partners, consultants and suppliers to obtain data, validate information and support sustainability initiatives.
  • Provide clear evidence, insight and practical information to gain internal awareness and behaviour change activity
  • Assist ESG reporting, including SECR, SHIFT and internal sustainability reporting requirements.
  • Maintain sustainability KPIs and dashboards to track performance against carbon reduction targets.
  • Ensure carbon reporting methods are consistent, transparent and aligned with recognised carbon accounting principles where applicable.
  • Identify data gaps, reporting risks and quality issues, escalating these with proposed improvements.
  • Support responses to customer, investor, funder or regulatory sustainability queries.

Requirements

  • Knowledge of climate change, carbon reduction and sustainability principles.
  • Awareness of carbon accounting principles, including Scope 1, Scope 2 and Scope 3 emissions.
  • Knowledge of ESG and sustainability reporting requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and draw clear conclusions.
  • High attention to detail and accuracy when collecting, validating and reporting data.
  • Strong organisation skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and meet reporting deadlines.
  • High proficiency in Microsoft Office applications including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners.
  • Experience of carbon, sustainability, ESG or environmental reporting.
  • Experience using data dashboards, Power BI or other reporting tools.
  • Degree or equivalent experience in a relevant subject such as sustainability, environment, data, engineering, geography, housing or the built environment
  • Right to Work in the UK - Visa Sponsorship is not available.
  • Commutable distance of BD17 7BN and able to be onsite 2 days per week.

Benefits

  • Starting salary from £29,978 per year
  • Social Housing Pension Scheme with up-to 10% employer contribution
  • 28 days annual leave that increases with service plus bank holidays
  • Option to buy and sell annual leave
  • Training, development, and qualification opportunities
  • Our Hub: our wellbeing and benefits site, with exclusive access to discounts and savings (at over 800 retailers)
  • Corporate health scheme membership
  • Access to an Employee Assistance Programme
  • Cycle to work scheme
  • Local gym membership discounts.
  • A team of trained Mental Health First Aiders who are available for colleagues to contact for support

Join Our Team!

We’re looking for great people to join us! At Incommunities, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels valued, included, and supported. We actively welcome applicants from all backgrounds, abilities, and experiences—because we know that diverse perspectives make us stronger.

Based in Bradford, a city known for its rich cultural diversity, we serve vibrant communities. As a social housing provider, we’re passionate about making a real difference by providing safe, affordable homes and improving lives.

Our recruitment process is designed to support you every step of the way. If you need any adjustments or assistance, just let us know.

We’re proud to be a Mindful Employer, committed to mental health and wellbeing. We also hold the ‘Committed’ Menopause Friendly Accreditation, recognising the importance of support in the workplace.

💡 Apply early! We review applications as they come in and may close the advert before the deadline.

Ready to make an impact? Come work with us!

title: LAC Advocacy Intern 2027-1
description:
Job Title: LAC Advocacy Intern

Department: Global Legal Programs, Latin America & the Caribbean

Bogota Office

Center Background: The Center for Reproductive Rights is a global human rights organization working to ensure that reproductive rights are protected in law as fundamental human rights worldwide. With offices in New York City, and Washington, D.C.; Nairobi, Kenya; Bogota, Colombia; and Geneva, Switzerland, the Center is a non-profit, non-partisan organization changing law and policy throughout Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the United States. Our 270+ diverse professionals are committed to advancing the Center’s human rights mission through game-changing litigation, legal policy, and advocacy work. This has powered the Center’s exceptional growth to an operating budget of over $67 million and won the respect of law firms in countries around the world. Our global pro bono network includes over 3,000 lawyers across 6 continents, 64 countries, and 130 law firms. Last year, law firms contributed over $35 million USD in pro bono legal services. The Center’s Strategic Plan sets a high mark for impact: By 2030, half of the world’s population will be living under stronger protections for reproductive rights than they were in 2020. The Center has a record of success to back up this ambitious goal. Since our founding in 1992, the Center has transformed how reproductive rights are understood and applied by courts, governments, and human rights bodies worldwide on issues including maternal health, abortion, assisted reproduction, and adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights. We have won groundbreaking cases before national courts, U.N. Committees, and regional human rights bodies. The Center has also led development of historic, proactive legislation advancing robust protections for reproductive rights. It has built the legal capacity of women’s rights advocates in more than 65 countries and counting. To learn more about the Center, please go to

The Role:

The Center’s Bogota Office is looking for an enthusiastic, resourceful and highly organized intern with a commitment to reproductive rights issues to engage in a variety of mini projects related to the Colombia office. This internship will provide someone with experience in many aspects of as well as insight into the inner working of organizational management.

The internship is full-time, beginning January 12th, 2026 to July 10th, 2026.


Responsibilities: As an intern with LAC Office, your primary responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Assist members of our legal team with researching and writing reproductive rights-related submissions to United Nations and regional human rights bodies.
  • Assist of our Advocacy team with monitoring and documenting of media coverage of the Center and updating media placements archives.
  • Bluebooking and fact-checking as needed for current reports and publications.
  • Support administrative duties.
  • Monitor applications and concluding observations of UN committees as directed by the team
  • Following up requests for hearings before the CIDH.
  • Monitoring CIDH reports (thematic and country reports).

Qualifications:

  • Current Law or Government and International Relations student
  • Strong advocacy research and writing skills
  • Demonstrated an interest in gender/women's issues and reproductive rights
  • Taken Constitutional Law and International Law classes
  • Knowledge of human rights as well as a basic understanding of the Inter-American Human Rights System
  • Fluency in Spanish and English (B1), knowledge of Portuguese is a plus

How to Apply: Please click on the link below to apply. A cover letter, résumé and contact information for three references must be included in your application in order to be considered for this position. Please include these application materials as attachments.

Deadline for Applications: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

To learn more about our DEI Organizational Commitments, go here. The Center for Reproductive Rights is an equal opportunity employer, committed to inclusive hiring, and dedicated to diversity in our work and staff. We strongly encourage people from all groups and communities to apply.

Please note that all genuine Center openings must be applied through the Center website. The Center does not charge a fee at any stage in the recruitment process (application, interviews, or selection). Nor does it request any medical examinations or bank account inform as part of this process. Título del puesto: Practicante de Incidencia LAC 2026

Departamento: Programas Legales Globales, América Latina y el Caribe

Oficina de Bogotá

Antecedentes del Centro: El Centro de Derechos Reproductivos es una organización global de derechos humanos que trabaja para garantizar que los derechos reproductivos estén protegidos en la ley como derechos humanos fundamentales en todo el mundo. Con oficinas en Nueva York y Washington, D.C.; Nairobi, Kenia; Bogotá, Colombia; y Ginebra, Suiza, el Centro es una organización sin fines de lucro y no partidista que impulsa cambios en leyes y políticas en África, Asia, Europa, América Latina y el Caribe, y Estados Unidos.

Nuestros más de 270 profesionales diversos están comprometidos con avanzar la misión de derechos humanos del Centro a través de litigios transformadores, políticas legales y trabajo de incidencia. Esto ha impulsado el crecimiento excepcional del Centro, con un presupuesto operativo de más de 67 millones de dólares, y ha ganado el respeto de bufetes de abogados en países de todo el mundo. Nuestra red global de pro bono incluye a más de 3.000 abogados en 6 continentes, 64 países y 130 firmas legales. El año pasado, los bufetes de abogados contribuyeron con más de 35 millones de dólares en servicios legales pro bono.

El Plan Estratégico del Centro establece una meta ambiciosa de impacto: para 2030, la mitad de la población mundial vivirá bajo protecciones más sólidas para los derechos reproductivos que las que tenían en 2020. El Centro cuenta con un historial de éxito que respalda este objetivo ambicioso. Desde nuestra fundación en 1992, el Centro ha transformado la manera en que los derechos reproductivos son entendidos y aplicados por tribunales, gobiernos y organismos de derechos humanos en todo el mundo en temas como salud materna, aborto, reproducción asistida y salud y derechos sexuales y reproductivos de los adolescentes.

Hemos ganado casos históricos ante tribunales nacionales, Comités de la ONU y organismos regionales de derechos humanos. El Centro también ha liderado el desarrollo de legislación histórica y proactiva que impulsa protecciones sólidas para los derechos reproductivos. Además, ha fortalecido la capacidad legal de defensoras de los derechos de las mujeres en más de 65 países y en aumento.

Para obtener más información sobre el Centro, por favor visita: www.reproductiverights.org

Rol:

La oficina del Centro en Bogotá está buscando un pasante entusiasta, ingenioso y altamente organizado con un compromiso con los temas de derechos reproductivos para participar en una variedad de mini proyectos relacionados con la oficina de Colombia. Esta pasantía proporcionará a alguien experiencia en muchos aspectos, así como una visión del funcionamiento interno de la gestión organizacional. La práctica es de tiempo completo, comenzando el 12 de enero de 2026 y finalizando el 10 de julio de 2026.


Responsabilidades: Como practicante del Programa para América Latina y el Caribe del Centro de Derechos Reproductivos, sus actividades estarán enfocadas principalmente a:

· Asistir en la investigación y redacción de documentos legales relacionados con derechos reproductivos, dirigidos a órganos internacionales y regionales de derechos humanos.

· Asistir en el proceso de comprobación y verificación de las citas y fuentes bibliográficas de las publicaciones.

· Asistir en el monitoreo de prensa regional.

· Apoyar en la preparación de materiales para las acciones de incidencia a nivel regional e internacional.

· Apoyar actividades administrativas.

· Monitorear convocatorias y observaciones finales de comités de ONU según le indiquemos desde el equipo

· Estudiante de Derecho, Gobierno & Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Políticas o carreras afines.

· Gran capacidad de investigación y redacción

· Interés demostrado en cuestiones de género/mujeres y derechos reproductivos

· Haber tomado clases de Derecho Constitucional y Derecho Internacional

· Conocimiento de los derechos humanos así como una comprensión básica del Sistema Interamericano de Derechos Humanos

title: Quality Leader
description:
At Highland Spring Group, we’re proud of what we do, who we are, and the natural-source water we share with our customers. Every drop of Highland Spring comes from the majestic Ochil Hills, where we carefully protect 2,500 acres of natural, organic and untouched land.

We’re looking for a Quality Leader to join our Technical team at our Ochils site. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems, improving standards and working with others to make sure our products continue to meet the highest expectations for quality, food safety and compliance.

You’ll play an important role in maintaining site and Group Technical requirements, supporting our Quality Management System, leading allocated quality projects and helping drive continuous improvement across the site.

What you can expect:

In this role, you’ll help ensure our products are safe, legal, authentic and consistently high quality. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Investigating complaints, quality incidents and quarantines, identifying root causes and supporting effective corrective and preventative actions.
  • Maintaining the Ochils Quality Management System and supporting document control.
  • Managing and improving quality checks, including kiosk and SOP requirements.
  • Leading allocated quality projects that support site and Group objectives.
  • Reviewing kiosk data and identifying trends or improvement opportunities.
  • Completing GMP, traceability and shop floor compliance audits.
  • Supporting customer complaint responses and quality-related information requests.
  • Creating and maintaining retailer quality attribute sheets.
  • Collating technical data and Group information when required.
  • Completing scheduled TACCP horizon scanning.
  • Deputising for the Quality Manager and Technical Services Manager when needed.

About you:

We’re looking for someone who takes pride in their work, enjoys being part of a team and cares about doing things properly. You’ll be confident working with systems, standards and procedures, and you’ll be comfortable turning requirements into practical ways of working for the site.

You’ll ideally bring:

  • Experience in a similar quality or technical role, ideally within the food or drink industry.
  • A good understanding of food safety, quality systems and compliance requirements.
  • The ability to interpret accreditation standards and customer codes of practice, then translate them into workable site procedures.
  • Strong attention to detail and confidence handling documentation, data and audits.
  • A practical, collaborative approach to problem-solving.
  • Experience with retailer specifications, artwork sign-off systems or food labelling requirements would be beneficial.
  • A degree in Food Safety, Food Management, Food Science or a related subject would be helpful, but it is not essential.
  • Food Hygiene and HACCP training would also be advantageous, but we welcome candidates with relevant experience and a willingness to learn.

Our values guide how we do things at Highland Spring Group:

We’re a Team — we support each other, listen, problem-solve and work together to make things happen
We’re Proud — we take ownership, continuously improve and take pride in our products, our brand and our work
We Care — we respect each other, care about our customers, protect our environment and believe everyone should have a voice

This role would suit someone who is organised, curious and proactive; someone who is comfortable asking questions, sharing ideas and helping others do a good job.

If you could be our next Quality Leader, please apply today.

Please note, this role is Monday to Friday, 37.5 hours per week with a starting salary of £35,200 per annum.

title: Program Facilitator, FirstHand™
description:
Position Summary

About the Science Center
For 60 years, the West Philadelphia-based Science Center has been a leader and partner in innovation-driven regional economic development. Located at the heart of the uCity Square campus, home to over 200 businesses, the Science Center operates at the intersection of startups, healthcare, and community to drive inclusive growth across Greater Philadelphia and beyond.

About FirstHand™
The Science Center launched FirstHand in 2014 to provide equitable, high-quality STEM experiences to Philadelphia students in middle and high school. FirstHand offers a suite of free, industry-informed STEM curricula with no tests, grades, or homework through which students engage in the same hands-on tasks as professionals. Middle school students participate as a cohort and travel once a week, during school hours, for ten weeks (20 hours) to the FirstHand lab with a school chaperone. High school students participate in 8-week (approximately 16-hour), targeted career-exposure programs called “Sprints” that are co-developed and co-delivered by STEM professionals, and students are paid achievement-based stipends. All FirstHand cohorts are 16 students or less.

The Program Facilitator, FirstHand, will lead several of the University City Science Center’s (UCSC) FirstHand youth lab-based programs. This position will be responsible for organizing, facilitating, and leading 4 - 6 programs a week for middle school & high school Philadelphia youth that will run during normal business hours with occasional exceptions in the Science Center’s FirstHand Lab.

This is a hands-on program lead position, requiring the capacities to inspire and manage youth, coordinate in-person course delivery schedules, deliver high-quality STEM program facilitation, and maintain relationships with partners. The Program Facilitator should be comfortable in workshop and lab environments and engaging with students of diverse backgrounds and learning styles.

The Program Facilitator will collaborate with external partners and industry professionals to design new industry-aligned curricula and refine the existing curricula to continue to meet the needs of the 21st-century workforce. Additionally, this position works closely with the Director and Program Manager to develop and maintain partnerships that advance the Science Center’s role in youth education and programming.

This position has regular contact with community members and is expected to professionally represent the Science Center. The Program Facilitator, FirstHand has internal contacts with the entire staff of UCSC and external contact with scientists, designers, technologists, entrepreneurs, and the wider Philadelphia community. This position has access to sensitive UCSC information and is expected to handle such information with integrity and professionalism. The Program Facilitator is expected to follow Science Center policies and work cross-functionally with team members across UCSC.

The Program Facilitator will report directly to the Senior Manager, STEM Education Initiatives and participate in department activities as necessary.

Essential Functions

STEM Program Implementation and Coordination

· Works with the FirstHand Senior Manager to plan, coordinate, and facilitate approximately 4-6 multi-week youth programs in the FirstHand Lab which includes communicating with teachers and administration, coordinating transportation, and other related duties.

· Serves as a support role for FirstHand classes when not leading.

· Serves as point-of-contact for school chaperones from local youth-serving organizations, including schools and community-based organizations to ensure student participation.

· Works with the Senior Manager on recruiting and maintaining relationships with STEM mentors from the startup and entrepreneurial community in Philadelphia.

STEM Curriculum Design

· Works with Senior Manager and other FirstHand staff to refine and develop industry-relevant STEM curriculum, documenting internal curriculum.

· Documents and revises curricular outlines as well as student and mentor activities for internal and external use. Adheres to internal document sharing protocols (i.e. SharePoint).

· Engages with STEM mentors to create dynamic activities that showcase workplace skills and career pathways for FirstHand students. This includes activity orientation, one-on-one activity planning and coaching, and planning mentor recruitment events with the Senior Manager and the rest of Facilitation team.

Supporting Organizational Systems

· Attends relevant staff meetings to promote communication and execution of goals.

· Participates in reporting and evaluation activities to include scheduled site visits with funders, maintaining student attendance and mentor volunteer records, follows program budget protocols, and ensures appropriate grant compliance.

· Supports SC marketing team by promoting FirstHand via social media and networking functions.

· Completes special projects specific to the function of the department or as needed for the department under the guidance of the managers.

· Actively participates and engages in wider Science Center meetings, programs, and events.

· Adheres to UCSC’s security guidelines and ensures the appropriate handling of sensitive information.

· Facilitates and attends relevant staff meetings to promote communication and execution of goals.

· Other duties as assigned within the scope of position expectations.

title: QA Engineer
description:
Czym będziesz się zajmować?

Responsibilities:

  • Building and running test sessions directly from the Unity Editor: assemble builds, execute scenarios, capture logs and performance data.
  • Verifying object placement against design references, checking lighting/rendering correctness, memory usage per object, prop behavior, and collisions/geometry gaps at the seams between map blocks.
  • Verifying traversability of levels/maps – identifying non-traversable areas, geometric holes, and navigation issues.
  • Running performance testing across the agreed device matrix: Avg FPS, 1% Low FPS, Memory Peak, CPU Load, Battery Drain.
  • Producing performance dashboards and raw profiler logs for engineering to dig into anomalies.
  • Supporting playtest sessions and feature acceptance where engine-level or map-specific expertise is required.
  • Re-testing performance fixes and map fixes after they are addressed by the client's development team.
  • Feeding back into briefing packs: documenting what to look for in map/level content so the pool can be onboarded on simpler, well-scoped map tasks over time.


Kogo poszukujemy?

Requirements:

  • Experience as a QA Engineer in GameDev for 4+ years.
  • Hands-on experience with the Unity Editor, including comfortable navigating scenes, hierarchy, GameObjects, Transforms, Layers/Tags and Prefabs to accurately reproduce and describe bugs.
  • Experience with level/map testing specifically: object placement QA, collision/geometry verification, lighting checks – 2D or 3D.
  • Comfortable working from design documentation/content specs and translating them into concrete test scenarios.
  • Level of English – from Intermediate and above.

Nice-to-haves:

  • Experience with mobile performance profiling: FPS, memory, CPU load, battery drain, and reading raw profiler output.


Czego wymagamy?

Znajomości:
  • Unity

title: Director of Real Estate
location: Roman Catholic Services Corporation for Parishes and Schools in San Diego and Imperial Counties
description:
Site Name: Roman Catholic Services Corporation for Parishes and Schools in San Diego and Imperial Counties (“RCSC”)
Location: 3888 Paducah Drive, San Diego, CA 92117
Reports to: Board of Directors or its designee
Employment Type: Full Time
FLSA Status: Exempt

Salary: commensurate with experience


General Description

The Director of Real Estate is responsible for overseeing the management of all real estate owned by the Diocese of San Diego and its parishes. S/he will serve as the Secretary of the Board of Directors of 94 parish real estate holding corporations and coordinate their compliance with corporate formalities. The position assists parish pastors, administrators and councils, as well as other staff and clergy members with the stewardship of parish and other diocesan real estate assets in accordance with the particular policies and norms of the Diocese of San Diego contained in the Diocesan Handbook and the RCSC’s policies and procedures.


Primary Responsibilities

The duties and responsibilities of the Director of Real Estate include but are not limited to the following:

  • Assist with the governance of the boards of directors of 94 parish real estate support corporations ("PSC")
  • Serve as ex officio board member for all 94 PSCs.
  • Coordinate compliance by PSC with corporate formalities, including scheduling of and attendance at annual meetings of boards of directors, maintaining board minutes, and filing biannual Statements of Information with the Secretary of State
  • Coordinate providing the Diocese and parishes with informed appraisals of the value of their respective properties, as needed
  • Assist the Diocese and parishes with understanding how to increase the returns and enhance the value of their real estate holdings; meet with parish finance councils and PSC concerning how to meet their goals for real estate
  • Research and report on potential properties for acquisition by the Diocese and parishes, as needs arise
  • Review all proposed real estate sales, purchases and leases by the Diocese and parishes and advise concerning their financial viability and compliance with diocesan policy, civil law, and where appropriate, canon law
  • Primarily responsible for review, documentation and processing of all purchases and sales of improved and unimproved properties
  • Coordinates and monitors due diligence activities related to real estate transactions with outside counsel, real estate professionals, engineering, planning, appraisal and environmental consultants
  • Negotiate terms of diocesan and parish real estate leases with third parties
  • Advise the Diocese and parishes on miscellaneous real property issues, e.g. title, zoning, easements, boundaries; respond to inquiries and notices from governmental entities and private parties (e.g. neighbors) concerning the same
  • Regularly attend weekly RCSC team meetings, prepared to provide meaningful progress updates regarding ongoing real estate transactions, RCSC and Diocese projects
  • Contribute to the management and updating of the RCSC’s referral network database
  • Attend city/county planning and commission meetings to seek approval of diocesan and parish real estate projects and obtain necessary entitlements
  • Work cooperatively with other diocesan offices and parishes, and the RCSC Director of Construction as needed, concerning real estate issues related to construction and remodeling projects
  • Manage the RCSC’s proprietary Lease Database per the direction of the RCSC’s Executive Director
  • Coordinate and manage the annual filing by the Diocese and parishes of Claims for Real Estate Welfare Exemption with County Assessors
  • Review and coordinate the maintenance of RCSC and diocesan files pertaining to diocesan and parish real estate
  • Provide real estate-related services to parishes as outlined in the Parish Services Agreements with the Services Corporation
  • Respond timely to requests of the Services Corporation board, PSC boards, the Bishop(s) and Diocesan personnel
  • Coordinate the investigation of historical utility billings and assessments for the Diocese and parishes

title: Customer Experience Associate
description:
About Withings

Withings is on a mission to be the trusted leader in clinical-grade smart health devices. Already the leading innovator of smart scales, our product portfolio includes connected scales, blood pressure monitors, sleep monitors, thermometers, and health/activity wearables.

In 2019, we launched Withings Health Solutions (WHS) to bridge the gap between patients and providers. This fast-growing B2B division enables healthcare innovators—from chronic condition management to clinical research—to provide better care through our ecosystem of connected devices and our remote patient monitoring platform.

The Opportunity: A Global Bridge

We are looking for a talented individual to help us build the future of healthcare from our Issy-les-Moulineaux office. While you will be based in France, you will be a key member of a global team:

  • Global Reporting: You will report directly to the WHS Customer Support Manager based in Boston, MA.
  • Transatlantic Collaboration: You will act as a vital link between our French headquarters and our US-based operations, requiring high autonomy, the ability to manage workflows across different time zones and flexibility in working hours.
  • Bilingual Communication: Because you will be supporting global partners and collaborating with a US-based manager, professional fluency in both English and French (written and verbal) is strictly required.

What You’ll Do

Reporting to the Boston-based Manager, you will serve as the primary point of contact for our dedicated B2B products and partners.

  • Product Expertise: Act as the lead technical expert for WHS devices and remote support.
  • Escalation Management: Master ticketing systems to handle complex escalations, decrease resolution times, and ensure strict adherence to SLAs.
  • Knowledge Engineering: Systematically document contact drivers and ensure frontline agent training and Help Centers remain world-class.
  • Strategic Documentation: Lead the creation of internal SOPs and external support assets in both English and French.
  • Partner Onboarding: Monitor and participate in the onboarding journey for new WHS partners.
  • Project Leadership: Lead cross-team initiatives to solve contact reasons and improve user journeys.
  • Data Analysis: Monitor KPIs to propose and implement operational solutions.

Requirements

  • Bilingual Fluency: Native or professional-level proficiency in English and French. You must be capable of technical writing and partner communications in both languages.
  • Experience: 2–3 years in Customer Support, specifically within Hardware, SaaS, or HealthTech.
  • Exceptional Communication: Proven ability to explain technical concepts clearly. Strong technical writing skills are a must, particularly for creating logical SOPs.
  • Critical Thinking: A "problem-solver" mindset with the ability to use investigative questioning to find root causes.
  • Process Optimization: A track record of bringing best practices to a team and optimizing workflows.
  • Interpersonal Excellence: Ability to build instant credibility with international partners and stakeholders in Boston and France.
  • Operational Discipline: High attention to detail and a commitment to meeting deadlines and SLAs.
  • Experience in the healthcare industry is a significant plus.

Benefits

  • Joining one of the pioneers and global leaders in connected health—a multi-award winner at the Consumer Electronics Show.
  • Contributing to innovative and ambitious projects shaping the future of healthcare, within an agile and constantly evolving environment.
  • Joining an international company—a member of the FrenchTech 120—with teams based in Issy-les-Moulineaux, Boston, Hong Kong, and Shenzhen.
  • Participating in the continuous improvement of our products and services by beta-testing them prior to launch—particularly during our many sports sessions with colleagues.
  • Enjoying a wide range of benefits: stock options, a smartphone and computer of your choice, discounts on cultural and sports activities, an on-site company restaurant, and much more.
  • Collaborating with passionate colleagues and celebrating every success together!
  • All applications are reviewed regardless of a candidate’s ethnic origin, opinions, beliefs, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or health status. Withings is committed to providing and guaranteeing equal opportunities to all candidates; access to information regarding your application is restricted to authorized personnel only (HR and Management).

Note to Applicants: As your direct manager and core team are based in Boston, please submit your application and CV in English.

title: Finance Business Partner
description:
Finance Business Partner.

Our client is seeking a commercially minded and hands-on finance professional to establish and manage a centralised accounting and financial-control function.

The successful candidate will initially assume responsibility for the complete bookkeeping and accounting function. Once the relevant systems, processes and controls are operating effectively, the role will progressively expand to cover the other entities within the group.

This is a practical, operational role requiring someone who is comfortable managing day-to-day accounting activities from the ground up, while also providing management-level financial oversight and advice.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Bookkeeping and financial accounting

• Take responsibility for the complete bookkeeping and accounting function of the Group.

• Record and review all accounting entries, including sales, purchases, receipts, payments, journals and accruals.

• Maintain accurate general ledgers, cashbooks, accounts receivable and accounts payable records.

Financial documentation and transaction processing

• Establish and maintain an organised document-management system for invoices, purchase orders, receipts, contracts and other financial supporting documents.

• Prepare and issue purchase orders, customer invoices, credit notes and other relevant documentation.

Management and annual reporting

• Prepare timely monthly and periodic management accounts.

• Produce profit-and-loss statements, balance sheets, cash-flow reports and other management information.

• Investigate material variances and provide clear explanations and recommendations to management.

Cash-flow and working-capital management

• Prepare and regularly update cash-flow forecasts.

• Develop creditor-payment plans that optimise the group’s use of available cash while ensuring agreed payment terms are respected.

Inventory and trading controls

• Maintain oversight of inventory accounting, reconciliations, costing and valuation.

• Work with operational teams to ensure that inventory movements are properly documented and recorded.

• Investigate and resolve discrepancies between physical inventory, operational records and accounting records.

Internal controls and process improvement

• Review existing accounting and operational processes and identify control weaknesses.

• Design, implement and document appropriate financial policies, approval procedures and internal controls.

• Establish clear reporting formats and reporting timetables in consultation with management.

Commercial and management support

• Provide reliable financial information to support operational and strategic decision-making.

• Advise management on financial risks, cash-flow priorities and business performance.

• Work closely with directors, management and operational personnel across the group.

Requirements

Qualifications and Experience

• Fully qualified or part-qualified accountant, preferably pursuing or holding ACCA, ACA, CIMA or another recognised accounting qualification.

• Relevant experience in bookkeeping, financial accounting, management accounting or financial control.

• Experience at senior accountant, assistant financial controller, financial controller or comparable mid-management level would be advantageous.

• Demonstrated ability to prepare management accounts and annual financial information.

• Practical experience managing accounts receivable, accounts payable, cash flow and working capital.

• Experience with inventory accounting or a trading, distribution, aviation or similarly operational business would be advantageous.

• Experience establishing or improving accounting processes and internal controls.

• Experience supporting multiple entities or a group structure would be beneficial.

• Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Excel.

• Sound understanding of accounting principles, reconciliations and financial-reporting requirements.

title: Fundraising Officer

Fundraising Officer

Contract: Permanent

Location: 3 locations available, North, Midlands, London & South (Remote working from home)

About READ Foundation

READ Foundation is a UK based registered charity working to provide access to quality education to vulnerable children in our regions of work. We create opportunities for orphan and needy children to go to school, to gain an education and build a better life for themselves. We currently focus on constructing new schools, providing sponsorship for orphans and are now expanding our educational portfolio to reflect the large humanitarian and development needs ongoing throughout the world.

Directly reporting to the National Fundraising Manager UK, you will have responsibility for the full cycle of maximising donation income from research, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship.

  • Arrange and manage fundraising events

title: Director of Religious Education
description:
Parish Name: St. Michael's Catholic Church

Location: 15546 Pomerado Rd, Poway, CA 92064

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Pay: $25 - $30 per hour, depending upon experience


Job Summary

The Director of Religious Education (DRE) works in collaboration with the Pastoral Associate to develop and maintain comprehensive parish catechetical programs for youth and children, kindergarten through grade 8.

The goals of this position include:

  • Communicating an enthusiasm for the Catholic faith among our young people and their families
  • Planning and oversight of the parish religious education program, including sacramental preparation, Children’s Liturgy of the Word, OCIA adapted for Children, Vacation Bible School.
  • Facilitating parent and catechist meetings and workshops.

Duties & Responsibilities

Administrative

The DRE completes or delegates the following:

  • Supervise administrative assistant and numerous volunteers.
  • Orders books and supplies
  • Sets the calendar for catechetical programs and events.
  • Reserves needed facilities and equipment.
  • Provides a safe environment for all: secures and runs background checks and training for all volunteers working with children and youth per diocesan guidelines.
  • Answers administrative questions regarding catechetical programs.
  • Conducts an annual registration process
  • Maintains records of participation in catechetical programs and celebrations of sacraments.
  • Maintains records of achievement for catechists that include participation in all safe environment requirements, parish and Diocesan catechetical formation events, and applicable certification processes.
  • Maintain volunteer records.
  • Participates in parish diocesan, deanery, and parish staff meetings, coordinating catechetical ministry with other ministries.
  • Serves as liaison with the diocesan office of RE and their programs, services, and resources
  • Oversee traffic during class times.
  • Communicate policies and procedures to parents, students, catechists, aides and other adults in collaboration with the professional staff.
  • Maintain open communication with members of the Parish staff, volunteers and RE families.
  • Maintain close communication with the Diocesan Office for Evangelization and Catechetical Ministry.
  • Serve as RE representatives on the Liturgy Committee, Pastoral Council and Council of Ministries.
  • Organize, supervise, and maintain RE Offices.
  • Oversee the proper use of parish facilities that RE uses including locking up all buildings that RE uses on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
  • Prepare an annual budget for RE and present to Pastoral Associate for approval before submitting to the Pastor.
  • Be available to parents, students, and adults for consultation, advice, and referral.

Catechetical

The DRE

  • Set and implement catechetical vision for the parish based on contemporary Church documents to develop the parish as an evangelizing community.
  • Develop and provide total parish catechetical program for youth and children in grades kindergarten – grade 8.
  • Provide formation for the celebration of the sacraments for youth, children, and their parents.
  • Provide sacramental preparation classes to students in grades 3-8 who are preparing for first reconciliation and first communion.
  • Evaluate and select catechetical resources (texts, materials, etc.) utilizing diocesan norms and policies.
  • Recruit, screen and provide in-service to catechists.
  • Support and develop catechists by leading catechist training and providing catechetical resources in accordance with diocesan guidelines.
  • Provide opportunities for on-going education and spiritual formation of RE personnel, catechists and aides.
  • Inform personnel and catechists of opportunities for professional courses/workshops for spiritual growth.
  • Recognize, encourage, and support the catechetical efforts of those involved in religious education.

title: Automotive Module Product Engineer
description:

General Summary:

Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. is a global leader in the development and commercialization of advanced semiconductor solutions for mobile, automotive, compute, connectivity, IoT, XR/VR, and other high-performance technology markets. The Product Development and Test Engineering organization supports design validation, silicon characterization, production test development, and high-volume manufacturing readiness for leading-edge products built on advanced semiconductor process technologies.

The Automotive Product and Test Engineering group is responsible for the various phases in the lifecycle of integrated SOC’s and QAM’s used in IVI, ADAS & Telematics automotive applications. The selected candidate will support the new product introduction (NPI) to production and return material analysis. This includes verification & validation, characterization, qualification, development of high-volume manufacturing solutions, and customer support. The selected candidate will work with global cross functional teams (SW, System and HW Design, Test, Operations and other engineering organizations) to provide engineering test solutions to drive products to commercialization and production manufacturing.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Responsibilities for this position include supporting bring up of new system level test (SLT) HW platforms and handler solutions, development and automation of SW test modules, test program integration, optimization of test modules for stability and validation across temperature, developing/executing test strategies and test plans, troubleshooting/analyzing problems, performing systems correlation for power and thermal, evaluating and qualifying HW solutions, debug and failure analysis, and customer support.

We’re committed to building an organisation where people from all walks of life feel they belong—where different voices, experiences, and backgrounds are valued and respected.

Closing date: 4th September 2026

Weetabix is on an exciting growth journey, and many of the opportunities we are recruiting for are newly created roles. These positions reflect our investment in people, capabilities and innovation as we continue to build for the future.

The Recipe (About the Role)

As Domain Architect – Microsoft and Cloud, you will define, govern, and evolve the architectural vision across Microsoft, Cloud, and End User Compute domains. You will ensure that the organisation’s technology foundations are secure, scalable, and resilient, aligned to both current priorities and long‑term business strategy.

You will play a key role in guiding the transformation of digital capabilities, ensuring the Information Technology (IT) landscape enables business growth, operational effectiveness, and modern ways of working. Working closely with stakeholders, you will provide strategic direction while maintaining strong architectural governance and standards.

This role combines deep technical expertise with forward‑looking thinking, ensuring that technology resolutions are practical, future‑ready, and commercially aligned as the organisation continues to adopt advanced and emerging technologies.

  • Define and own the architecture strategy across Microsoft technologies, cloud, End User Computing, identity and access management (Active Directory and Microsoft Entra), and Windows Server, ensuring alignment to business priorities
  • Act as design authority, governing and approving solutions through the Technical Design Authority to ensure consistency with enterprise standards
  • Produce high-level designs and assure the quality and approval of low-level designs, ensuring all outputs meet standards and are fully documented
  • Provide design assurance throughout delivery, ensuring solutions remain aligned to architecture and transition smoothly into aid with full operational readiness
  • Define and embed non-functional requirements, including performance, security, scalability, resilience and operability, ensuring they are measurable and consistently applied
  • Identify technical debt, capability gaps and risks, shaping a strategic roadmap that drives resilience, modernisation, security and cost efficiency
  • Monitor platform health and prioritise improvement initiatives that strengthen performance and long-term sustainability
  • Partner with senior stakeholders to align architecture with business strategy, growth plans and transformation priorities
  • Provide oversight during delivery, ensuring adherence to architecture, early risk identification and effective governance of any deviations
  • Manage supplier and vendor engagement, assisting selection, evaluation and performance, ensuring solutions align to architectural standards
  • Stay current with emerging technologies, trends and regulatory requirements, keeping the architecture modern and adaptable
  • Shape a scalable, secure and cost-effective technology landscape, enabling cloud adoption, modern workplace capabilities and future growth

  • Drive architecture maturity, enabling a more integrated, data-led and cloud-enabled environment that improves teamwork, mobility and productivity

The Ingredients (What we need from you)

Key Know How:

  • Deep technical expertise across Microsoft technologies, including cloud platforms, Microsoft Azure, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365 (M365), End-User Computing (EUC) and Windows Server
  • Enterprise architecture experience, designing and governing complex, scalable technology solutions
  • Broad awareness of emerging technologies, industry trends and evolving regulatory requirements
  • Experience applying architecture frameworks, governance standards and structured design methodologies
  • Proven ability to produce high-quality High-Level Designs (HLDs), guide Low-Level Design (LLD) development and manage architecture governance
  • Stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and guide deliberation at all levels
  • Rational mindset with the ability to assess complex systems and long-term architectural impacts

Desirable:

  • Experience working in a manufacturing or FMCG IT/OT environment.
  • Exposure to modern identity, security frameworks, and Zero Trust principles.
  • Knowledge of automation, containerisation, and modern application hosting patterns.
  • Enterprise Architecture certification (e.g., TOGAF), Azure certifications, or equivalent.
  • Vendor and commercial evaluation experience.
  • Familiarity with data architecture concepts to support future cross‑domain integration.

title: Senior Investment Analyst - Film Funds
description:
About Parrot Analytics

Parrot Analytics is the global authority on media and entertainment intelligence, providing the strategic decision support that the world’s leading studios, producers, streamers, investors, and government bodies rely on to de-risk content investment and maximize returns.

Trusted across the full media economy — from studios and streaming platforms to film funds, sports leagues, and government bodies — Parrot Analytics informs capital allocation, acquisitions, programming strategy, and IP valuation at the highest levels of the industry.

By measuring the demand and preferences of more than 2 billion audiences worldwide, Parrot Analytics’ AI platform quantifies the value of content, talent, franchises, and sports rights — enabling partners to forecast revenue, assess risk, optimize portfolio strategy, and drive more predictable success.

About the Role

The global entertainment industry invests hundreds of billions of dollars into film and television content every year. Yet investment decisions are still largely made using fragmented market signals, limited financial modelling, and incomplete audience insight.

Parrot Analytics is building a new analytical layer for the industry — combining the world’s largest dataset on global audience demand with structured financial modelling to help studios, investors, and funds make more disciplined content investment decisions.

We are seeking a Senior Investment Analyst to lead the development of financial models used to evaluate film and television projects. This role sits at the intersection of entertainment economics, investment analysis, and data science, translating audience demand signals, project budgets, and distribution assumptions into structured financial forecasts and investment insights.

The successful candidate will play a key role in helping investors understand the risk and return profile of content investments before capital is committed.

Build Investment Models for Film & Television Projects

  • Develop sophisticated financial models that evaluate the commercial performance of film and television projects across multiple distribution windows.
  • Models will incorporate production budgets and cost structures, financing structures and investor positions, distribution revenue streams across global markets and investor return scenarios and capital recovery timelines.
  • Revenue modelling will consider multiple distribution pathways including theatrical, SVOD, AVOD, FAST, Pay TV, and international licensing.
  • Leverage Parrot Analytics’ global dataset on audience demand and content valuation to inform revenue assumptions within financial models.
  • Develop structured approaches to translating audience demand signals and valuation into realistic commercial scenarios, benchmarking projects against comparable titles across genres, markets, and platforms.

Quantify Investment Risk

  • Evaluate projects through structured scenario modelling that assesses downside risk and capital exposure, break-even performance thresholds and investor return scenarios under different market conditions
  • Conduct sensitivity analysis across key variables including budget changes, distribution outcomes, and shifts in audience demand.

Support Investment Decision-Making

  • Produce financial analyses used by funds, studios, and investors evaluating content opportunities.
  • Translate complex financial models into clear insights that help decision-makers understand the economic implications of project budgets, distribution strategies, and market positioning.

Develop Industry-Leading Modelling Frameworks

  • Help design the financial modelling frameworks used to evaluate film and television investments using Parrot Analytics’ data.
  • The goal is to build repeatable analytical tools that allow projects to be evaluated with institutional investment discipline, enabling more structured decision-making across the industry.

Requirements

Your experience

5–10+ years of experience in roles that require strong financial modelling and investment analysis in the following environments:

  • film or television investment funds
  • studio finance or content strategy teams
  • media-focused investment banking or private equity
  • entertainment strategy consulting
  • corporate finance roles within media or technology companies

Direct experience working with film finance structures, production budgets, or distribution economics is required.

The skills you bring

Advanced financial modelling - Ability to build complex Excel models from scratch incorporating scenario analysis, sensitivity modelling, and structured investment return frameworks.

Investment analysis mindset - Strong ability to evaluate opportunities through structured risk and return analysis.

Data-driven thinking - Comfortable integrating external datasets and quantitative signals into financial forecasts and commercial assumptions.

Intellectual curiosity - A genuine interest in understanding how film and television projects generate economic value.

Communication - Ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear insights for non-technical decision-makers. Ideally fluent in Arabic to service regional clients.

Who Will Thrive in This Role

This role is best suited to individuals who:

  • enjoy building deep, structured financial models
  • are naturally curious about the economics of media and entertainment
  • think rigorously about downside risk as well as upside potential
  • enjoy turning messy real-world information into structured analysis
  • are excited about building new analytical frameworks for an industry

Benefits

  • Be Part of a Founding Team: Join a pivotal, early team member group supporting our newly established HQ in Qatar, with the opportunity to help shape its direction and impact from the ground up.
  • Global & Distributed by Design: Work as part of a globally distributed team, collaborating across timezones while contributing to high-impact, international projects.
  • Flexible Ways of Working: Operate in a flexible environment that supports autonomy while enabling seamless collaboration across teams and regions.
  • Collaborative & Transparent Culture: Be part of a team that values openness, knowledge-sharing, and strong cross-functional collaboration.
  • Purpose-Driven Work: Join a team of problem solvers who care deeply about delivering meaningful insights and real value to clients.
  • Stay Connected Globally: Take part in monthly virtual all-hands sessions to celebrate wins, share updates, and stay aligned on company goals and strategy.

title: Director of Quantum Error Correction (QEC)
description:
At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it.

Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve successfully transitioned quantum computing from an academic dream into a commercial reality.

The most exciting thing is that we’re just getting started and we’ve recently closed our £260 million Series C funding round – the largest fundraise ever completed by a quantum computing company in Europe.

The Purpose

As Director of Quantum Error Correction (QEC), you will lead the scientific strategy that enables fault-tolerant quantum computing. Working within our Quantum Science & Exploratory Research (QSER) department, you'll build and inspire world-class research teams, shaping the architectures, algorithms and hardware co-design that will define the next generation of quantum computing.

The Role

You will lead multidisciplinary teams of QEC Theorists, Architecture Researchers and Quantum Engineers.

You'll set the strategic direction for Quantum Error Correction at OQC, ensuring our research translates into practical demonstrations that maximise the performance and scalability of our superconducting quantum hardware.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Build, develop and lead a world-class Quantum Error Correction organisation spanning theory, architecture, numerical modelling, hardware co-design and implementation.
  • Drive OQC's QEC strategy by developing cutting-edge error correction and mitigation techniques that reduce logical qubit overheads and strengthen our hardware roadmap.
  • Translate long-term company objectives into ambitious, executable research programmes delivered across multiple technical teams.
  • Partner closely with hardware, software and engineering teams to ensure theoretical advances are grounded in experimental reality and accelerate product development.
  • Represent OQC as a recognised technical leader, presenting research breakthroughs and logical systems milestones to international conferences, customers and strategic partners.
  • Own the planning and management of QEC budgets, including simulation infrastructure, software tooling and external technology partnerships.
  • Mentor and develop technical leaders, fostering a collaborative, high-performance research culture while removing obstacles and maintaining delivery momentum.

What We're Looking For

  • Significant industrial and/or academic experience developing Quantum Error Correction technologies, including bosonic, surface or LDPC codes, logical architectures, decoders or large-scale numerical simulations.
  • Proven leadership experience building and managing high-performing technical or scientific teams, including the development of senior researchers and technical managers.
  • Experience delivering complex research programmes within multidisciplinary environments spanning quantum hardware, software and experimental physics.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop long-term technical strategy, manage competing priorities and translate vision into execution.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills, with experience influencing executive stakeholders and cross-functional engineering organisations.
  • Experience managing technical budgets, external collaborations and strategic research partnerships.
  • PhD in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or another relevant scientific discipline, with a strong focus on Quantum Information Theory or a related field.

The 'Nice-to-Haves'

  • Commercial experience developing quantum computing technologies.
  • Experience designing or implementing quantum or cryogenic systems.
  • Knowledge of superconducting qubit architectures or cryogenic engineering.
  • Experience owning end-to-end technical project delivery in fast-paced R&D environments.
  • Strong roadmapping, external partnership management and technical presentation experience.
  • Experience coordinating multiple large technical teams delivering complex scientific programmes.

Why Join OQC

You will join a world-class team at the forefront of the next computational era. We offer a culture of bold innovation, the chance to work with unique lab infrastructure, and the opportunity to see your work redefine the limits of computation.

description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it’s a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn’t been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

Overview

You will work closely with cross-functional teams to design, develop, and implement scalable and robust solutions that meet our customers' needs and exceed their expectations. Some of the key products as part of the digital portfolio are – mobile and desktop applications, vehicle connectivity solutions, mapping services, production, inventory and planning optimization, servicing and repairs, and more. At the same time, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to be hands-on building key systems and will be directly responsible for the successful delivery of complex and large-scale technical efforts as well as acting as a technical mentor and leader for other engineers.

title: Medical Education Program Manager
description:
About IHI

At Innovative Hematology, Inc. (IHI), we offer a future where people with rare blood disorders flourish. Our experts provide the highest quality comprehensive services and holistic care to patients with bleeding, clotting, and other hematologic disorders, and to their families.

What You Will Do

As the Medical Education Program Manager, you will be responsible for building a professional and sustainable medical education infrastructure by developing, planning, implementing, and evaluating education programs that ensure clinical staff competency and compliance with organizational standards. In this role you will focus on orientation, ongoing skills validation and competency assessments, and educational support for clinical staff, including but not limited to nursing, medical assistants, phlebotomists, and allied health professionals. The position partners with clinical leadership teams, Organizational & Talent Development Program Manager, Learning Experience Designer, quality, and subject matters experts to align medical education initiatives with strategic goals and regulatory requirements and ensures education is accurate, role-specific, patient-centered and health literate.

The Opportunity

  • Develop and deliver structured orientation programs for new nursing staff and other clinical roles. Ensure all new hires complete required education, competencies and skills checklists within designated timelines.
  • Design and maintain annual competency programs for nursing and other clinical staff. Conduct skills checkoffs and validate proficiency in clinical procedures, documentation, and safety protocols. Maintain accurate records of staff education, competencies and certifications.
  • Partner with education committee members and subject matter experts to develop, revise, and maintain annual education modules, presentations, quizzes, and competency materials and prioritize, track and complete education updates.
  • Assess educational needs across clinical teams and create targeted learning opportunities. Provide in-service training and continuing education sessions for clinical roles. Collaborate with clinical leadership teams to ensure education programs support quality, safety, and compliance standards.
  • Serve as a subject matter expert for nursing practice and clinical protocols. Assist in implementing new technologies, procedures, and medications by educating staff and ensuring alignment with best practices.
  • Assisting with educational events, needs and requests related to oral, printed, or electronic materials, and presentations.
  • Maintain education calendars, project plans, and documentation related to assigned education initiatives.
  • Monitor effectiveness of education programs through feedback, audits, and performance metrics. Recommend improvements based on best practices and industry standards. Support continuous improvement efforts related to education standardization, accessibility, and staff engagement.
  • Collaborate with management to foster a culture of education and define clinical educational requirements for staff, communicate offerings and encourage staff attendance.

Performance Requirements

Knowledge:

  1. Knowledge of learning theories related to healthcare education for all age levels and learning styles.
  2. Knowledge of computer applications including medical records and clinical care processes.
  3. Clinical knowledge in areas related to nursing, medicine and allied health.
  4. Knowledge of e-learning modalities (website, videos, iPads).
  5. Familiarity with policies and standards for CME/CE activities preferred.
  6. Knowledge of assessing effectiveness of education programs.

Skills:

  1. Excellent verbal (including presentation) skills and written communication.
  2. Teambuilding and interpersonal relations; mentor and provide feedback and redirection.
  3. Exercising initiative, discretion and good decision-making.
  4. Possess good problem-solving skills
  5. Proficient in use of Microsoft Office tools including Word, PowerPoint, Teams and Excel
  6. Basic skills in data analysis and program assessment

Abilities:

  1. Ability to educate staff in both verbal and written form in formal and informal settings.
  2. Ability to work collaboratively with diverse individuals at all levels of medical practice.
  3. Ability to prioritize projects, meet deadlines and proactively follow-up; handle many tasks simultaneously and deal effectively with changing priorities.
  4. Ability to read and comprehend moderately complex written materials, such as medical materials.
  5. Must be extremely organized, efficient, and detail-oriented

Travel: Occasional travel for training/conferences as well as supporting IHI initiatives.

Requirements

  • Valid RN license in the state of Indiana
  • Master's or doctorate degree in nursing required; certification as a Clinical Nurse Specialist Advanced Practice Registered Nurse (CNS-APRN), with specialized training in patient and provider education (preferred).
  • Minimum five years of experience in a healthcare setting with three years of experience in healthcare education preferred.
  • All IHI employees are expected to enable multi-factor authentication via their personal smart phone/smart device in order to access IHI systems as a requirement of the role.

This position is open to residents of the State of Indiana, and requires routine presence at our Center in Indianapolis, IN. Frequency of on-site presence is dependent upon role and department needs.

Benefits

Benefits

Why join our team?

IHI is a not-for-profit program based in Indianapolis and offers a competitive salary and benefit package.

IHI is the only federally designated comprehensive hemophilia program in Indiana and serves the entire state through services available in Indianapolis and at outreach clinics.

IHI is a leader in hemophilia care, education and clinical research and has a dedicated on-site multidisciplinary staff to ensure availability of a wide range of required services.

IHI participates in national and international clinical research, including new infusion products and therapies, investigation of long-term outcomes, and the impact of associated conditions. The IHI research program provides patients access to new therapies, and an opportunity to improve care. Our center has more than 50 clinical research projects involving bleeding disorders, sickle cell disease, thrombosis and more.

Innovative Hematology, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Lead Engineer
description:
At Weetabix, we believe that diverse teams drive better ideas, stronger decisions, and a more inclusive workplace for everyone. We’re committed to building an organisation where people from all walks of life feel they belong—where different voices, experiences, and backgrounds are valued and respected.

Working pattern: 24/7 Panama Shift Pattern

As a Lead Engineer, you will provide day-to-day engineering leadership for a manufacturing shift, ensuring equipment and processes run safely, reliably, and efficiently. Working closely with a team of multi-skilled engineers, you will coordinate planned maintenance, respond to breakdowns, and support strong shift performance.

Balancing hands-on technical expertise with people leadership, you will support skills development, uphold high engineering standards, and ensure maintenance is delivered effectively. You will play a key role in maximising asset uptime, reducing downtime, and enabling the shift to consistently achieve production, safety, and quality targets.

  • Deploy resources effectively to minimise downtime, remove bottlenecks, and improve productivity.
  • Support performance management, coaching, and development planning, including apprentices.

  • Produce shift reports, including engineering performance, breakdown trends, and operational impact.

  • Manage Permit to Work processes and the safe control of contractors and high-risk activities.
  • Maintain accurate CMMS records, ensuring quality data and timely job completion.
  • Coach and develop engineering and production colleagues to build capability.
  • Support engineering activities across multiple production facilities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Lead root cause investigations and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
  • Respond to major breakdowns, driving rapid fault resolution and reducing downtime.
  • Collaborate with engineering and operational teams to improve reliability, performance, and continuous improvement.
  • Support wider business needs through additional duties as required.

The Ingredients (What we need from you)

Key Know How:

  • Engineering maintenance expertise across mechanical, electrical and control systems in complex manufacturing
  • Experience developing engineering capability, including assisting teams and apprentices across maintenance and improvement activities
  • Proficient in Computerised Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS), using data to improve planning and inform outcomes
  • Clear insight of manufacturing operations and impact on Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), downtime, cost, quality and waste
  • Ability to work jointly with production and engineering teams to align maintenance planning, scheduling and continuous improvement

Your Bowl of Perks (Benefits)

Competitive salary & Annual Flexible benefits

  • Double-matched pension scheme (up to 12% from us)

  • Access to 24/7 counselling service (via Grocery Aid partnership)

  • Working Parents Support Group
  • Fully stocked kitchens filled with our delicious products for you to enjoy

description:
Advocate Radiation Oncology’s mission is to provide compassionate health care expertise to cancer patients.

Advocate Radiation Oncology is expanding and this position is for a Clinical Medical Physicist to join our group of knowledgeable Physicists in the beautiful Southwest Florida area.


Advocate Radiation Oncology is a group of Radiation Therapy offices located in Southeast & Southwest Florida. This is a unique and very exciting opportunity for a clinical Medical Physicist to join a team of experienced staff working at a state of the art facility, using new technology, in a collaborative work environment.


The Advocate Radiation Oncology offices in this region are equipped with Varian TrueBeam, Edge, and Halcyon linear accelerators, Varian Bravos HDR, and excellent Physics equipment including: Sun Nuclear 1D scanning tank, IC Profiler, & DoseLab. All of the offices have Varian machines (TrueBeam, Edge, Halcyon, Bravos HDR), ARIA Record & Verify System, and Eclipse Treatment Planning System.


Advocate Radiation Oncology is committed to utilizing new technology, including use of 3D, IMRT, VMAT, SBRT, SRT, SGRT, and HDR treatments. This is a clinical position and the ideal candidate will be very involved in the clinical duties of the office. It is very important that the candidate be a team player and contribute to a positive work environment.

title: Photographer
description:
We are looking for a detail-oriented and highly motivated Photographer to join the NIQ Brandbank Studio team. This role is responsible for capturing high-quality, print-ready product images at volume while maintaining strict quality standards and agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced studio environment, works effectively both independently and collaboratively, and has a strong understanding of product photography, lighting techniques, image quality standards, and workflow management.

This is a full-time position.

Key Responsibilities

  • Capture high-quality, print-ready images of grocery and consumer products to support data collection and digital content requirements.
  • Ensure all product images are clear, accurate, legible, and comply with NIQ Brandbank quality standards.
  • Maintain high productivity while consistently meeting image quality expectations.
  • Prioritize workload according to SLAs, internal service KPIs, and business requirements.
  • Manage daily photography workflow, product organization, and studio shelving systems.
  • Resolve photography-related queries and issues in a timely manner.

  • Collaborate across studio functions as required to maintain operational productivity during peak periods.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, ethical standards, and data confidentiality requirements.

Required

  • Experience working in a high-volume production environment.
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality.
  • Strong organizational and time management skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing positively to team objectives.
  • Basic computer proficiency and ability to learn new systems and workflows.
  • Understanding of data confidentiality and information security principles.

Preferred

  • Experience photographing FMCG, retail, grocery, packaged goods, or e-commerce products.
  • Experience working with image quality control processes and production KPIs.
  • Familiarity with image editing or asset management workflows.
  • Knowledge of color management, image standards, and print-ready digital assets.

Key Competencies

  • Collaboration and Teamwork
  • Accountability
