title: Prior Authorization Specialist
description:
The Prior Authorization Specialist is responsible for obtaining and coordinating insurance authorizations and precertifications for medical services, procedures, diagnostic testing, medications, and other services requiring payer approval. This position plays a critical role in supporting timely patient care while helping ensure the organization receives appropriate reimbursement for services provided.

The Prior Authorization Specialist will work closely with clinical teams, scheduling staff, physicians, insurance companies, and other members of the Revenue Cycle department to ensure authorization requirements are identified, submitted, tracked, and completed accurately and within required payer timeframes.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with multiple insurance plans, payer portals, and authorization requirements in a fast-paced healthcare environment.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Review scheduled services and patient accounts to determine whether prior authorization or precertification is required.
  • Verify patient insurance eligibility, benefits, and authorization requirements.
  • Obtain prior authorizations for procedures, diagnostic services, imaging, medications, and other services as required by the patient's insurance plan.
  • Submit authorization requests through payer portals, telephone systems, fax, or other designated methods.
  • Gather and submit all required clinical documentation, including physician notes, medical records, test results, treatment plans, and other supporting information.
  • Ensure authorization requests contain accurate patient, provider, diagnosis, procedure, and insurance information.
  • Monitor pending authorization requests and follow up with insurance companies within required timeframes.
  • Document authorization numbers, effective dates, approved services, units, and other pertinent information in the appropriate systems.
  • Communicate authorization status to scheduling, clinical, billing, and other appropriate departments.
  • Identify authorization issues or missing documentation that may delay patient care and work proactively to resolve them.
  • Communicate with physicians and clinical staff when additional documentation or clarification is needed.
  • Assist with authorization denials by reviewing payer responses and determining appropriate next steps.
  • Coordinate peer-to-peer reviews, reconsiderations, and appeals when applicable.
  • Track authorization expiration dates and obtain extensions or updated authorizations when necessary.
  • Verify that approved services and dates correspond with the services scheduled or rendered.
  • Maintain accurate records of all authorization activity and communications.
  • Follow payer-specific requirements, guidelines, and submission procedures.
  • Maintain knowledge of changing insurance requirements and authorization policies.
  • Work with Revenue Cycle staff to help prevent claim denials related to missing or incorrect authorizations.
  • Identify recurring authorization issues and communicate trends or concerns to management.
  • Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and all applicable healthcare regulations.
  • Provide professional and timely customer service to patients, insurance representatives, physicians, and internal departments.
  • Perform other Revenue Cycle and administrative duties as assigned.

title: LAC Program Intern 2027-1
description:
Job Title: Program Intern, Latin America & the Caribbean

Department: Program Division for Latin America & the Caribbean


Bogota Office

Center Background: The Center for Reproductive Rights is a global human rights organization working to ensure that reproductive rights are protected in law as fundamental human rights worldwide. With offices in New York City, and Washington, D.C.; Nairobi, Kenya; Bogota, Colombia; and Geneva, Switzerland, the Center is a non-profit, non-partisan organization changing law and policy throughout Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and the United States. Our 270+ diverse professionals are committed to advancing the Center’s human rights mission through game-changing litigation, legal policy, and advocacy work. This has powered the Center’s exceptional growth to an operating budget of over $67 million and won the respect of law firms in countries around the world. Our global pro bono network includes over 3,000 lawyers across 6 continents, 64 countries, and 130 law firms. Last year, law firms contributed over $35 million USD in pro bono legal services. The Center’s Strategic Plan sets a high mark for impact: By 2030, half of the world’s population will be living under stronger protections for reproductive rights than they were in 2020. The Center has a record of success to back up this ambitious goal. Since our founding in 1992, the Center has transformed how reproductive rights are understood and applied by courts, governments, and human rights bodies worldwide on issues including maternal health, abortion, assisted reproduction, and adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights. We have won groundbreaking cases before national courts, U.N. Committees, and regional human rights bodies. The Center has also led development of historic, proactive legislation advancing robust protections for reproductive rights. It has built the legal capacity of women’s rights advocates in more than 65 countries and counting. To learn more about the Center, please go to

The Center’s Bogota Office is looking for an enthusiastic, resourceful and highly organized intern with a commitment to reproductive rights issues to engage in a variety of mini projects related to the Colombia office. The internship is full-time, beginning January 12th through July 10th, 2026.

· Drafting and organizing Power Point presentations, documents and preparing talking points for meetings and presentations.

· Reviewing information and producing charts and tools to organize various types of information.

· Gathering, organizing and drafting information related to procurement contracts, professional services contracts and partnership agreements.

· Supporting internal processes for the execution and payment of procurement contracts, professional services contracts and partnership agreements.

· Translating documents and sections of documents from ENG to SPA and vice versa.

· Supporting internal processes for the coordination and logistics of events and travel.

· Support event logistic when needed.

· Assist with special projects as needed.


Qualifications:

· To be eligible for this internship, the candidate must be enrolled in a college or university, bachelor’s candidate.

· Pursuing a degree in Business Administration/ Industrial Engineering/Management/ International Relations/ International Business / Political Science, other related.

· Fluency in Spanish and English (speaking, reading, writing), minimum B1 level.

· Must have exceptional interpersonal, written and verbal presentation skills.

· Ability to work independently and cooperatively as part of a growing group.

· Enthusiastic, approachable, enthusiastic, resourceful and highly organized.

· Ability to handle & maintain confidential matters appropriately.

· Have the capability to multitask and adjust priorities as needed.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office.

How to Apply: Please click on the link below to apply. A cover letter, résumé and contact information for three references must be included in your application in order to be considered for this position. Please include these application materials as attachments.

Deadline for Applications: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applicants are strongly encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

To learn more about our DEI Organizational Commitments, go here. The Center for Reproductive Rights is an equal opportunity employer, committed to inclusive hiring, and dedicated to diversity in our work and staff. We strongly encourage people from all groups and communities to apply.

Cargo: Practicante División de Programas, América Latina y el Caribe 2026

Departamento: División de Programas, América Latina y el Caribe

Oficina de Bogotá


Antecedentes del Centro: El Centro de Derechos Reproductivos es una organización global de derechos humanos que trabaja para garantizar que los derechos reproductivos estén protegidos en la ley como derechos humanos fundamentales en todo el mundo. Con oficinas en Nueva York y Washington, D.C.; Nairobi, Kenia; Bogotá, Colombia; y Ginebra, Suiza, el Centro es una organización sin fines de lucro y no partidista que impulsa cambios en leyes y políticas en África, Asia, Europa, América Latina y el Caribe, y Estados Unidos.

Nuestros más de 270 profesionales diversos están comprometidos con avanzar la misión de derechos humanos del Centro a través de litigios transformadores, políticas legales y trabajo de incidencia. Esto ha impulsado el crecimiento excepcional del Centro, con un presupuesto operativo de más de 67 millones de dólares, y ha ganado el respeto de bufetes de abogados en países de todo el mundo. Nuestra red global de pro bono incluye a más de 3.000 abogados en 6 continentes, 64 países y 130 firmas legales. El año pasado, los bufetes de abogados contribuyeron con más de 35 millones de dólares en servicios legales pro bono.

El Plan Estratégico del Centro establece una meta ambiciosa de impacto: para 2030, la mitad de la población mundial vivirá bajo protecciones más sólidas para los derechos reproductivos que las que tenían en 2020. El Centro cuenta con un historial de éxito que respalda este objetivo ambicioso. Desde nuestra fundación en 1992, el Centro ha transformado la manera en que los derechos reproductivos son entendidos y aplicados por tribunales, gobiernos y organismos de derechos humanos en todo el mundo en temas como salud materna, aborto, reproducción asistida y salud y derechos sexuales y reproductivos de los adolescentes.

Hemos ganado casos históricos ante tribunales nacionales, Comités de la ONU y organismos regionales de derechos humanos. El Centro también ha liderado el desarrollo de legislación histórica y proactiva que impulsa protecciones sólidas para los derechos reproductivos. Además, ha fortalecido la capacidad legal de defensoras de los derechos de las mujeres en más de 65 países y en aumento.

Para obtener más información sobre el Centro, por favor visita: www.reproductiverights.org


Rol: La oficina del Centro en Bogotá está buscando un pasante entusiasta, ingenioso y altamente organizado con un compromiso con los temas de derechos reproductivos para participar en una variedad de mini proyectos relacionados con la oficina de Colombia. Requisitos:

title: AI Data & Insights Officer
description:
AI Data & Insights Officer
Borough, South London (SE1 1EP)

Worldwide Events Group

Worldwide Events Group, founded in 2004, is a recognised leader in global MICE and luxury travel. Across our portfolio, we bring people together and facilitate meaningful relationships, a philosophy we call H2H, human‑to‑human connection. Innovation drives our evolution. We’re embracing AI to elevate personalisation, streamline event design and create smarter, more intuitive experiences for our global communities.

Private Luxury Events: Expect the Extraordinary

Private Luxury Events delivers world‑class experiences to the luxury travel community through its event brands Amour, Private Luxury, TFest and Ultra. Our ethos has always been to put the human experience first. This mantra has powered some of the most respected events in the industry, inspiring thousands of luxury travel professionals around the world and at the heart of everything we do lies a passion for connecting people.

M&I

M&I brings together high-calibre meeting planners and exhibitors from the hospitality industry through a series of standout events across Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas. Our portfolio includes M&I Expo, M&I Flagship, M&I Healthcare, and M&I Luxe. We create beautifully crafted events that spark meaningful engagement, from curated 1-2-1 meetings to immersive moments that showcase exceptional destinations, hotels, venues and MICE services. Our events take place across Europe, the Americas and the Middle East in some of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

The Role

The AI Data & Insights Officer is responsible for turning WWE's business data into reliable insight, reusable intelligence and measurable value. Working within Agent Factory, you will ensure that AI agents, automations and decision-makers can access accurate, well-structured and actionable information.

You will work across Salesforce, event platforms, marketing systems, operational tools and AI knowledge sources to improve data quality, build analytical capabilities, support retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), identify commercial opportunities and measure the performance of deployed agents.

This is a hands-on, business-facing role at the intersection of data analysis, business intelligence, AI enablement and commercial decision-making.

This is an initial six-month fixed-term contract opportunity, with the potential for extension, reporting to the Head of AI Implementation.

Responsibilities

Data & Intelligence

  • Develop and maintain datasets, models and insights that support AI agents and business decision-making.
  • Consolidate, cleanse and structure information from Salesforce, event platforms, marketing systems and operational tools.
  • Define practical data-quality, metadata and governance standards for information used by Agent Factory.
  • Identify trends, risks and commercial or operational opportunities within WWE datasets.
  • Support secure, reliable data flows between approved systems and agent solutions.

AI & Agent Enablement

  • Create and maintain knowledge bases and retrieval structures that improve agent accuracy and usefulness.
  • Support the design, testing and optimisation of RAG capabilities across the Agent Factory ecosystem.
  • Prepare evaluation datasets and test cases for assessing agent outputs.
  • Work with Agent Engineers and Agentic Capability Engineers to translate business data into reusable agent skills, tools and intelligence services.
  • Monitor data-related failure patterns and recommend improvements to source content, retrieval and agent behaviour.

Analytics & Performance

  • Design dashboards, scorecards and reporting that provide meaningful visibility of business performance.
  • Define and track measures for agent adoption, accuracy, time saved, operational impact and commercial value.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness and return on investment of AI agents and automations.
  • Develop actionable insight for leadership and business teams rather than producing reporting for its own sake.
  • Establish repeatable methods for monitoring and communicating the value created by Agent Factory.

Commercial & Operational Insight

  • Develop insight that supports customer retention, buyer and supplier engagement, sales effectiveness, event performance and workflow improvement.
  • Explore predictive and segmentation approaches where they can support better business decisions.
  • Turn analytical findings into clear recommendations, prioritised opportunities and defined next actions.
  • Help teams move from descriptive reporting towards decision intelligence and next-best-action capabilities.

Business Partnering

  • Work with departments across WWE to understand their data, reporting and insight requirements.
  • Translate business questions into clear analytical work and practical data products.
  • Present complex findings in a concise, accessible way to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Promote responsible, evidence-led use of data and AI across the organisation.
  • Document analytical methods, data definitions and reusable assets so capabilities can scale.

Due to the nature of our work, you may occasionally be required to work outside standard hours to support events or meet key deadlines

Requirements

You’ll thrive in this AI Data and Insights Officer role if you bring:

  • Professional experience in data analysis, business intelligence, analytics engineering or a closely related role.
  • Strong experience of data preparation, cleansing, modelling and quality assurance.
  • Experience using SQL and visualisation tools such as Power BI, Microsoft Fabric or equivalent platforms.
  • Experience working with CRM, customer, commercial or operational data; Salesforce experience is particularly relevant.
  • Ability to combine information from multiple systems and work effectively with APIs or structured data integrations.
  • Strong understanding of KPI design, dashboarding and the communication of actionable insight.
  • Ability to translate complex evidence into clear business recommendations.
  • Excellent problem-solving, critical-thinking and attention-to-detail skills.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Sound understanding of data privacy, access control and responsible use of business information.
  • Curiosity about AI, automation and the practical application of emerging technology.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

  • Practical experience with RAG architectures, semantic search, vector databases or AI knowledge-management systems.
  • Strong understanding of large language models, machine-learning concepts and agent evaluation methods.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Copilot Studio, Azure AI services or related Microsoft technologies.
  • Familiarity with OpenClaw, Hermes or similar agent platforms.
  • Track record of measuring AI, automation or digital-product performance.
  • Knowledge of predictive analytics, propensity modelling, segmentation or recommendation systems.
  • Understanding of marketing attribution, customer journey analytics or revenue analysis.
  • Ability to design trusted data products or reusable analytical services for consumption by other systems.
  • Background supporting AI transformation, digital transformation or cross-functional change programmes.
  • Background in the events and/or travel industry.

Benefits

We offer a thoughtful package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and work–life balance.

  • Competitive salary.
  • 28 days holiday plus UK bank holidays pro-rata, with additional days awarded for length of service.
  • A centrally located London office with a summer terrace within walking distance of the world‑famous Borough Market.
  • Regular employee social events supported by our Happiness & Culture team.
  • Monthly contribution towards Bupa private health insurance (post probation).
  • Employee Assistance Program offering confidential wellbeing support.
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity leave to support growing families.
  • 4 pm Friday finish!

How to Apply

We review applications on a rolling basis and will close the role once we’ve found our match. To avoid disappointment, apply via the button shown.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We foster an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and able to thrive. We welcome individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences, including differences in gender identity, orientation, expression, age, race, ethnicity, physical or mental ability, neurodiversity, religion or belief, and socio‑economic background. Our diversity strengthens our perspective, fuels innovation, and deepens our connection to the clients and communities we serve around the world.

description:

title: Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional (KIEWIT202609IH104)
description:
ProSidian Seeks a Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional - Construction/Industrial Hygiene (KIEWIT202609IH104) as an Engagement Team Member generally located across the Savannah River Site / Aiken, South Carolina, supporting Environmental Management Sector requirements to support an engagement for a liquid waste contractor (Savannah River Remediation [SRMC]) at the Savannah River Site in Aiken, SC, which is owned by the U.S. Department of Energy..

JOB OVERVIEW

Provide services and support as a Construction/Industrial Hygiene Functional Area Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional (KIEWIT202609IH104) under Labor Category: Health and Safety Specialist at Savannah River Site / Aiken, South Carolina. Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional - Construction/Industrial Hygiene (KIEWIT202609IH104) will work collaboratively as a Contract Consultant on the ProSidian Engagement Team. Dedicated Planned Labor Hours (DPLH) of 1250 Straight Time (ST) Estimated Annual Quantity (Hrs. Per Yr.) | 0 Overtime Time (OT) Estimated Annual Quantity (Hrs. Per Yr.). This is a Labor Hour Subcontract or Contract W-2 (IRS-1099) position, and ProSidian reserves the right to convert to a Full-Time ProSidian employed W-2 Position. The role(s) are located at Savannah River Site / Aiken, South Carolina, with the identified Work Site Address (121 Richland Ave E, Aiken, SC 29801, USA), providing Construction/Industrial Hygiene functions working to provide BOA Support Services for multiple department requirement Service Areas (SA) for Savannah River Remediation LLC (The SRMC/LW Contractor) at the U.S. Department of Energy | Savannah River Site (DOE-SRS) in Aiken, SC, to support the evolving needs of the organization.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES - Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional - Construction/Industrial Hygiene (KIEWIT202609IH104)

  • Serve as a Contract Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional to support construction activities at the U.S. Department of Energy's Savannah River Site (SRS) near Aiken, South Carolina. This client-facing role is with ProSidian and supports Kiewit within its Contractor-Controlled Construction Zone. It is not a direct employment position with Kiewit, and the work area is not a standalone Kiewit facility.
  • The anticipated engagement supports construction and buildout of the High-Fidelity Training and Operations Center (HFTOC), a 103,000-square-foot, non-nuclear training facility supporting the Savannah River Plutonium Processing Facility (SRPPF). The HFTOC will use surrogate materials, like-for-like equipment, and simulated radiological controls to prepare future operators for production, maintenance, material-handling, safety, and emergency-response activities before the SRPPF Main Process Building becomes operational.
  • The project involves demolishing and replacing concrete flooring, modifying the building's interior and exterior, and installing ventilation, process-gas, and electrical systems. It also includes procuring, installing, integrating, testing, and commissioning a high-fidelity production line, along with a material-characterization laboratory, receipt-inspection laboratory, salt-processing training line, balance-of-plant systems, and supporting utilities.
  • The CIH will combine expertise in occupational health science, construction safety leadership, regulatory adherence, contractor oversight, and risk management to prevent injuries, illnesses, releases, property damage, and operational incidents. The role demands regular on-site presence, meticulous documentation, sound technical judgment, and strong coordination with ProSidian, Kiewit, Savannah River Nuclear Solutions (SRNS), DOE/NNSA representatives, subcontractors, occupational medicine, and site industrial hygiene, safety, emergency management, and radiological control teams.

Desired Qualifications For Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional - Construction/Industrial Hygiene (KIEWIT202609IH104) (KIEWIT202609IH104) Candidates:

Integrated Safety and Industrial Hygiene Responsibilities

  • Serve as a dedicated, on-site ProSidian Safety and/or Industrial Hygiene Professional Supporting Kiewit's HFTOC construction activities.
  • Implement and continuously improve applicable elements of the project Safety Management System, Worker Protection Plan, industrial-hygiene program, and Integrated Safety Management requirements.
  • Maintain visible field presence and partner with project leadership, superintendents, supervisors, craft personnel, and subcontractors to plan and execute work safely.
  • Participate in constructability reviews, work-package planning, daily coordination meetings, pre-job briefings, safety meetings, plan-of-the-day meetings, and readiness reviews.
  • Review Job Hazard Analyses (JHAs), Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs), work packages, permits, procedures, and pre-task plans for completeness, technical adequacy, changing conditions, and appropriate controls.
  • Verify that hazards are identified and controlled before work begins and that controls remain effective throughout execution.
  • Exercise stop-work responsibility and immediately elevate imminent-danger, uncontrolled-hazard, or noncompliant conditions in accordance with project procedures and delegated authority.
  • Conduct and document routine field inspections, worker observations, housekeeping inspections, and compliance assessments; communicate deficiencies and track corrective actions to closure.
  • Interpret and apply applicable provisions of 29 CFR Parts 1910 and 1926, 10 CFR Part 851, DOE requirements, SRS procedures, consensus standards, contractual requirements, and project-specific plans.
  • Support event reporting, fact-finding, causal analysis, lessons learned, corrective-action development, and verification of corrective-action effectiveness.
  • Prepare accurate, timely, and defensible records, reports, dashboards, trend analyses, and management briefings.
  • Coordinate safety and health requirements across subcontractors and ensure consistent communication to affected workers.
  • Protect sensitive project and personnel information and maintain records in accordance with site document-control, records-management, and quality-assurance requirements.

Education / Experience Requirements / Qualifications

Standard Qualifications

  • Active CIH certification issued by the Board for Global EHS Credentialing for CIH-designated work; active CSP certification issued by the Board of Certified Safety Professionals for CSP-designated work. Both credentials are required when one individual is assigned both scopes.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible construction field safety, industrial hygiene, or integrated EHS experience, with demonstrated responsibility for high-hazard work.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting large-scale commercial, industrial, nuclear, power, chemical, defense, or federal construction projects.
  • Thorough working knowledge of 29 CFR Parts 1910 and 1926 and 10 CFR Part 851.
  • Working knowledge of hazard identification, exposure assessment, hierarchy of controls, contractor safety, incident investigation, emergency planning, and corrective-action management.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret technical drawings, specifications, safety data sheets, work packages, sampling data, procedures, and regulatory requirements.
  • Experience working independently in the field while coordinating effectively with multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Strong technical writing, presentation, coaching, facilitation, and conflict-resolution capabilities.
  • Ability to maintain certification, training, medical, respirator-use, site-access, and other qualification requirements throughout the assignment.
  • U.S. citizenship and ability to satisfy DOE, SRS, SRNS, Kiewit, and ProSidian background screening, badging, drug-testing, fitness-for-duty, and site-access requirements.
  • Valid driver's license. Any personal vehicle used for project business must maintain valid registration and legally required insurance, with proof available as required.

Education Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution in industrial hygiene, occupational safety and health, environmental health, engineering, chemistry, biology, physics, public health, or a closely related scientific or technical discipline.
  • An advanced degree in industrial hygiene, occupational health, safety engineering, environmental health, or a related discipline is preferred.
  • For CIH assignments: active CIH credential in good standing and professional-level experience encompassing exposure anticipation, recognition, evaluation, control, and program management across multiple occupational-health stressor categories.

Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional - Construction/Industrial Hygiene (KIEWIT202609IH104) Candidates shall work to support requirements for KIEWIT09042026IH104 Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH)/Safety Professional (Construction/Industrial Hygiene Services) and provide BOA Support Services for multiple department requirement Service Areas (SA) for Savannah River Remediation LLC (The SRMC/LW Contractor) at the U.S. Department of Energy | Savannah River Site (DOE-SRS) in Aiken, SC to support the evolving needs of the organization.

Skills Required

Primarily focused on Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) / Safety Professional initiatives and aligned with Program Support activities in the Construction/Industrial Hygiene Functional Area.

  • Industrial hygiene exposure assessment, sampling strategy, instrumentation, calibration, data interpretation, and control validation.
  • Construction safety planning, field inspection, JHA/AHA review, permit review, hazard mitigation, and compliance assurance.
  • Knowledge of chemical hazards, toxicology, respiratory protection, ventilation, noise, heat stress, ergonomics, silica, asbestos, lead, welding fumes, coatings, solvents, and hazardous-material controls.
  • Knowledge of fall protection, scaffolding, excavation, electrical safety, lockout/tagout, confined spaces, hot work, cranes, rigging, lifting, mobile equipment, and emergency response.
  • Ability to apply the hierarchy of controls and distinguish engineering, administrative, work-practice, and PPE controls.
  • Incident investigation, interviewing, evidence evaluation, causal analysis, trend analysis, and corrective-action tracking.
  • Clear written and verbal communication with executives, engineers, field supervision, craft personnel, clients, regulators, and subcontractors.
  • Ability to deliver training, facilitate meetings, influence without direct authority, and intervene constructively when unsafe conditions arise.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and electronic EHS, document-control, or reporting systems.
  • Ability to organize high-volume technical records while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality, traceability, and timely reporting.

Competencies Required

  • Safety and health leadership: Demonstrates personal ownership of worker protection and reinforces that production objectives never justify uncontrolled risk.
  • Technical credibility: Applies current scientific, regulatory, and professional principles and recognizes when additional expertise is required.
  • Risk-based judgment: Prioritizes hazards based on severity, probability, exposure, uncertainty, and changing field conditions.
  • Field engagement: Builds trust with craft personnel and supervisors through visibility, responsiveness, practical solutions, and respectful intervention.
  • Communication and influence: Converts complex technical requirements into clear expectations and gains cooperation across organizational boundaries.
  • Problem solving: Identifies root causes, evaluates alternatives, and develops controls that are protective, practical, and sustainable.
  • Quality and documentation discipline: Produces complete, accurate, traceable, and timely records suitable for management, audit, and regulatory review.
  • Collaboration: Coordinates effectively with construction, engineering, quality, operations, occupational medicine, emergency management, environmental, and radiological-control functions.
  • Adaptability: Responds effectively to evolving designs, schedules, work fronts, hazards, and client priorities without compromising standards.
  • Integrity and professional ethics: Exercises independent professional judgment, communicates limitations or unresolved risk, and protects workers, the public, and the environment.
  • Continuous improvement: Uses observations, monitoring data, trends, events, and lessons learned to improve planning and performance.

Security, Access, and Conduct

  • Must maintain eligibility for unescorted or assigned access to applicable SRS facilities and work areas. A specific security clearance is not promised unless identified in the final task order.
  • Must comply with all federal-site security, prohibited-article, cybersecurity, information-protection, fitness-for-duty, substance-abuse, and workplace-conduct requirements.
  • Must immediately report any condition that could affect credential status, site access, fitness for duty, or ability to perform assigned responsibilities.
  • Must protect controlled, proprietary, personal, and project-sensitive information and use approved systems and communication channels.

Reporting and Interfaces

The CIH/CSP will report administratively through the designated ProSidian Engagement Manager and receive day-to-day priorities through authorized project leadership. The role will interface with Kiewit project management and EHS personnel; SRNS safety, industrial-hygiene, engineering, quality, and operations organizations; DOE/NNSA representatives; subcontractors; vendors; analytical laboratories; occupational medicine; emergency-response organizations; and radiological-control personnel.

Representative Deliverables

  • Daily and weekly field safety and industrial-hygiene reports
  • Exposure-assessment plans and similar-exposure-group determinations
  • Sampling records, calibration logs, chain-of-custody forms, laboratory results, and exposure notifications
  • JHA/AHA, work-package, permit, and procedure review comments
  • Inspection findings, worker-observation records, and corrective-action logs
  • Incident fact-finding, investigation, causal-analysis, and lessons-learned documentation
  • Training materials, attendance records, qualification records, and safety-meeting documentation
  • Leading and lagging indicator reports, trend analyses, dashboards, and management briefings
  • Readiness review, walkdown, punch-list, commissioning, and turnover support documentation

title: Agent Engineer
description:
Agent Engineer (FTC)
Borough, South London (SE1 1EP)

Worldwide Events Group

Worldwide Events Group, founded in 2004, is a recognised leader in global MICE and luxury travel. Across our portfolio, we bring people together and facilitate meaningful relationships, a philosophy we call H2H, human‑to‑human connection. Innovation drives our evolution. We’re embracing AI to elevate personalisation, streamline event design and create smarter, more intuitive experiences for our global communities.

Private Luxury Events: Expect the Extraordinary

Private Luxury Events delivers world‑class experiences to the luxury travel community through its event brands Amour, Private Luxury, TFest and Ultra. Our ethos has always been to put the human experience first. This mantra has powered some of the most respected events in the industry, inspiring thousands of luxury travel professionals around the world and at the heart of everything we do lies a passion for connecting people.

M&I

M&I brings together high-calibre meeting planners and exhibitors from the hospitality industry through a series of standout events across Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas. Our portfolio includes M&I Expo, M&I Flagship, M&I Healthcare, and M&I Luxe. We create beautifully crafted events that spark meaningful engagement, from curated 1-2-1 meetings to immersive moments that showcase exceptional destinations, hotels, venues and MICE services. Our events take place across Europe, the Americas and the Middle East in some of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

The Role

The Agent Engineer is responsible for designing, building, testing, deploying and maintaining production-ready AI agents, tools and workflows using WWE's approved technology ecosystem.

Working alongside Agent Factory, technical colleagues and business stakeholders, you will turn defined requirements into reliable agent solutions, create reusable technical capabilities and improve deployed agents through rapid iteration.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on agent delivery rather than organisational change management or team leadership.

This is an initial six-month fixed-term contract opportunity, with the potential for extension, reporting to the Head of AI Implementation.

Responsibilities

Agent Development

  • Design, build and deploy AI agents for teams across the business.
  • Create reusable agent skills, tools and workflows.
  • Develop multi-agent orchestration patterns where appropriate.
  • Translate functional requirements into robust, production-ready solutions.

Platform Delivery

  • Build solutions using WWE's approved AI platforms and frameworks.
  • Configure and maintain OpenClaw environments and develop Hermes-based workflows.
  • Build and maintain Microsoft Copilot Studio agents.
  • Integrate agents with Salesforce, SharePoint, Microsoft 365 and approved internal systems.

Automation & Workflow Engineering

  • Develop automations that remove manual effort from operational processes.
  • Build secure integrations between internal platforms and approved AI services.
  • Improve agent reliability, performance and accuracy.
  • Design technical components that can scale across multiple departments.

Testing, Security & Quality Assurance

  • Test agents against real business scenarios and defined acceptance criteria.
  • Monitor performance, diagnose failure points and implement improvements.
  • Ensure solutions operate within WWE security, governance and data-access requirements.
  • Document architecture, dependencies, functionality and support requirements.

Reusable Capability Library

  • Build reusable components that can be shared across the organisation.
  • Create and maintain a catalogue of agent skills and integrations.
  • Contribute to Agent Factory engineering standards and best practices.
  • Support the development of orchestration agents and the wider AI harness.

Due to the nature of our work, you may occasionally be required to work outside standard hours to support events or meet key deadlines

Requirements

You’ll thrive in this Agent Engineer role if you bring:

  • Practical experience building AI agents, automations or LLM-enabled applications.
  • Strong prompt engineering and agent-instruction design skills.
  • Experience integrating APIs and business systems.
  • Familiarity with large language models, agent frameworks and tool use.
  • Programming experience in Python, JavaScript or a comparable language.
  • Understanding of structured and unstructured data sources.
  • Strong analytical, debugging and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to prototype rapidly and convert successful prototypes into supportable solutions.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

  • Experience with OpenClaw and Hermes.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365 integrations.
  • Practical experience integrating Salesforce platforms and APIs.
  • Familiarity with Model Context Protocol (MCP) and agent tooling.
  • Knowledge of retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases and orchestration patterns.
  • Understanding of secure enterprise AI development, access control and auditability.
  • Proficiency with Git, automated testing and deployment practices.
  • Background in the events and/or travel industry.

Benefits

We offer a thoughtful package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and work–life balance.

  • Competitive Salary.
  • 28 days holiday plus UK bank holidays pro-rata, with additional days awarded for length of service.
  • A centrally located London office with a summer terrace within walking distance of the world‑famous Borough Market.
  • Regular employee social events supported by our Happiness & Culture team.
  • Monthly contribution towards Bupa private health insurance (post probation).
  • Employee Assistance Program offering confidential wellbeing support.
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity leave to support growing families.
  • 4 pm Friday finish!

How to Apply

We review applications on a rolling basis and will close the role once we’ve found our match. To avoid disappointment, apply via the button shown.

Our Commitment to Diversity

We foster an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and able to thrive. We welcome individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences, including differences in gender identity, orientation, expression, age, race, ethnicity, physical or mental ability, neurodiversity, religion or belief, and socio‑economic background. Our diversity strengthens our perspective, fuels innovation, and deepens our connection to the clients and communities we serve around the world.

title: DevOps Engineer @ Scaleworks
description:
The Role
You will join a lean engineering organization and take ownership of cloud infrastructure, delivery pipelines, database operations, and observability for a revenue-generating production platform. This is a hands-on role with direct exposure to engineering leadership. You will make infrastructure decisions, document them, and carry them through to production. The scope is broad by design: infrastructure, databases, security operations, and the automation that ties it all together.
What You Will Work On
  • Operating and evolving a production AWS environment: EC2, load balancing, S3, RDS, IAM, VPC networking, and infrastructure automation
  • Administering and tuning databases across multiple engines in production: MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MSSQL, including performance work, replication health, backup and recovery, and cost control
  • Supporting analytical data workloads, including Snowflake-based pipelines and reporting infrastructure
  • Building and maintaining the observability layer: monitoring, alerting, SLOs, synthetic checks, and availability reporting that supports customer-facing commitments
  • Owning CI/CD pipelines end to end, from build tooling and static checks to deployment automation and rollback procedures
  • Applying AI tooling to DevOps work in practice: AI-assisted incident analysis, infrastructure code generation and review, automated runbook execution, and agent-based workflows for routine operations
  • Supporting a SOC 2 compliance program on the infrastructure side: log retention, access control, asset inventory, and audit evidence collection
  • Planning and executing maintenance windows, OS image lifecycle management, and database upgrades with minimal customer impact

Our Stack
AWS, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Snowflake, GitHub, containerized CI/CD, compliance automation tooling, and a modern AI-assisted engineering workflow used across the team.
  • 4+ years of hands-on experience running production infrastructure on AWS

title: Senior FPGA Engineer
description:
The Mission

At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve successfully transitioned quantum computing from an academic dream into a commercial reality. The most exciting thing is that we’re just getting started.

As a Senior FPGA Engineer, you’ll play a critical role in designing and delivering the precision control hardware that powers our quantum computing systems. You’ll help solve complex technical challenges across FPGA architecture, high-speed data systems, and real-time signal processing — contributing directly to the advancement of scalable quantum computing technologies.

The Role

We’re looking for a Senior FPGA Engineer to join our Advanced Product Development Group (APD), working on purpose-built FPGA hardware for quantum computing applications. This role combines deep technical expertise with cross-functional collaboration, system-level thinking, and mentorship responsibilities within a highly innovative engineering environment.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Defining scalable FPGA architectures with a focus on deterministic timing, synchronization, maintainability, and multi-card communication.
  • Designing, implementing, and verifying complex RTL for high-performance microwave and RF applications.
  • Developing interfaces and control logic for high-speed ADCs, DACs, memory systems, and RF SoC platforms.
  • Implementing real-time DSP algorithms optimized for FPGA resources and multi-clock domain designs.
  • Supporting hardware bring-up, lab integration, verification activities, and system-level testing.
  • Collaborating closely with Electronics, Embedded Software, Mechanical, Cryogenic, and Deployment teams to deliver fully integrated systems.
  • Mentoring junior engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and development best practices while contributing to project planning and technical documentation.

What We're Looking For

  • Commercial experience in FPGA design and verification within complex hardware environments.
  • Experience with System Verilog, and/or VHDL.
  • Expert-level proficiency in Verilog and deep understanding of FPGA architectures.
  • Strong experience achieving timing closure on high-utilization FPGA designs and writing timing constraints.
  • Experience developing systems involving high-speed ADCs/DACs, synchronization across multiple boards/subsystems, and real-time DSP.
  • Ability to work independently on technically challenging projects while balancing delivery, quality, and risk.
  • Experience collaborating across multidisciplinary engineering teams in fast-paced R&D or product development environments.
  • Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Engineering or a related technical discipline.
  • Strong communication, leadership, problem-solving, and stakeholder management skills.

The 'Nice-to-Haves'

  • Background in RF and microwave applications.
  • Experience developing control electronics for quantum computing systems.
  • Familiarity with Altera Quartus toolchains.
  • Experience using spectrum analysers, oscilloscopes, and MATLAB/Simulink for DSP modelling.
  • Exposure to compliance and validation activities including EMI/EMC, CE, or FCC standards.
  • Experience representing engineering teams externally through conferences, technical talks, or industry collaborations.

Why Join OQC

You will join a world-class team at the forefront of the next computational era. We offer a culture of bold innovation, the chance to work with unique lab infrastructure, and the opportunity to see your work redefine the limits of computation.

title: Platform Engineer (DevOps)
description:
About Us

Food waste costs the world over $1 trillion a year. At Winnow, we're on a mission to change that — bringing AI-powered technology into hospitality kitchens to help eliminate waste at scale, with an ambition to save our clients $1 billion annually.

We started in London in 2013 with a simple belief: technology could make kitchens smarter and food systems more sustainable. Today that belief has grown into a global team spanning the UK, Romania, Dubai, Shanghai, Singapore, Malaysia, North America, and Mexico, working across 90+ countries and 3,500+ sites.

We're proud of the results we help our clients achieve. Names like IKEA, Hilton, Accor, Marriott, IHG, Compass Group, Iberostar, and Mandarin Oriental trust us to cut their food waste by over 50% on average — and when our technology is fully adopted, it reduces pre-consumer waste by 50–70% and delivers food cost savings of 2–8%.

We're building something that matters, and the people who thrive here feel that every day. We're proud to have been named one of The Sunday Times Best Places to Work and ranked #4 in the FoodTech 500 (2025) — recognition of both our innovation and our commitment to building a purpose-led company where people can make a real difference.

Our values

Our values aren't just words on a page. They sit at the centre of all that we do and shape our behaviours and the way we show up. If they resonate with you, we'd love to hear from you and for you to help us on our mission.

  • People of action — done beats perfect. We move fast, learn faster
  • Equal parts head and heart — we balance urgency with long-term thinking
  • Hungry and humble — we're ambitious about our mission, not our egos
  • Bravely honest — we say what we think, respectfully, with colleagues and customers alike
  • Bound by food — it's what unites us, and it's what we're fighting for
  • People and planet positive — we're leaving both better than we found them

The team

You'd be joining a small, senior platform team. We work closely with the engineers who rely on our platform daily, so communication and empathy for their day-to-day pain points matter as much as technical depth.

This is a team that's comfortable with ambiguity, a lot of what we're building (especially around agentic engineering) doesn't have a playbook yet, so we value people who can define the problem as well as solve it.

About the role

Most platform jobs mean AWS or GCP accounts and a Kubernetes cluster. This one also means a fleet of Linux IoT devices we design and manufacture ourselves, sitting in commercial kitchens around the world and streaming data back to us. There's an on-prem GPU cluster running ML workloads, and a data estate covering Aurora Postgres, MySQL, Redshift, Timescale, Mongo and DynamoDB.

We use that stack to fight food waste. Our devices watch what gets thrown away in professional kitchens and tell chefs how to stop it. It works, and we’re deployed in kitchens in 94 countries and counting.

Your customers are our own engineers and data scientists. Your job is to make their route to production short, safe and boring.

The problem we most want help with

We're working out how agentic engineering actually works at Winnow: how AI agents fit into the way we build, review, test and ship, and what platform they need underneath them to be useful rather than a liability.

This work has just begun. We need to design the guardrails, the golden paths, the evaluation, the permissions model and the cost controls. In large part it's a platform problem, and nobody seems to have properly solved it yet, here or anywhere else.

Key responsibilities:

  • Design and build the platform for agentic engineering at Winnow: guardrails, golden paths, evals and cost controls, so our engineers can hand real work to an agent without it going badly.
  • Build and run the golden paths for humans too, the paved routes our engineers use to ship to production without having to become infrastructure experts.
  • Own our AWS and GCP infrastructure as code (Terraform with Terragrunt), across ECS for services and EKS for platform components like ELK, Grafana and Airflow.
  • DevOps: Work with development teams to improve how we deploy. Faster feedback, fewer manual steps, safer rollbacks. We measure this and we expect it to get better.
  • Support our data science and AI workloads: Airflow pipelines, SageMaker, and GPU scheduling on the on-prem cluster.
  • Debug the hard things across clouds, databases, containers, network and edge.

Requirements

Education and experience

  • You are likely to be degree-educated having completed studies in Computer science, computer engineering, information technology, or a related field.
  • Solid AWS experience, plus Linux and networking fundamentals you can reason from
  • Essential skills:
    • Infrastructure as code, Terraform or OpenTofu.
    • Containers and orchestration: ECS, Kubernetes, or both.
    • Bash, plus Python or Go at a level where you'd happily own a service.
    • CI/CD pipelines you've built and maintained, not just used.
    • You use AI coding assistants and agents day to day, and you have views on where they help, where they don't, and what would have to be true before you'd trust one with something that matters.
  • Nice to have:
    • Observability (OpenTelemetry, Grafana, ELK, New Relic)
    • GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux)
    • Airflow, SageMaker or MLflow
    • LLM infrastructure such as inference serving, evals and LLM/ MCP gateways
    • SecOps, container scanning (Checkov, Trivy) & secrets management
    • Cloud and GPU cost optimisation
    • Postgres, MySQL, Redshift beyond the basics
    • IoT or edge fleet operations
    • Ansible or similar
    • Jenkins, Github Actions

Nobody has all of these. Apply anyway. We'd rather hire someone curious who learns fast than someone who ticks nine boxes and stops there.

Our Technology

Technology is at the forefront of what we do, and the success of our company is based on our world-class technology and on finding solutions to real-world problems that have not been solved to date. Our current stack includes:

  • Designing and manufacturing IoT ‘smart’ edge devices and expanding using Linux-powered devices on the field collecting data using cutting-edge technologies.
  • AWS Cloud focused (with minor parts in GCP and Azure) managed by Terraform with Terragrunt.
  • AWS ECS for containerised “microservice” workloads.
  • EKS for many of our platform components, including ELK, Grafana, Apache airflow.
  • Databases include Aurora Postgres + MySQL, Redshift, Timescale, Mongo, and DynamoDB.
  • Apache airflow and AWS SageMaker for data science uses.
  • On-prem data center for ML GPU workloads.
  • BitBucket, Jenkins, SonarQube, New Relic, Docker, Terraform.
  • JIRA, Confluence, BitBucket (Atlassian products), Agile team using Scrum or Kanban (each team chooses the best approach to drive results).

Personal attributes

  • You are results-driven and can demonstrate how you have delivered effective solutions in a timely manner.
  • You take ownership without waiting to be asked, and you flag ambiguity early instead of guessing.
  • You have experience working as part of a global team and building positive relationships with internal and external individuals across borders.
  • You treat other engineers as customers, and you solve for the underlying problem, rather than patching the same solution for the nth time.
  • You're pragmatic about trade-offs, and happy to ship something good now and improve it rather than wait for perfect.
  • You work well across borders and time zones. Our team is distributed and much of the collaboration is written and asynchronous.
  • You pitch in when you see someone stuck
  • Able to organise self, including effective scheduling, prioritisation, and time management skills, managing multiple tasks in parallel and completing tasks to tight deadlines.
  • Demonstrates excellent communication skills in English. You are a confident and articulate presenter. You communicate clearly in both written and spoken language. You listen attentively; you process and comprehend what you hear. You are also confident enough to ask questions and clarify ambiguous points.
  • Track record of identifying problems, analysing options, and deploying sound decision-making skills.
  • Motivated and curious, you love absorbing new information and are able to reliably recall and figure out how to rapidly apply it. You have the courage, when appropriate to learn new technology rather than sticking to what you know already.

Benefits

  • Company stock options package
  • Company part-funded private health insurance and eye care allowance
  • Life insurance (3 times base salary)
  • Meal tickets – 40 RON per working day
  • 25 days of paid vacation time in addition to national holidays, plus the option to buy a further 5 days annual leave
  • Learning and development allowance of 1,730 RON annually
  • 274 RON gross monthly wellness allowance, or the option to swap the wellness allowance for a 7Card subscription
  • Employee Assistance Programme – 24/7 helpline for your wellbeing
  • Hybrid way of working – we're all in the office on Wednesdays and Thursdays
  • Early Finish Fridays – log off at 3 PM on a Friday if you have completed your tasks by then
  • Our own office space with a great working environment
  • You will love what you do – waking up every day solving one of the biggest social problems of our generation – food waste
  • Committed team members with broad experience who share a common passion to build a world class business

title: Join our Talent Pool: Strategy, Design, and Experimentation
description:
Location: Fully remote (Europe)
Contract: Freelance (per project requirements)
Day Rate: TBD based on role, experience, and project scope

The problem we solve

Most corporate innovation fails because teams spend months (and millions) building things nobody wants. They guess. They assume. They plan in detail, and then reality arrives – the customer.

At Future Foundry, we help large organisations test first, build later. We replace costly assumptions with lightweight, real-world experiments that reveal what customers actually want before our clients commit serious time and money.

We've spent the last five years developing a structured, repeatable approach to business experimentation. In that time, we've run +500 experiments and saved +£1 billion in misallocated investment for some of the largest global innovation teams. Working with the likes of Mars, Experian, HSBC, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Hilton to de-risk new propositions, get to market faster, and make evidence-backed investment decisions.

What we do

We break experimentation into four core services:

1. Innovation Strategy – Defining where and how corporate innovation teams can realise growth over the next 3–5 years, forming an investment thesis around a portfolio of new opportunities.

2. Opportunity Validation – This is where the practical testing comes in. We design and deploy lightweight, behavioural experiments to validate the riskiest assumptions about new growth opportunities. The outcome is a clear, de-risked investment decision to accelerate, adapt, or withdraw.

3. Pre-launch Test Roadmap – Once teams have decided to pilot an opportunity, we develop structured test plans that ensure they're measuring the right things to make an informed decision on launch or roll-out.

4. Capability Building – Designing the capability and operating model required to embed experimentation in large organisations – from hands-on experiment training and innovation leadership programmes to practical courses and workshops.

Requirements

We're always on the lookout for great talent to help us deliver our projects on a freelance basis. Whether you have a few days or a few weeks available, we'd love to hear from you.

We typically hire across three types of roles:

Lead: 5–10 years of experience, including proven leadership of experimentation or innovation programmes. You'll lead the design and execution of experimentation programmes for clients, manage small teams (2–3 people), and act as the primary client interface. You're comfortable facilitating workshops with senior stakeholders, turning evidence into strategic recommendations, and taking ownership of complex projects end-to-end.

Consultant: 3–7 years of experience in experimentation, user research, venture design, or corporate innovation. You'll design and run experiments hands-on – from recruiting participants and conducting interviews to setting up ads and tracking data. You can facilitate workshops, synthesise findings into clear recommendations, and flex across research, analysis, and client management with comfort in ambiguity.

Associate: 1–3 years of experience in user research, customer validation, or supporting innovation teams. You'll support the execution of behavioural experiments, recruit and coordinate participants, conduct customer interviews, and track validation metrics. You're highly organised, proactive, and comfortable documenting findings clearly while working collaboratively with senior consultants.

Across all our roles, we are looking for the following attributes:

  • Hands-on experimentation experience – We're not looking for "desk research" consultants; we need people who've run real-world tests with customers
  • A proactive, get-things-done mentality – We're a lean, flat organisation where everyone rolls up their sleeves
  • Comfort with ambiguity – Experiments don't always go to plan; you adapt quickly when they don't
  • Collaborative mindset – You're energised by working closely with clients and teammates, not operating solo
  • Strong communication skills – You can distil complex findings into clear, compelling insights (written and verbal)
  • Right to work in Europe – We're unfortunately not able to sponsor visas at this time

Nice to have:

  • Experience working in or with startups (you understand the "build-measure-learn" mentality)
  • Familiarity with the industries we work in: retail, FMCG, healthcare, and financial services
  • Knowledge of design thinking, lean startup, jobs-to-be-done, or similar methodologies

Benefits

  • Flexibility – Work on projects that fit your schedule, whether that's a few days or a few weeks
  • Impact – Be part of the innovation journey for top-tier corporate clients, helping them make multi-million-pound investment decisions with confidence
  • Learning – Work with a small, dedicated team of highly skilled practitioners; you'll learn cutting-edge experimentation methodologies
  • Variety – Exposure to diverse industries and complex challenges (construction, financial services, healthcare, climate tech)
  • Remote-first – Work from anywhere in Europe with occasional travel to client sites (UK/Europe/US, all expenses covered)
  • Fair compensation – Day rates negotiated based on role, experience, and project scope

Procon seeks an experienced Construction Inspector for a long-term opportunity in the Charlotte, NC area, supporting a Tenant Improvement interior fit-out for a new Passport Office. The Construction Inspector will provide on-site quality assurance and construction oversight, ensuring work is completed in accordance with contract documents, project specifications, applicable codes, and established quality and safety standards. This is primarily a day-shift position, with some weekend work required based on project needs and the construction schedule.

This position does not offer employment visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship.

  • Strong knowledge of construction safety protocols, OSHA requirements, and jobsite safety best practices.

title: Assistant Behavior Analyst (BCaBA, LABA)
description:

The Opportunity: Assistant Behavior Analyst (BCaBA, LABA)

Interested in Early Intervention?

The Assistant Behavior Analyst role is a mid-tier supervisory position that combines providing direct therapy services with acting as a licensed assistant behavior analyst for various insurance-based school district funding sources. This is a unique hybrid role that allows BCBA candidates to accrue unrestricted fieldwork supervision hours while delivering direct therapy to assigned clients. The primary focus is young kiddos, or early intervention learners.

You will assist an assigned clinician with a defined caseload, providing critical support to the clinical team and contributing to the overall success of the agency. This position requires a positive, supportive attitude, independent thinking, excellent communication, and strong clinical critical thinking skills.

Key Responsibilities (Duties include, but are not limited to):

  • Clinical Service Delivery:
    • Provide direct therapy services as assigned clinic, school, and/or home settings.
    • Implement evidence-based ABA service delivery procedures (intake, therapy, assessment, parent training, staff training).
    • Work with clients varying in age from infant to young adult, demonstrating competence with a wide variety of behaviors, including aggression, self-injury, eloping, and property destruction.
    • Demonstrate effective de-escalation skills and the ability to independently support novel clients.
  • Documentation & Compliance:
    • Independently use the clinical software system (CentralReach) for review of client progress and data-based modification of learning programs.
    • Accurate and timely documentation of all client service session notes.
    • Development and timely submission of client-specific treatment and behavior intervention plans to funding sources.
    • Adherence to billing standards and delivering 90% utilization of all authorized hours/codes monthly.
  • Professional Conduct:
    • Strictly adhere to the Professional and Ethical Compliance Code issued by the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).
    • Consistently demonstrate a high level of integrity, responsibility, accountability, and teamwork.

Requirements

    • Must be at least 21 years of age.
    • Have a Bachelor’s or Master's Degree in ABA, Psychology, Education, or a related field and currently be enrolled in an accredited ABA Master’s Degree program seeking certification as a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA).(Must be actively seeking certification to continue in this role.)
    • Hold a current certification as a licensed assistant behavior analyst in the state of Washington.
    • Completion of at least three BACB certification courses with a verified course sequence from the Association of Behavior Analysis International (ABAI).
    • Must be qualified under state, county, and payor requirements for your region on an ongoing basis.
    • Completion of First Aid and CPR training within 30 days of hiring (Required).
    • Background and fingerprinting clearance (Required).

Pay Scale:

Direct Intervention: $28.00-$30.00/hour

Supervision: $35.00-$40.00/hour

Work Environment Highlights

The working environment involves working directly with individuals with developmental disabilities. This includes managing high-volume auditory sounds and behaviors such as aggression, eloping, self-injury, and property destruction. Services may require flexible scheduling, including rotating opening/closing shifts (clinic based), and driving to treatment sites (home, clinic, or community). Support activities may involve activities of daily living such as eating, toileting, and hygiene skill development.
