title: Senior Product Designer (UX/UI)
description:
About the Role

CubX is looking for a Senior Product Designer to own the design of complex internal and client-facing IT products and workflows.

This is a hands-on product design role for someone who can take a messy operational problem, understand how it actually works, turn it into a clear system, and design a polished, intuitive product experience.

You'll work across UX, interaction design, systems design, and visual UI design. Strong systems thinking is essential, but so is strong visual craft.

We're looking for someone who can determine what should be built, how it should work, and what the final product should look and feel like.

This is not a role where you hand off a workflow diagram or wireframe and move on. You'll own the experience from discovery and problem definition through polished, implementation-ready designs.

What You'll Do

  • Own end-to-end product design for complex internal operational tools, many of which may eventually extend into client-facing experiences.
  • Turn manual and ambiguous processes currently handled through tickets, spreadsheets, notes, conversations, and human judgment into structured product workflows.
  • Partner closely with product, engineering, operations, and other stakeholders to understand how processes work today and determine how they should work in software.
  • Define the underlying structure of complex experiences, including:
  • User flows and information architecture
  • Roles and permissions
  • Approval paths
  • System states and edge cases
  • Business rules
  • Configuration models
  • Error and exception handling
  • Ask strong questions during discovery and challenge assumptions when requirements are unclear, incomplete, or unnecessarily complicated.
  • Determine what should be solved through UX, what should be configurable, and what logic belongs within the underlying system.
  • Create wireframes and interactive prototypes to validate workflows before moving into detailed design.
  • Design polished, production-ready interfaces in Figma.
  • Design real operational UI, including forms, tables, dashboards, navigation, configuration interfaces, admin controls, filters, bulk actions, permissions, empty states, error states, and loading states.
  • Collaborate closely with engineering throughout implementation to resolve details and ensure the shipped product reflects the intended experience.
  • Help establish reusable components, patterns, and design standards across a growing multi-product platform.
  • Design experiences that serve both internal operators who need power, efficiency, and flexibility and end users who need clarity and simplicity.

What We're Looking For

You have strong product design experience working on complex software products, particularly in areas such as:

  • B2B SaaS
  • Internal tools
  • Admin platforms
  • Enterprise software
  • Workflow-heavy applications
  • Configuration-heavy systems

You should be comfortable taking a vague business problem and independently turning it into:

Problem Definition → Workflow → System Model → UX → Polished UI → Implementation-Ready Design

Strong candidates will have experience with:

  • Product and UX discovery
  • Complex workflow design
  • Information architecture
  • Interaction design
  • High-quality visual UI design
  • Forms and configuration experiences
  • Tables and data-heavy interfaces
  • Role-based access and permissions
  • Approval workflows
  • Edge cases and system states
  • Design systems and reusable components
  • Prototyping in Figma
  • Cross-functional collaboration with engineering and operations

Strong Visual Craft Is Required

  • This is not a purely visual design role, but visual design is an essential part of the job.
  • We need someone who can untangle a complicated workflow and create the right system behind it—and then turn that thinking into a polished, intuitive, professional product interface.
  • You'll be expected to own both the underlying UX logic and the final UI.
  • A designer who creates beautiful screens but struggles with systems thinking will not be successful in this role.
  • Likewise, a designer who is strong at research, diagrams, and wireframes but cannot produce high-quality final product designs will not be successful.

We're looking for someone who can do both.

You'll Be Designing for Complexity

Many of our products operate in environments where seemingly simple actions can have significant downstream consequences.

You'll need to naturally think through questions such as:

  • Who is allowed to perform this action?
  • Does someone else need to approve it?
  • What happens if the request is rejected?
  • What changes depending on the client, user, location, or role?
  • What should be configurable versus hardcoded?
  • What information does an internal operator need that an end user shouldn't see?
  • What happens when something fails halfway through a workflow?
  • How do we make a powerful system simple without removing necessary flexibility?

We're looking for a designer who naturally considers these questions while designing—not only after problems arise.

Nice to Have

Experience with any of the following is a plus:

  • MSP or IT operations
  • IT service management
  • Provisioning
  • Device or inventory management
  • Procurement
  • Approval systems
  • Enterprise administration
  • Multi-tenant SaaS
  • Security-sensitive products
  • Rule-based or configuration-heavy software
  • AI-assisted design and development workflows

Prior MSP experience is not required. However, you should be comfortable learning operationally complex domains and translating them into understandable software experiences.

What Success Looks Like

  • You're able to take a process currently managed through tickets, spreadsheets, notes, tribal knowledge, and human judgment and turn it into a productized workflow with clear rules and minimal ambiguity.
  • You understand that scalable product design isn't just about designing screens.
  • You think about: Systems. Rules. Metadata. Permissions. Configuration. Edge cases. Reusable patterns.
  • You consider how the product will evolve—not only what it needs to accomplish today.
  • At the same time, you care deeply about the quality of the interface users actually experience.
  • Your work makes complicated systems feel understandable without hiding the complexity that operators genuinely need.

You can effectively design for both:

  • Internal operators, who need efficiency, visibility, control, and flexibility.
  • End users, who need simplicity, guidance, and confidence.

Most importantly, you can partner closely with engineering to turn those designs into real, shipped software.

What This Role Is Not

  • This is not primarily a branding or marketing design role.
  • This is not a UX-only role that stops at research, journey maps, flows, or wireframes.
  • This is not a purely visual role where requirements are handed to you and your job is simply to make them look better.
  • This is not a junior production design role.

We're looking for a Product Designer who can understand the problem, design the system, and design the actual product.

Requirements

Required

  • 3+ years of Product Design experience building B2B SaaS, enterprise software, internal tools, or workflow-driven products.
  • Proven ability to take ambiguous business problems from discovery through shipped product.
  • Strong systems-thinking skills with experience defining workflows, permissions, approvals, business rules, configurations, system states, and edge cases.
  • Experience designing complex operational software, including forms, tables, dashboards, admin tools, and configuration interfaces.
  • Strong UX, interaction design, information architecture, and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong visual design skills with the ability to create polished, production-ready interfaces.
  • Advanced proficiency in Figma, including prototyping and design systems.
  • Experience collaborating closely with engineering, product, and operational stakeholders.
  • Ability to lead discovery, ask insightful questions, challenge assumptions, and clarify requirements.
  • Portfolio demonstrating end-to-end ownership from problem definition → workflow design → UX → final UI → implementation.

Preferred

  • Experience with enterprise software, internal tools, workflow automation, configuration-heavy systems, or multi-tenant SaaS.
  • Experience designing role-based access, approval workflows, and administrative platforms.
  • Familiarity with MSP, IT Operations, ITSM, provisioning, procurement, inventory, or asset management systems.
  • Experience designing security-sensitive or rules-based products.
  • Experience using AI-assisted design and product development workflows.

Benefits

  • Competitive pay with performance-based growth
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance options
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • On-site gym for employee wellness
  • Modern, collaborative office environment
  • Ongoing training and professional development
  • Opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology
  • Team events and employee appreciation initiatives
  • Strong company culture focused on innovation and teamwork

title: Knowledge Hub Coordinator - Coordonnateur du Knowledge Hub
description:
About the Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages (OCIL)


The Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages is dedicated to promoting and championing Indigenous languages by supporting the efforts of Indigenous Peoples across Canada to reclaim, revitalize, maintain, and strengthen their languages.

Our national team is passionate about our work, and the difference we make with the research, resources and innovation we develop collaboratively with partners and share with Indigenous communities. We have policies in place to ensure a welcoming, safe and respectful workplace, as well as rigorous standards for transparency and accountability.

Our Vision: All Indigenous languages in Canada are safe, vibrant, and thriving.

Our Guiding Principles

  1. There is an urgent need for concerted efforts and investments toward the revitalization of Indigenous languages to arrest and reverse the erosion that has already occurred. Research shows that no Indigenous language in Canada is safe and that all are in varying stages of endangerment.
  2. Indigenous languages are fundamental to the identities, cultures, spirituality, relationships to the land, worldviews, and self-determination of Indigenous peoples.
  3. Indigenous languages have and continue to contribute to the strength of Canada as a whole, including biodiversity and the richness of linguistic and cultural heritage. The Commission is committed to protecting the vitality of all Indigenous languages, including sign languages and sleeping languages.

We welcome interest by qualified candidates as we expand our national team to launch new, exciting projects and to meet growing organizational needs.



About the Role

The Knowledge Hub Coordinator is responsible for identifying, collecting, organizing, maintaining, and promoting Indigenous language resources, research, tools, and promising practices from across Canada and internationally. The position supports the development of a comprehensive and accessible national repository of Indigenous language knowledge, ensuring that communities, educators, researchers, and organizations can access high-quality information to support language revitalization efforts.

The Coordinator will work collaboratively with Indigenous communities, language organizations, researchers, governments, and partners to compile resources, maintain knowledge inventories, support resource development, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

Key Responsibilities

Resource Development and Management



  • Identify, collect, and compile Indigenous language resources, tools, research, reports, and best practices.
  • Maintain a national inventory of Indigenous language programs, initiatives, organizations, and services.
  • Organize and catalogue resources using established information management standards.
  • Develop and maintain searchable databases, repositories, and knowledge libraries.
  • Ensure resources remain current, accurate, and accessible.

Knowledge Collection and Environmental Scanning

  • Conduct ongoing environmental scans of Indigenous language revitalization initiatives, research, technologies, funding programs, and educational resources.
  • Monitor emerging trends, innovations, policies, and practices relevant to Indigenous languages.
  • Identify gaps in resources and recommend priorities for future development.
  • Prepare summaries, inventories, and resource collections on priority topics.

Knowledge Mobilization

  • Develop resource guides, toolkits, directories, and curated collections.
  • Prepare plain-language summaries of research and technical materials.
  • Support dissemination of resources through digital platforms, newsletters, webinars, and events.
  • Assist in translating research findings into practical tools for communities and language practitioners.

Community and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build relationships with Indigenous communities, language authorities, academic institutions, and partner organizations.
  • Coordinate requests for information, resources, and research materials.
  • Support collaboration and information-sharing initiatives.
  • Facilitate contributions to the Knowledge Hub repository from external partners.

Information and Records Management

  • Maintain records, metadata, and resource documentation.
  • Ensure information is organized according to established governance and accessibility standards.
  • Support quality assurance and content review processes.
  • Track usage, downloads, and resource engagement metrics.

Reporting and Administration

  • Prepare briefing notes, inventories, status reports, and dashboards.
  • Track resource development activities and project deliverables
  • Support Knowledge Hub planning, reporting, and evaluation activities.
  • Contribute to annual work plans and organizational reporting requirements.
  • Assist with review committee logistics, RFP development, and review of print and digital material.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Degree or diploma in Library and Information Studies, Information Management, Indigenous Studies, Communications, Social Sciences, Education, Public Administration, or a related discipline.
  • Experience working with Indigenous communities, organizations, governments, or research environments is considered an asset.
  • Equivalent combination of education lived experience, and professional experience will be considered.

Knowledge Skills and Competencies

  • Knowledge of Indigenous language revitalization initiatives and organizations.
  • Understanding of knowledge management and information-sharing practices.
  • Familiarity with Indigenous data sovereignty principles.
  • Knowledge of digital repositories, content management systems, and resource libraries.
  • Strong research and analytical skills.
  • Excellent organizational and information management abilities.
  • Strong writing, editing, and summarization skills.
  • Ability to synthesize large volumes of information into practical resources.
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft 365, SharePoint, databases, and knowledge management tools

Assets

  • Experience working with Indigenous organizations, communities, or research initiatives
  • Knowledge of one or more Indigenous languages.
  • Proficiency in an Indigenous language and bilingualism (English/French).



What We Offer

The Commission offers a competitive benefits package, including medical and dental benefits and a pension plan, two weeks paid holidays to begin, plus additional paid days off through the year, including federal and provincial holidays. The Commission offers a wonderful, supportive work environment, with opportunities for career development, mentorship, and professional development.

The Commission recognizes that our success requires us to have a workforce that reflects the community we serve, and diversity in its widest context, one where all people, regardless of difference, are valued and respected.

Preference will be given to Indigenous applicants in accordance with section 16(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act. Candidates are encouraged to self-identify in their cover letter.




À propos du Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones (OCIL)


Le Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones s'engage à promouvoir et défendre les langues autochtones en soutenant les efforts des peuples autochtones à travers le Canada pour reconquérir, revitaliser, maintenir et renforcer leurs langues.

Notre équipe nationale est passionnée par notre travail et par la différence que nous faisons grâce à la recherche, aux ressources et à l'innovation que nous développons en collaboration avec des partenaires et que nous partageons avec les communautés autochtones. Nous avons mis en place des politiques pour garantir un milieu de travail accueillant, sécuritaire et respectueux, ainsi que des normes rigoureuses de transparence et de responsabilité.

Notre vision : Toutes les langues autochtones au Canada sont sécuritaires, vibrantes et florissantes.

Nos principes directeurs

  1. Il est urgent d'efforts concertés et d'investissements pour la revitalisation des langues autochtones afin d'arrêter et d'inverser l'érosion déjà survenue. Les recherches démontrent qu'aucune langue autochtone au Canada n'est sécuritaire et que toutes sont à différents stades de danger.
  2. Les langues autochtones sont fondamentales pour les identités, les cultures, la spiritualité, les relations avec la terre, les visions du monde et l'autodétermination des peuples autochtones.
  3. Les langues autochtones ont contribué et continuent de contribuer à la force du Canada dans son ensemble, y compris la biodiversité et la richesse du patrimoine linguistique et culturel. La Commission s'engage à protéger la vitalité de toutes les langues autochtones, y compris les langues des signes et les langues du sommeil.

Nous accueillons l'intérêt des candidats qualifiés alors que nous élargissons notre équipe nationale pour lancer de nouveaux projets passionnants et répondre aux besoins organisationnels croissants.

À propos du rôle

Le coordonnateur du Knowledge Hub est responsable de l'identification, de la collecte, de l'organisation, du maintien et de la promotion des ressources, recherches, outils et pratiques prometteuses en langues autochtones, provenant de partout au Canada et à l'international. Le poste soutient le développement d'un dépôt national complet et accessible des connaissances linguistiques autochtones, assurant que les communautés, éducateurs, chercheurs et organisations puissent accéder à une information de haute qualité pour soutenir les efforts de revitalisation linguistique.

Le coordonnateur travaillera en collaboration avec les communautés autochtones, les organisations linguistiques, les chercheurs, les gouvernements et les partenaires pour compiler des ressources, maintenir des inventaires de connaissances, soutenir le développement des ressources et faciliter le partage des connaissances.

Responsabilités clés

Développement et gestion des ressources



  • Identifier, collecter et compiler des ressources, outils, recherches, rapports et meilleures pratiques en langues autochtones.
  • Maintenir un inventaire national des programmes, initiatives, organisations et services en langues autochtones.
  • Organiser et cataloguer les ressources selon les normes établies de gestion de l'information.
  • Développer et maintenir des bases de données, des dépôts et des bibliothèques de connaissances consultables.
  • Assurez-vous que les ressources demeurent à jour, précises et accessibles.

Collecte de connaissances et analyse environnementale

  • Effectuer des analyses environnementales continues des initiatives de revitalisation des langues autochtones, de la recherche, des technologies, des programmes de financement et des ressources éducatives.
  • Surveillez les tendances émergentes, les innovations, les politiques et les pratiques pertinentes aux langues autochtones.
  • Identifier les lacunes dans les ressources et recommander des priorités pour le développement futur.
  • Préparez des résumés, des inventaires et des collections de ressources sur les sujets prioritaires.

Mobilisation des connaissances

  • Développer des guides de ressources, des trousses à outils, des annuaires et des collections sélectionnées.
  • Préparez des résumés en langage clair des documents de recherche et techniques.
  • Soutenir la diffusion des ressources par le biais de plateformes numériques, d'infolettres, de webinaires et d'événements.
  • Aider à traduire les résultats de la recherche en outils pratiques pour les communautés et les praticiens du langage.

Engagement communautaire et des parties prenantes

  • Bâtir des relations avec les communautés autochtones, les autorités linguistiques, les institutions académiques et les organisations partenaires.
  • Coordonnez les demandes d'informations, de ressources et de documents de recherche.
  • Soutenez la collaboration et les initiatives de partage d'informations.
  • Faciliter les contributions de partenaires externes au dépôt du Knowledge Hub.

Gestion de l'information et des archives

  • Maintenez les dossiers, les métadonnées et la documentation des ressources.
  • Assurez-vous que l'information est organisée selon les normes établies de gouvernance et d'accessibilité.
  • Soutenir les processus d'assurance qualité et d'évaluation de contenu.
  • Suivez l'utilisation, les téléchargements et les indicateurs d'engagement des ressources.

Rapports et administration

  • Préparez des notes d'information, des inventaires, des rapports d'état d'état et des tableaux de bord.
  • Suivre les activités de développement des ressources et les livrables des projets
  • Soutenez les activités de planification, de rapports et d'évaluation du Knowledge Hub.
  • Contribuer aux plans de travail annuels et aux exigences de rapport organisationnel.
  • Aider à la logistique du comité d'examen, au développement de la demande de propositions et à la révision du matériel imprimé et numérique.

Qualifications

Éducation et expérience

  • Diplôme ou diplôme en bibliothéconomie et sciences de l'information, gestion de l'information, études autochtones, communications, sciences sociales, éducation, administration publique ou discipline connexe.
  • L'expérience de travail avec les communautés, organisations, gouvernements ou environnements de recherche autochtones est considérée comme un atout.
  • Une combinaison équivalente d'éducation, d'expérience vécue et d'expérience professionnelle sera prise en compte.

Connaissances et compétences

  • Connaissance des initiatives et organisations de revitalisation des langues autochtones.
  • Compréhension de la gestion des connaissances et des pratiques de partage de l'information.
  • Familiarité avec les principes de souveraineté des données autochtones.
  • Connaissance des dépôts numériques, des systèmes de gestion de contenu et des bibliothèques de ressources.
  • Solides compétences en recherche et en analyse.
  • Excellentes compétences organisationnelles et en gestion de l'information.
  • Solides compétences en rédaction, révision et synthèse.
  • Capacité à synthétiser de grands volumes d'informations en ressources pratiques.
  • Solides compétences en création de relations et en engagement des parties prenantes.
  • Maîtrise de Microsoft 365, SharePoint, des bases de données et des outils de gestion des connaissances

Actifs

  • Expérience de travail avec des organisations autochtones, des communautés ou des initiatives de recherche
  • Connaissance d'une ou plusieurs langues autochtones.
  • Maîtrise d'une langue autochtone et bilinguisme (anglais/français).

Ce que nous offrons

La Commission offre un ensemble d'avantages sociaux compétitif, incluant des prestations médicales et dentaires ainsi qu'un régime de pension, deux semaines de congés payés pour commencer, ainsi que des jours de congé payés supplémentaires au cours de l'année, y compris les jours fériés fédéraux et provinciaux. La Commission offre un environnement de travail merveilleux et bienveillant, avec des occasions de développement de carrière, de mentorat et de développement professionnel.

La Commission reconnaît que notre succès exige que nous ayons une main-d'œuvre qui reflète la communauté que nous servons, et la diversité dans son contexte le plus large, où toutes les personnes, peu importe leurs différences, sont valorisées et respectées.

La préférence sera accordée aux demandeurs autochtones conformément à l'article 16(1) de la Loi canadienne sur les droits de la personne. Les candidats sont encouragés à s'identifier dans leur lettre de motivation.

title: Information Management Officer - Agent de gestion de l'information
description:
About the Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages (OCIL)


The Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages is dedicated to promoting and championing Indigenous languages by supporting the efforts of Indigenous Peoples across Canada to reclaim, revitalize, maintain, and strengthen their languages.

Our national team is passionate about our work, and the difference we make with the research, resources and innovation we develop collaboratively with partners and share with Indigenous communities. We have policies in place to ensure a welcoming, safe and respectful workplace, as well as rigorous standards for transparency and accountability.

Our Vision: All Indigenous languages in Canada are safe, vibrant, and thriving.

Our Guiding Principles

  1. There is an urgent need for concerted efforts and investments toward the revitalization of Indigenous languages to arrest and reverse the erosion that has already occurred. Research shows that no Indigenous language in Canada is safe and that all are in varying stages of endangerment.
  2. Indigenous languages are fundamental to the identities, cultures, spirituality, relationships to the land, worldviews, and self-determination of Indigenous peoples.
  3. Indigenous languages have and continue to contribute to the strength of Canada as a whole, including biodiversity and the richness of linguistic and cultural heritage. The Commission is committed to protecting the vitality of all Indigenous languages, including sign languages and sleeping languages.

We welcome interest from qualified candidates as we expand our national team to launch new, exciting projects and to meet growing organizational needs.



About the Role

The Information Management Officer (IMO) is responsible for the governance, organization, protection, and lifecycle management of the organization's information assets — both physical and electronic. Working closely with the IMIT Lead, the IMO develops and maintains recordkeeping standards, data structures, and classification systems; safeguards information repositories; and advises staff and management on information management best practices and compliance obligations.

Key Responsibilities

Cloud Data Governance & Protection

  • Ensure cloud-stored data is properly organized, tagged, and easily retrievable — including labeling/classification work done in conjunction with the IMIT Lead (e.g., Microsoft Purview) as well as manual tagging by staff.
  • Train staff on manual data tagging and classification practices to keep information consistently protected.
  • Support Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies through proper classification, tagging, and handling of data.

Policy, Procedure & Documentation

  • Review, and maintain information management policies, procedures, and documentation; provide recommendations and assist in development of new processes as gaps are identified.
  • Draft and maintain Information Management Administrative Instructions and related documentation.
  • Maintain file plans and classification structures and catalogue records accordingly.

Storage, Archiving & Disposal

  • Assist with storage requirements, archival, and destruction/disposal of records, both electronic and physical.
  • Recommend and implement improvements to storage, retrieval, archiving, and disposal processes, coordinating with the IMIT Lead on infrastructure needs.

Compliance, Security & Continuity

  • Collaborate with the IMIT Lead to safeguard information repositories and support information security systems.
  • Monitor and audit information management practices for compliance; coordinate responses to information requests and data breaches.
  • Identify and manage essential records within emergency preparedness and business continuity frameworks.
  • Stay up to date on new legislative requirements.

Stakeholder Support & Program Improvement

  • Support other departments' document and records management needs and advise staff and leadership on IM best practices.
  • Identify content management issues and recommend process improvements; report on the effectiveness of IM programs and standards.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Diploma or degree in Information Management, Records Management, Library and Information Science, Archival Studies, Computer Science, or a related field — or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 2+ years of experience in records management, information management, or a related discipline; experience in a Canadian regulatory environment is an asset.
  • Experience developing or maintaining file plans, classification schemes, or retention/disposal schedules.
  • Experience working with electronic document and records management systems (EDRMS), such as SharePoint/OneDrive or a comparable platform.

Knowledge and Expertise

  • Understanding of the records lifecycle, creation, active use, retention, and archival/disposal, and how file plans and classification structures support it
  • General literacy in what constitutes personal or sensitive information and how it should be handled
  • Understanding of data classification and tagging concepts, including why tagging accuracy matters for tools like DLP and Microsoft Purview
  • Ability to identify essential records and what needs to remain accessible through a disruption
  • Ability to translate written policy into practical guidance
  • Legislative requirements

Skills and Competencies

  • Strong analytical and organizational skills, with meticulous attention to detail.
  • Clear written and verbal communication; able to explain information management concepts to non-technical staff.
  • Comfortable working independently and collaboratively with the IMIT Lead and other departments.
  • Sound judgment in handling sensitive, confidential, or personal information.
  • Adaptable to new systems and evolving information management technologies.

Assets

  • Certified Records Manager (CRM), Information Management Professional (IMP/IIM), Certified Information Professional (CIP), or Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP)
  • Rough working understanding of Microsoft Purview (or similar data governance/classification platforms)

What We Offer

The Commission offers a competitive benefits package, including medical and dental benefits and a pension plan, two weeks paid holidays to begin, plus additional paid days off through the year, including federal and provincial holidays. The Commission offers a wonderful, supportive work environment, with opportunities for career development, mentorship, and professional development.

The Commission recognizes that our success requires us to have a workforce that reflects the community we serve, and diversity in its widest context, one where all people, regardless of difference, are valued and respected.

Preference will be given to Indigenous applicants in accordance with section 16(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act. Candidates are encouraged to self-identify in their cover letter.



À propos du Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones (OCIL)


Le Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones s'engage à promouvoir et défendre les langues autochtones en soutenant les efforts des peuples autochtones à travers le Canada pour reconquérir, revitaliser, maintenir et renforcer leurs langues.

Notre équipe nationale est passionnée par notre travail et par la différence que nous faisons grâce à la recherche, aux ressources et à l'innovation que nous développons en collaboration avec des partenaires et partageons avec les communautés autochtones. Nous avons mis en place des politiques pour assurer un milieu de travail accueillant, sécuritaire et respectueux, ainsi que des normes rigoureuses de transparence et de responsabilité.

Notre vision : Toutes les langues autochtones au Canada sont sécuritaires, vibrantes et florissantes.

Nos principes directeurs

  1. Il est urgent de déployer des efforts et des investissements concertés pour la revitalisation des langues autochtones afin d'arrêter et d'inverser l'érosion déjà survenue. La recherche démontre qu'aucune langue autochtone au Canada n'est sécuritaire et que toutes sont à différents stades de danger.
  2. Les langues autochtones sont fondamentales pour les identités, les cultures, la spiritualité, les relations avec la terre, les visions du monde et l'autodétermination des peuples autochtones.
  3. Les langues autochtones ont contribué et continuent de contribuer à la force du Canada dans son ensemble, y compris la biodiversité et la richesse du patrimoine linguistique et culturel. La Commission s'engage à protéger la vitalité de toutes les langues autochtones, y compris les langues des signes et les langues du sommeil.

Nous accueillons l'intérêt des candidats qualifiés alors que nous élargissons notre équipe nationale pour lancer de nouveaux projets passionnants et répondre aux besoins organisationnels croissants.



À propos du rôle

L'agent de gestion de l'information (OMI) est responsable de la gouvernance, de l'organisation, de la protection et de la gestion du cycle de vie des actifs d'information de l'organisation — tant physiques qu'électroniques. En collaboration étroite avec le chef de l'IMIT, l'OMI élabore et maintient les normes de tenue de dossiers, les structures de données et les systèmes de classification; protège les dépôts d'information; et conseille le personnel et la direction sur les meilleures pratiques en gestion de l'information et les obligations de conformité.

Responsabilités clés

Gouvernance et protection des données cloud

  • Assurez-vous que les données stockées dans le nuage sont bien organisées, étiquetées et facilement accessibles — y compris le travail d'étiquetage et de classification effectué en collaboration avec le responsable de l'IMIT (par exemple, Microsoft Purview) ainsi que le taguage manuel par le personnel.
  • Former le personnel aux pratiques manuelles d'étiquetage des données et de classification afin de garder l'information constamment protégée.
  • Soutenir les politiques de prévention de la perte de données (DLP) grâce à une classification, un étiquetage et une gestion appropriés des données.

Politique, procédures et documentation

  • Examiner et maintenir les politiques, procédures et documentation de gestion de l'information; fournir des recommandations et aider au développement de nouveaux processus au fur et à mesure que des lacunes sont identifiées.
  • Rédiger et maintenir les instructions administratives de gestion de l'information et la documentation associée.
  • Maintenir les plans de dossiers et les structures de classification et cataloguer les dossiers en conséquence.

Entreposage, archivage et élimination

  • Assister aux besoins de stockage, à l'archivage et à la destruction/élimination des documents, tant électroniques que physiques.
  • Recommander et mettre en œuvre des améliorations aux processus de stockage, de récupération, d'archivage et d'élimination, en coordonnant avec le responsable de l'IMIT sur les besoins en infrastructure.

Conformité, sécurité et continuité

  • Collaborer avec le responsable de l'IMIT pour protéger les dépôts d'information et soutenir les systèmes de sécurité de l'information.
  • Surveiller et auditer les pratiques de gestion de l'information pour la conformité; coordonner les réponses aux demandes d'information et aux violations de données.
  • Identifier et gérer les dossiers essentiels dans les cadres de préparation aux situations d'urgence et de continuité des activités.
  • Restez à jour sur les nouvelles exigences législatives.

Soutien aux parties prenantes et amélioration des programmes

  • Soutenir les besoins en gestion documentaire et documentaire des autres départements et conseiller le personnel et la direction sur les meilleures pratiques en gestion de la médecine instantanée.
  • Identifier les enjeux de gestion du contenu et recommander des améliorations des processus; faire un rapport sur l'efficacité des programmes et normes de MI.

Qualifications

Éducation et expérience

  • Diplôme ou diplôme en gestion de l'information, gestion des documents, bibliothéconomie et sciences de l'information, études archivistiques, informatique, ou un domaine connexe — ou une combinaison équivalente de formation et d'expérience.
  • 2+ ans d'expérience en gestion de documents, gestion de l'information ou discipline connexe; expérience dans un environnement réglementaire canadien est un atout.
  • Expérience dans l'élaboration ou la tenue de plans de dossiers, de schémas de classification ou de calendriers de rétention/élimination.
  • Expérience de travail avec des systèmes électroniques de gestion de documents et d'enregistrements (EDRMS), tels que SharePoint/OneDrive ou une plateforme comparable.

Connaissances et expertise

  • Compréhension du cycle de vie des enregistrements, de la création, de l'utilisation active, de la conservation et de l'archivage/élimination, ainsi que de la manière dont les plans de fichiers et les structures de classification les soutiennent
  • L'alphabétisation générale sur ce qui constitue une information personnelle ou sensible et la façon dont elle doit être traitée
  • Compréhension des concepts de classification des données et d'étiquetage, y compris pourquoi la précision du balisage est importante pour des outils comme DLP et Microsoft Purview
  • Capacité à identifier les documents essentiels et ce qui doit rester accessible en cas de perturbation
  • Capacité à traduire la politique écrite en directives pratiques
  • Exigences législatives

Compétences et aptitudes

  • Solides compétences analytiques et organisationnelles, avec une attention méticuleuse aux détails.
  • Communication écrite et orale claire; capacité à expliquer les concepts de gestion de l'information au personnel non technique.
  • À l'aise de travailler de façon autonome et collaborative avec le responsable de l'IMIT et d'autres départements.
  • Faites preuve de bon jugement dans la gestion des renseignements sensibles, confidentiels ou personnels.
  • Adaptable aux nouveaux systèmes et aux technologies de gestion de l'information en évolution.

Actifs

  • gestionnaire certifié des dossiers (CRM), professionnel en gestion de l'information (IMP/IIM), professionnel certifié en information (CIP) ou professionnel certifié en gestion des données (CDMP)
  • Compréhension générale de Microsoft Purview (ou de plateformes similaires de gouvernance/classification des données)



Ce que nous offrons

La Commission offre un ensemble d'avantages compétitifs, incluant des prestations médicales et dentaires ainsi qu'un régime de retraite, deux semaines de congés payés pour commencer, plus des congés payés supplémentaires au cours de l'année, y compris les jours fériés fédéraux et provinciaux. La Commission offre un environnement de travail formidable et bienveillant, avec des occasions de développement de carrière, de mentorat et de développement professionnel.

La Commission reconnaît que notre succès exige que nous ayons une main-d'œuvre qui reflète la communauté que nous servons, et la diversité dans son contexte le plus large, où toutes les personnes, peu importe leurs différences, sont valorisées et respectées.

La préférence sera accordée aux demandeurs autochtones conformément à l'article 16(1) de la Loi canadienne sur les droits de la personne. Les candidats sont encouragés à s'identifier dans leur lettre de motivation.

title: Instructor General Application
description:
About Mission Bit

Mission Bit is a San Francisco-based nonprofit that equips youth with hands-on computer science and AI education that builds confidence, technical skills, and pathways to meaningful careers in technology. We serve public high school students who've historically had limited access to tech and tech careers through semester-long coding courses, self-paced learning, workshops, and more.

Overview

Every semester, Mission Bit seeks talented and passionate instructors to mentor, support, and uplift the next generation — empowering youth through hands-on computer science education. We have three student-facing instructional roles: In-school Instructor, Lead Instructor, and Teaching Assistant (TA). All roles are highly visible, work directly with students, and are essential to delivering Mission Bit's project-based computer science curriculum.

Our instructors teach a variety of introductory coding courses: Web Design (HTML/CSS, UI/UX Design), Game Design (Unity/C#), VR (Meta Quest/Unity/C#), Python, and AI. We're proud to provide training to all instructional staff before the semester begins, along with ongoing support throughout the course. If you have a passion for community, social justice, education, and coding, and want to uplift high school youth and bridge the tech divide, this might be the opportunity for you!

By completing this general application, our team will reach out with opportunities that align with your experience and interests.

Hiring Cycles

This is a general application. We review applications and match candidates to open positions across three hiring cycles per year:

  1. Spring cycle: October - January
  2. Summer cycle: February - June
  3. Fall cycle: July - August

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis within each hiring cycle listed above, and our team will follow up if there's a match to a role.

Roles and responsibilities

All roles work with high school students ages 14–18.

In-school Instructor:

  • Create an inclusive, community-based classroom culture rooted in Mission Bit's core values of social justice, community, accountability, smart risks, and love
  • Prepare and facilitate 4 lessons per week using Mission Bit's in-house project-based curriculum at partner school site
  • Foster individual and meaningful relationships with students, adjust lessons to meet their learning needs, and grade student assessments throughout the school year
  • Plan and lead engaging community-building games and activities
  • Effectively manage classroom behavior and routines to maintain a safe, productive learning environment for all students throughout the day
  • Collaborate closely with the partner school's teacher of record and other instructional staff, attend weekly staff meetings, and help suggest and implement ideas that improve the quality of Mission Bit's curriculum and program
  • Keep students, families, Program Staff, and the Education Program Manager informed on course and student progress throughout the school year

Lead Instructor:

  • Create an inclusive, community-based classroom culture rooted in Mission Bit's core values of social justice, community, accountability, smart risks, and love
  • Prepare and facilitate 2-3 lessons per week using Mission Bit's in-house project-based curriculum, adjusting to meet the needs of a diverse group of learners
  • Foster individual and meaningful relationships with students, and guide them toward building a final project they can proudly showcase at Demo Day
  • Collaborate closely with your TA and other instructional staff, attend weekly staff meetings, and help suggest and implement ideas that improve the quality of Mission Bit's curriculum and program
  • Keep students, families, and Program Staff informed on course and student progress throughout the semester

Teaching Assistant (TA):

  • Create an inclusive, community-based classroom culture rooted in Mission Bit's core values of social justice, community, accountability, smart risks, and love
  • Plan and lead engaging community-building games and activities
  • Foster individual and meaningful relationships with students, promote positive and productive collaboration between them, and effectively manage classroom behavior to support a productive learning environment
  • Ensure students receive the support they need to confidently showcase a capstone project at Demo Day, and step in to lead class when the Lead Instructor is out
  • Collaborate with the Lead Instructor and other instructional staff, attend weekly staff meetings, and keep students, families, and Program Staff informed on progress

Schedule

Both roles are seasonal and part-time, generally following the academic semester tied to each hiring cycle above. Specific weekly hours, class days/times, training dates, and site locations vary by cohort and will be confirmed with matched candidates once classes are identified.

title: Marketing Design Lead
description:
Brand and marketing design · Remote (India) · Full-time · 6 to 8 years of experience

Why this role

Firstwork is judged on how it looks the moment it reaches someone. A deck in a meeting with a senior client. A one-pager forwarded to a decision maker. The website an investor opens before a call. In each of these moments, the work has to match the quality of the company behind it, and that standard needs an owner.

That is this role. You lead marketing design at Firstwork and own the visual standard of everything the company puts in front of the market. It is a brand and marketing role, not a product design one, and it is hands-on. You lead the standard by producing the work yourself, not by directing others, and you work closely with the founders and the marketing team, with the room to take your own calls and hold the line on quality without being asked.

What you'll do

You lead marketing design at Firstwork and own the full surface, end to end.

  • Presentations and enablement. Much of our business runs through decks: sales, partnerships, and investment. Alongside them, the one-pagers, case studies, and product materials the team uses to win and keep business, and this is where craft is noticed first

  • Our website runs on Webflow, and you design and extend it as we grow, keeping the identity consistent across new pages and campaigns

  • Events and campaigns. The look and the materials for the moments where our work meets the market, in person and online

  • Motion and video. Product explainers, short films, and social content, where motion is used to make something clearer, not for its own sake

  • Brand consistency. You keep the identity coherent across every surface, and you evolve it with care rather than diluting it

  • The standard. You are the reason the quality of everything we publish rises and stays high

What we're looking for

  • A hands-on foundation in graphic design and, ideally, illustration, so you produce the finished work yourself and do not depend on someone else to turn your ideas into the final output

  • Production range. You can take a piece from idea to finished output across presentation, print, digital and motion, without a drop in quality

  • A strong command of typography, layout, color and hierarchy. You build and hold a visual system rather than simply decorate

  • An editorial, considered sensibility, comfortable in a direction that sits closer to art and print than to typical software design

  • A clear point of view you can defend, taking direction from good judgment rather than ego

  • Dependable and fast, including against fixed deadlines, with nothing unfinished or careless leaving your desk

  • Open to feedback, giving and taking it honestly in service of the work

  • Fluency with the modern design stack. Figma at the center, with the motion and web tools the work needs, and we will ask to see how you work

If you have wanted to own the full visual standard of a company that genuinely cares about craft, with a portfolio of finished, published work that speaks for itself, and you already hold that bar yourself, this is that role.

How to apply

To apply, share your portfolio and your LinkedIn. We review both carefully, and if there is a fit we will reach out for a phone call.

From there, expect two to three rounds, including a brief assignment and first conversations with the team. We would like to see your work.

Firstwork is an equal opportunity employer. We evaluate applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or any other protected status.

title: Special Event Security Cross Train 2026-034
description:
THE OPPORTUNITY AWAITS YOU

REAL finds itself in the enviable position of managing one of the most interesting and versatile connected spaces in North America with an opportunity to impact the lives of millions by creating life-long memories and delivering exceptional experiences.

Special Event Security (SES) are responsible for delivering safe, secure and regulatory compliant venues for daily operations and event-based activities held on the REAL District.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

1. Protect and secure staff and patrons visiting the REAL District by:

  • Communicating and enforcing adherence to the policy, procedure, rules and codes of conduct governing the use of REAL District property.
  • Responding to incidents of disruptive behavior within venues and taking measures to resolve the issue.
  • Verbally briefing supervisors on the circumstances of ongoing incidents.
  • Notifying the Command Centre for activation of first responders in the event of an emergency.

2. Protect and secure the physical assets of REAL and clients by:

  • Patrolling buildings to guard against unauthorized access.
  • Ensuring access points are appropriately secured.
  • Providing cash escorts when required.

3. Assists with crowd management at events by:

  • Verbally communicating venue and event specific policy and procedure to patrons.
  • Screening patrons during ingress through the use of physical bag searches and technological aids.
  • Controlling access to restricted areas.
  • Proactively monitoring crowds for disturbances and taking measures to resolve issues.

4. Enforces regulatory compliance around alcohol service by:

  • Ensuring venues remain secure from alcohol purchased outside of REAL district property.
  • Ensuring alcohol served on the REAL District is consumed within designated licensed areas.
  • Ensuring alcohol service outlets abide by the internal rules governing limits on the number of alcoholic beverages served at each visit.
  • Checking the age of suspected minors in possession of alcohol through verification of government issued photo identification and confiscating alcohol from those not verified as of legal age.

5. Documenting reportable incidents through note taking and report writing.

Performs other duties on an as needed and when required basis.

Requirements

WHAT IT TAKES

Apply today if you meet the following requirements:

Education and Experience

  • Must be at least nineteen (19) years of age.
  • Grade twelve (12) education or GED equivalent is required.
  • Valid security guard license and Serve-It-Right (SIRs) certification preferred.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Formal training and/or work experience in the field of security.
  • Demonstrated experience in customer service.
  • Excellent critical thinking and decision making skills.
  • Excellent communication skills (written and oral).

title: Generator Technician II - McCloud Power Station
description:
We are ERock!

ERock (NYSE: EROC) is enabling energy for a new era. ERock delivers onsite utility-grade power that gets customers up and running quickly, while supporting long-term grid development. ERock’s proprietary natural gas generators help critical facilities address grid constraints, interconnection delays, and outage risks while accelerating speed-to-power for new and expanding operations. Trusted by data centers, utilities, manufacturers, healthcare systems and government organizations, ERock engineers for rapid deployment, long-duration reliability, low local emissions, and scalable performance to meet the evolving energy demands of today and tomorrow.


Position Overview:

We are seeking a safety-focused, skilled, and dependable Power Generation Technician 2 to support operations and maintenance activities at ERock’s McCloud Power Station in El Paso, Texas. This position performs preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, and repair activities on modular natural gas generation equipment and associated microgrid systems at a single assigned site.


This role is designed as a stable, site-based position supporting McCloud Station’s high-density modular generation environment. Technicians work within established procedures, standardized maintenance practices, and defined safety requirements while applying intermediate mechanical, electrical, and troubleshooting skills to help maintain reliable, efficient, and compliant operation of assigned generation assets.


The Power Generation Technician 2 supports site reliability by independently completing routine maintenance work, assisting with more advanced repairs, documenting equipment condition, escalating abnormal findings, and partnering with senior technicians, operations, and supervision as needed. This role requires demonstrated technical capability, strong safety performance, sound judgment, and the ability to work with limited day-to-day direction within defined procedures.


This role reports to a Power Generation Group Supervisor at McCloud Station.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Performing preventive maintenance and corrective mechanical tasks on modular natural gas generation equipment in accordance with established procedures and safety requirements.
  • Troubleshooting and repairing mechanical, electrical, controls, and auxiliary equipment issues within defined Technician 2 scope.
  • Completing scheduled inspections and rounds to identify equipment conditions, maintenance needs, leaks, alarms, or potential issues requiring escalation.
  • Supporting equipment availability by completing maintenance activities on time, to standard, and within assigned work scope.
  • Accurately documenting completed work, inspections, findings, parts usage, and follow-up needs using company maintenance systems, shift logs, and required site records.
  • Adhering to all safety requirements, including PPE usage, lockout/tagout (LOTO), dead checks, environmental controls, spill prevention, and site-specific work practices.
  • Maintaining a clean, organized, and professional work area within the assigned McCloud Station work scope.
  • Communicating equipment conditions, abnormal findings, work status, and support needs clearly to supervisors, senior technicians, and operations personnel.
  • Supporting senior technicians, regional resources, or subject matter experts during advanced maintenance, troubleshooting, commissioning support, or repair activities when required.
  • Providing informal support, guidance, and work-task reinforcement to Technician 1 employees or less experienced team members when assigned.
  • Performing additional McCloud Station support tasks as assigned, within the defined scope of the role.
  • Other responsibilities as directed by supervisor.

title: CRM & Customer Insights Consultant
location: Reggio Emilia, Province of Reggio Emilia, Italy
description:
Siamo alla ricerca di una persona per il ruolo di CRM & Customer Insights Consultant, da inserire nel team dedicato ai progetti CRM e Direct Marketing.

Cerchiamo una persona capace di leggere insieme dati CRM, ecommerce e digital analytics, trasformandoli in segmenti, insight e iniziative concrete. Il ruolo unisce capacità analitiche, conoscenza del customer lifecycle e attitudine consulenziale.

RUOLO

Come CRM & Customer Insights Consultant lavorerai a stretto contatto con clienti e team interni per comprendere comportamenti, bisogni e opportunità lungo il customer journey.

Il tuo lavoro partirà spesso da domande di business concrete, come:

  • Quali clienti stanno riducendo la frequenza o il valore degli acquisti e come possiamo attivarli?
  • Quali segmenti presentano il maggiore potenziale di retention, cross-sell o crescita?
  • Quali comportamenti distinguono i clienti occasionali da quelli ad alto valore?
  • In quali punti del funnel perdiamo più utenti e quali audience dovremmo approfondire?
  • Come possiamo utilizzare meglio i dati first-party nelle attività CRM, Marketing Automation e media?
  • I dati disponibili sono sufficientemente completi e affidabili per prendere una decisione?

Per rispondere a queste domande analizzerai dati provenienti da CRM, ecommerce, campagne e digital analytics, trasformando le evidenze raccolte in segmenti, insight e iniziative concrete.

Gestirai in autonomia il tuo workstream, dalla definizione delle domande di analisi alla presentazione dei risultati, coordinandoti con Marketing Automation Specialist, MarTech Specialist, Digital Analyst e le altre competenze coinvolte nel progetto.

Utilizzerai abitualmente strumenti di Intelligenza Artificiale per accelerare l’esplorazione dei dati, la scrittura e il controllo delle query, la documentazione delle analisi e la preparazione dei deliverable. Sarai sempre responsabile della verifica, della correttezza e della qualità del risultato finale.

In particolare, potresti occuparti di:

  • Analizzare congiuntamente dati CRM, ordini, campagne e comportamento onsite, utilizzando anche Google Analytics 4 o Adobe Analytics;
  • Verificare qualità e coerenza dei dati, individuando anomalie, limiti e informazioni mancanti;
  • Sviluppare segmentazioni e analisi legate a lifecycle, retention, riattivazione, cross-sell e customer value;
  • Analizzare funnel, eventi, conversioni e audience, confrontandoti con gli specialisti tecnici quando sono necessari approfondimenti sul tracking;
  • Trasformare le evidenze raccolte in insight, use case, priorità e requisiti per attività di Marketing Automation, MarTech e media;
  • Utilizzare strumenti AI per esplorare ipotesi, produrre o controllare query SQL, sintetizzare risultati e preparare presentazioni;
  • Condurre meeting, workshop e presentazioni, spiegando in modo comprensibile risultati, implicazioni e limiti delle analisi;
  • Gestire attività, dipendenze, scadenze e stakeholder delle progettualità assegnate, garantendo la qualità degli output;
  • Collaborare con i team specialistici per trasformare gli insight in iniziative concretamente attivabili.

Requirements

Sei la persona che stiamo cercando se hai:

  • Familiarità con piattaforme come Klaviyo, Salesforce, Salesforce Marketing Cloud o soluzioni equivalenti;
  • Esperienza concreta in ambito CRM, customer analytics, ecommerce o consulenza data-driven;
  • Buona conoscenza di segmentazione, customer lifecycle e customer journey;
  • Capacità di ragionare con metodo su popolazioni, join, denominatori, periodi di confronto e qualità dei dati;
  • Conoscenza operativa di Google Analytics 4 e la capacità di interpretare funnel, eventi, conversioni e audience;
  • Familiarità con l’analisi di dati provenienti da fonti differenti, anche quando incompleti o non perfettamente allineati;
  • Esperienza nell’utilizzo di strumenti AI per analisi, SQL, ricerca, sintesi, documentazione e produzione di deliverable;
  • Capacità di verificare criticamente gli output generati dall’AI e di riconoscerne errori, assunzioni e limiti;
  • Capacità di trasformare un’analisi in raccomandazioni chiare, priorità e azioni concrete;
  • Ottime capacità di comunicazione e presentazione, anche verso clienti e interlocutori non tecnici;
  • Capacità di organizzare e portare avanti autonomamente un workstream, segnalando tempestivamente rischi, dipendenze o punti aperti;
  • Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese.

Nice to Have

  • Conoscenza di Google Ads e Meta Ads, in particolare per quanto riguarda audience, esclusioni e utilizzo dei segnali first-party;
  • Conoscenza pratica di SQL, anche utilizzato con il supporto di strumenti AI;
  • Esperienza in ambito ecommerce e in analisi di retention, RFM o customer value;
  • Esperienza nella preparazione e nella presentazione di assessment, workshop o proposte consulenziali;
  • Precedente esperienza in agenzie, società di consulenza o contesti multi-cliente.

Caratteristiche Personali

Ci piacerebbe incontrare una persona che:

  • Affronta i dati con curiosità e spirito critico, senza fermarsi alla prima risposta disponibile;
  • Pone domande utili quando la richiesta del cliente è poco chiara o i dati non sono sufficienti;
  • Lavora per evidenze, esplicitando assunzioni, limiti e livello di affidabilità delle conclusioni;
  • Distingue ciò che può gestire autonomamente da ciò che richiede il coinvolgimento di competenze specialistiche;
  • Comunica concetti complessi in modo semplice, adattando linguaggio e livello di approfondimento all’interlocutore;
  • Utilizza l’AI come acceleratore del proprio lavoro, mantenendo controllo e responsabilità sul risultato;
  • E' organizzata, affidabile e capace di portare avanti più attività rispettando priorità e scadenze;
  • Contribuisce in modo collaborativo al lavoro del team e alla crescita dei progetti

Benefits

Avrai la possibilità di entrare a far parte di un team affiatato a cui offriamo:

  • Smart Working libero
  • Contributo Smart Working Station: un’attrezzatura a tua scelta per lavorare meglio da casa
  • Flessibilità oraria
  • Buoni Pasto elettronici cumulabili (anche quando sei in smart working!)

  • Piano di sviluppo concordato con il proprio responsabile
  • Formazione interna e esterna con tempi e budget dedicati con occasioni di partecipazione a eventi in Italia e all’estero
  • Accesso illimitato ad Upskill for Webrankers, la nostra piattaforma interna di corsi e-learning.
  • Welcome kit: zaino, laptop e postazione di lavoro dedicata
  • Possibilità di partecipare ad eventi di team building aziendali (cene a tema, grigliate estive, ecc) offerti da Webranking
  • Spazi di relax e svago, dove rilassarsi e divertirsi con i colleghi (a Correggio avrai a tua disposizione una palestra e, nei mesi estivi, la piscina)

Cosa offriamo

title: Grc, privacy & ai governance consultant
description:
Command Post | Cybersecurity, GRC & AI Governance

Command Post is expanding its cybersecurity and governance capabilities and is looking for a GRC, Privacy & AI Governance Consultant to join our growing team.

This is a hands‑on, customer‑facing role supporting the delivery and continued development of the Command Post (CP) platform, with particular focus on GRC, Privacy, AI Governance / AI Ops, presales and platform support.

We are looking for someone who understands governance and compliance in practice — not simply someone who can quote frameworks. Privacy

Privacy and data‑protection programmes

title: Golf Artisan--Talent Pool
description:
As one of the most prestigious golf venues in the UK, Brocket Hall is proud to continue the Golf Artisan program following the successful first year. Located within the stunning grounds of Brocket Hall, our two championship golf courses - Melbourne and Palmerston - are revered for their rich history and exceptional playing conditions.

Our Golf Artisans will be responsible for supporting our golf operations and course maintenance teams in maintaining the quality of the golf courses and estate. This is a volunteer role that requires a hands-on approach, attention to detail, and a a passion for golf or gardening. If you have a love for the game and a desire to work in a beautiful setting, we invite you to apply.

The rich history of Golf Artisans:

The history of artisan golf can be traced back to the esteemed Royal North Devon (RND) Golf Club in Westward Ho!, England. This legendary club, founded in 1864 by the Reverend Issac Henry Gosset, holds the distinction of being the oldest golf course in England. It is within this historic setting that the roots of artisan golf took hold.

The term “artisan golf” refers to the traditional craftsmanship and artistry that goes into creating handcrafted golf clubs. These clubs are meticulously crafted by skilled artisans who have a deep understanding of the game and a passion for creating high-quality equipment

The Artisan Golfers’ Association is affiliated to England Golf with the aim of the Association are to unite the various Artisan Golf Clubs in England into one Association and to encourage and help in the formation of Clubs.

Artisan Golfers’ Association is run by a committee comprising of a Chairman, Hon Secretary, Hon Treasurer, Tournament Secretary, Captain and an England Golf Representative. They ensure the smooth running of the organisation and arrange several annual competitions throughout the year on different golf courses.

To build a successful artisan program we have limited the program to 45 available positions with the following roles available:

- Head Artisan

- Artisan Supervisor (Melbourne, Palmerston and Golf Academy)

- Skilled Artisan

- Trainee Artisan

Requirements

In order to fulfil the requirements of a golf artisan you would need to meet the following requirements:

  • Have a passion for playing golf (Handicap is not required)
  • Must be over 16 years of age
  • Availability to commit to 416 hours per year (based on 8 hours per week)
  • Valid drivers license or method of transport to attend scheduled shifts
  • Able to stand or carry out physical activities for up to 6 hours

· Staff uniform and HSE clothing provided

· Personal liability insurance to cover you while you are fulfilling authorised volunteer work.

· Injury insurance for injuries incurred while fulfilling your authorised volunteer work.

· Complimentary use of all golf and practice facilities at Brocket Hall

tournaments representing Brocket Hall.

title: Director of Client Management

title: Agentic Capability Engineer
description:
Agentic Capability Engineer (FTC)
Borough, South London (SE1 1EP) - Hybrid

Worldwide Events Group

Worldwide Events Group, founded in 2004, is a recognised leader in global MICE and luxury travel. Across our portfolio, we bring people together and facilitate meaningful relationships, a philosophy we call H2H, human‑to‑human connection. Innovation drives our evolution. We’re embracing AI to elevate personalisation, streamline event design and create smarter, more intuitive experiences for our global communities.

Private Luxury Events: Expect the Extraordinary

Private Luxury Events delivers world‑class experiences to the luxury travel community through its event brands Amour, Private Luxury, TFest and Ultra. Our ethos has always been to put the human experience first. This mantra has powered some of the most respected events in the industry, inspiring thousands of luxury travel professionals around the world and at the heart of everything we do lies a passion for connecting people.

M&I

M&I brings together high-calibre meeting planners and exhibitors from the hospitality industry through a series of standout events across Europe, the Middle East, and the Americas. Our portfolio includes M&I Expo, M&I Flagship, M&I Healthcare, and M&I Luxe. We create beautifully crafted events that spark meaningful engagement, from curated 1-2-1 meetings to immersive moments that showcase exceptional destinations, hotels, venues and MICE services. Our events take place across Europe, the Americas and the Middle East in some of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

The Role

The Agentic Capability Engineer is responsible for helping departments identify, design, deploy and optimise AI agents and automated workflows within their day-to-day operations.

Acting as the bridge between business teams and Agent Factory, you will work closely with stakeholders across the organisation to understand challenges, implement AI-powered solutions, train users and continuously improve agent performance.

This role is modelled on the highly cross-functional capabilities required to successfully introduce and scale agentic ways of working across WWE.

This is an initial six-month fixed-term contract opportunity, with the potential for extension, reporting to the Head of AI Implementation.

Responsibilities

Business Discovery & Process Analysis

  • Work with teams across the business to understand processes, pain points and opportunities for automation.
  • Document workflows and identify where AI agents can deliver measurable value.
  • Translate business requirements into agent and workflow specifications.

Agent Design & Deployment

  • Configure, test and deploy AI agents using WWE's agent platforms.
  • Collaborate with Agent Factory to develop new capabilities and improve existing agents.
  • Support the rollout of agentic solutions across multiple departments.
  • Ensure agents are aligned with operational and commercial objectives.

Training & Adoption

  • Deliver training and coaching to users across the organisation.
  • Support teams in embedding agentic working practices into their daily operations.
  • Promote best practice usage and encourage adoption of AI tools and workflows.

Optimisation & Feedback

  • Gather user feedback and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of deployed agents and workflows.
  • Work with Agent Factory to refine prompts, workflows and agent behaviours based on operational feedback.
  • Contribute to the continuous improvement of WWE's agent ecosystem.

Knowledge & Asset Creation

  • Develop reusable agent playbooks, workflows and documentation.
  • Help build a library of organisational capabilities that can be delivered through agents.
  • Share learning, best practice and successful use cases across the business.

Due to the nature of our work, you may occasionally be required to work outside standard hours to support events or meet key deadlines

Requirements

You’ll thrive in this Agentic Capability Engineer role if you bring:

  • Strong understanding of business processes and operational workflows.
  • Highly organised with excellent problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Comfortable working with both technical and non-technical teams.
  • Experience implementing process improvements or technology-driven change.
  • Ability to learn and apply new technologies quickly.
  • Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail.
  • A genuine enthusiasm for AI, automation and emerging technologies.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

  • Background working with AI agents, large language models or workflow automation tools.
  • Familiarity with Open Claw, Hermes or similar agent orchestration platforms.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Copilot, Power Automate, Power Platform or similar technologies.
  • Knowledge of prompt engineering and AI workflow design.
  • Exposure to software development, APIs or systems integration.
  • Ability to train users and support technology adoption.
  • Experience collaborating within cross-functional project teams.
  • Experience within the events and/or travel industry.

Benefits

We offer a thoughtful package designed to support your wellbeing, growth, and work–life balance.

  • Competitive salary.
  • 28 days holiday plus UK bank holidays pro-rata, with additional days awarded for length of service.
  • A centrally located London office with a summer terrace within walking distance of the world‑famous Borough Market.
  • Regular employee social events supported by our Happiness & Culture team.

  • Employee Assistance Program offering confidential wellbeing support.

We foster an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and able to thrive. We welcome individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and lived experiences, including differences in gender identity, orientation, expression, age, race, ethnicity, physical or mental ability, neurodiversity, religion or belief, and socio‑economic background. title: Per Diem Ultrasonographer

Dedicated to precision and professionalism, the Per Diem sonographer also ensures patient comfort, safety, and education throughout the imaging procedure.

We are seeking a sonographer to join our dedicated team. The role is a Per Diem on-site position with morning availability, and a minimum of 20-25 hours, offering flexibility and the opportunity to contribute to a patient’s life-changing journey.

Key Responsibilities

Perform transvaginal and abdominal ultrasounds to assess pelvic structures, monitor follicular development, and diagnose reproductive conditions.

  • Utilize advanced ultrasound technology to obtain high-quality images with precision.
  • Ensure accuracy in capturing, documenting, and analyzing diagnostic images.
  • Prioritize patient comfort, safety, and confidentiality during procedures.
  • Identify and interpret normal and abnormal findings to support fertility assessments.
  • Collaborate with physicians to provide timely, accurate diagnostic reports and assist in treatment planning.
  • Maintain detailed and organized patient records and ultrasound reports.
  • Educate and support patients by explaining procedures and their role in fertility care.
  • Ensure proper maintenance, calibration, and troubleshooting of ultrasound equipment.
  • Follow infection control protocols and maintain a clean, safe clinical environment.
  • Assist with additional projects and duties as assigned.

title: Buyer / Supply Chain Specialist
description:
NextGen RF Design is seeking a highly organized, adaptable Buyer / Supply Chain Specialist to support purchasing and day-to-day supply-chain execution in a growing RF manufacturing environment. The role will initially focus on component and material purchasing while helping improve inventory accuracy, material readiness, and production coordination.

We are looking for an ambitious, motivated individual who is interested in building a career in supply chain and is willing to learn. Prior experience in every area listed below is not expected. We will provide training and hands-on experience to help the right person learn our products, systems, suppliers, and supply-chain processes.

The ideal candidate is proactive, detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable taking on a variety of responsibilities as the business grows. This role provides an opportunity to build broad experience across procurement, inventory, production planning, compliance, and other supply-chain activities.


LOCATION: This is an onsite position at our North Mankato Facility. Remote work is not available.


WORK AUTHORIZATION: Candidates must be currently authorized to work in the United States. NextGen RF Design does not provide visa sponsorship for this position.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Purchasing and Supplier Support

  • Support day-to-day purchasing of electronic components, assemblies, and other production materials.
  • Create and manage purchase orders, follow open orders, and work with suppliers to support cost, lead-time, and delivery needs.
  • Develop strong supplier and distributor relationships and communicate shortages, pricing changes, obsolescence, and other supply risks.
  • Support sourcing and cost-reduction activities under the direction of Supply Chain leadership.

Material Readiness and Inventory Support

  • Monitor material availability and purchasing requirements to identify shortages, excess inventory, and long-lead risks.
  • Support material-readiness reviews and production scheduling by helping determine when builds are material complete.
  • Coordinate with Production & Logistics to understand inventory availability and resolve material-related issues affecting purchasing or production.
  • Cross-train on inventory-control activities, including cycle counting and reconciliation, to provide backup support when needed.



Cross-Functional Supply Chain Support

  • Work closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Manufacturing, Quality, and Operations to keep material needs, priorities, and changes aligned.
  • Support component lifecycle, alternate-source, approved vendor list, and obsolescence activities by gathering supplier, cost, lead-time, and availability information for review by Engineering and Quality.
  • Participate in material and production planning discussions and communicate purchasing or supply-chain risks that could affect schedules.

Compliance and Development Support

  • Support sourcing and documentation requirements such as country of origin, NDAA/TAA, traceability, counterfeit-part prevention, and other customer or defense supply-chain requirements.
  • Maintain organized procurement and supplier records to support audit and compliance needs.
  • Cross-train in related processes such as production scheduling, approved vendor list maintenance, ERP/PLM activities, and engineering change/configuration-management support as experience grows.
  • Take on additional supply-chain and operational responsibilities based on business needs, individual strengths, interests, and professional growth.

Systems and Data Management

  • Maintain accurate supplier, pricing, lead-time, part, and purchasing data in the ERP/MRP system.
  • Maintain visibility into open orders, material availability, inventory status, and supply risks needed to support purchasing and production planning.
  • Ensure purchasing activities align with current released Bills of Materials (BOMs), approved sources, and applicable engineering changes.
  • Support ERP/PLM activities, including data validation, system cleanup, and maintenance of accurate supply-chain information.
  • Support reporting and data analysis related to purchasing, inventory, supplier performance, and material readiness.

JOB REQUIREMENTS:

  • Strong organization, attention to detail, follow-through, and ability to manage changing priorities.
  • Prior experience in purchasing, supply chain, inventory, manufacturing, or a related environment preferred; electronic component purchasing experience is a plus.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products, particularly Excel, and comfort working with ERP/MRP systems, data, and inventory information; willingness to learn new systems and processes.
  • Strong communication and problem-solving skills with a collaborative, hands-on approach.
  • Interest and ability to learn electronic components, BOMs, sourcing requirements, and regulated/defense supply-chain expectations.



JOB SNAPSHOT

Base Pay: Competitive salary and is commensurate with experience

Employment: Full-Time Salary

Benefits: Health Insurance, PTO, HSA, Paid holidays

Job Type: Supply Chain, Procurement, Operations

Education: Bachelor's degree, associate degree, or equivalent relevant experience

Experience: Entry Level to 3 years

Manages Others: No

Industry: Contract Manufacturing & Engineering

Required Travel: Limited; occasional supplier visits or industry events as needed
