title: Product Manager
description:
As a Product Manager at Corcentric, you will join a fun, collaborative team within an ambitious, entrepreneurial global organization. You will drive the strategy, design, and maintenance of key modules and capability sets in our flagship SaaS solution, working as part of a product management team, focusing on improving the overall user experience while maintaining a leading position in the market.

This key position reports to the VP, Product Management, within our Downstream Source-to-Pay (S2P) team, and partners closely with development, professional services, support, sales, and other internal cross-functional teams as well as customers and company business partners. Your area of focus will be procure-to-pay (P2P) and core platform features of Corcentric’s flagship product for corporate purchasing and accounts payable business processes targeted towards mid-market and Fortune 1000 companies. We’re a dedicated, down-to-earth group in a growing organization offering plenty of opportunity. We look forward to adding you into the mix!

As a Product Manager, you’ll be responsible for:

  • Guiding the design, development, maintenance, and presentation of the procure-to-pay process business as enabled in our solution: requisition, purchase order, receipt, and invoice
  • Understanding customer needs and driving the evolution of the product by translating business requirements into software product functionality
  • Creating, refining, prioritizing and maintaining the product requirements backlog and product roadmaps
  • Developing detailed, crisp business requirements and user stories that can be used to create product specifications, queries, and architecture for each part of the procure to pay process
  • Managing prioritization and trade-offs among Corcentric customers and development resources
  • Engaging with customers and internal stakeholders in developing useful analytics and information for use in the platform
  • Working with the development team on User Interface (UI) design/validation, sprint reviews and User Acceptance Testing (UAT)
  • Supporting the creation of materials to educate and train cross functional teams and customers
  • Assisting sales and services teams as the product subject matter expert
  • Maintaining an awareness of current research and best practices in the field of procure to pay product management

The P2P Product Management team is distributed globally, and primarily operates remotely. We are considering candidates interested in working remotely out of the US Eastern Time Zone in the following states: NJ, VA, PA, MD, NC, FL, OH, GA. For candidates who prefer an in-office work environment, we operate offices in Cherry Hill, NJ and Bethesda, MD, although your immediate team members may not be local to those location.

Requirements

You’ll need to have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, or comparable career experience
  • Experience as a Product Manager or Product Owner for a technology company, getting into the weeds and being the go-to expert for the product; alternatively, you’ll need extensive experience utilizing procure to pay tools in a non-Product role.
  • Passion about dissecting challenges and coming up with solutions,
  • A very strong ability to analyze and synthesize complex topics, but simplify and organize it for others
  • Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills
  • Experience with Agile software development methodologies
  • Undergraduate degree in technical or a related field, or equivalent work experience

(We want to make sure you’re set up to succeed, and we view these as the critical skills you’ll need to achieve great things at Corcentric!)

It’s great if you also have:

  • An MBA
  • Technical understanding of coding and IT standards
  • Jira/Confluence experience
  • Experience with JavaScript or PHP
  • Experience collaborating with international team members
  • Experience with source to pay, payment, or invoicing processes, contract lifecycle management, catalog management, B2B commerce or sourcing software/services, or an ERP platform

About Us

Corcentric is a global provider of business spend management and revenue management software and services for mid-market and Fortune 1000 businesses. Corcentric delivers software, advisory services, and payments focused on reducing costs, optimizing working capital, and unlocking revenue.

We achieve success by exemplifying our core values in the way we work, communicate, and collaborate:

  • Do the Right Thing
  • Embrace + Drive Change
  • Be Empowered
  • Be Relentlessly Focused on the Customer

Benefits

At Corcentric, we know that the hard work of our employees is what drives the success of our organization. We care about who you are and what you value, both inside and outside of work.

Within our organization, you will have the opportunity to work with smart, collaborative team members and approachable leaders. Our down-to-earth, solutions-oriented culture means you'll have the opportunity to get hands-on with interesting work projects and be able to draw a short line from your contributions to business impacts. We prioritize professional development and encourage cross-functional promotional opportunities to enable you to reach your career goals. We have been in business for over 28 years and are thrilled to be actively growing and scaling our teams accordingly - it's an exciting environment and a great time to join.

title: Affiliated Institutions Only: Observership Application
description:
Thank you for your interest in an observership opportunity! Please read the information below carefully before applying:

NOTE: This opportunity is only available to individuals who attend an affiliated institution to Innovative Hematology, Inc. and have confirmed a specific staff member at IHI to serve as their preceptor.

What is an observership?

As a nationally and internationally recognized hemophilia treatment center, the organization actively supports training for professional colleagues working in related settings and observerships for students considering a career as a physician. We acknowledge that in providing training and observership experiences we must ensure a safe and confidential environment for patients, staff and invitees.

What are the eligibility criteria?

To be eligible for an observership, you must meet one of the following requirements:

  • College student seeking exposure to the medical field or hematology
  • Demonstrated interest or current trainee in medical school, residency, or fellowship
  • Physician or other clinical provider from the U.S. or abroad seeking to expand their knowledge of related fields

What is the timeline for applying?

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis; however a minimum of 4-6 weeks notice is required due to clinical schedules and departmental criteria.

What is the length of an observership?

College students may observe for 1-2 days as determined by the organization's ability to meet the needs of the student. Residents and fellows are generally allowed 2-4 weeks but may vary based on the objectives and availability of the department.

Requirements

Required application components

NOTE: You are only permitted one attempt to complete the application. Please ensure you have all your documents prepared to upload. This process takes approximately 15 minutes.

  • Complete Online Application and Visiting Colleague/Student Agreement
  • Medical License Number if applicable
  • Upload Curriculum Vitae (CV), 1-2 pages in length highlighting your education and employment
  • Upload Letter of Support from Home Institution as a cover letter**
    • **not required for affiliates of IU Med School, MUCOM, Ascension St. Vincent/PMCH, Purdue University School of Pharmacy, Yale University Hematology Fellowship, Franklin College PA Program, or St. Joseph's University - Philadelphia PA Program

Upon acceptance, the following must be completed prior to first day of program:

  • Send Malpractice Insurance Certificate to hr@ihtc.org
  • Acknowledgement of Center guidelines by return email
  • Submission of photo or copy of current student picture ID
  • Completion of Healthstream module(s)
  • HIPAA log signature upon first day arrival

Failure to timely complete the following as outlined may result in delay or cancellation of observership.

Innovative Hematology and its affiliates are an Equal Opportunity Employer

title: New Grad Full-Time Quantitative Trader
description:
About the Role

A proprietary trading firm based in Chicago is seeking a highly motivated New Grad Quantitative Trader to join the team full-time. In this role, you will apply analytical thinking, market intuition, and quantitative problem-solving to identify trading opportunities, manage risk, and contribute to the development of data-driven strategies across global markets.

This is an ideal opportunity for recent graduates who are passionate about financial markets, probability, game theory, technology, and fast-paced decision-making. You will work closely with experienced traders, quantitative researchers, and engineers to learn how modern trading strategies are designed, tested, and executed.

Requirements

Responsibilities

  • Monitor and analyze real-time market data to identify trading opportunities.
  • Support the development, testing, and refinement of quantitative trading strategies.
  • Make fast, data-informed trading decisions while managing risk.
  • Collaborate with traders, researchers, and engineers to improve trading models, tools, and execution systems.
  • Conduct statistical analysis on historical and live market data.
  • Evaluate market microstructure, liquidity, volatility, and other drivers of price movement.
  • Participate in trading simulations, training programs, and strategy review sessions.
  • Communicate trade ideas, risks, and performance insights clearly to the team.
  • Continuously improve decision-making through feedback, research, and post-trade analysis.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Economics, Finance, or a related quantitative field.
  • Strong quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Interest in financial markets, trading, probability, strategy games, or competitive problem-solving.
  • Ability to make decisions quickly and remain calm under pressure.
  • Strong attention to detail and intellectual curiosity.
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills.
  • Programming experience in Python or a similar language is preferred.
  • Prior internship, research, trading competition, or personal project experience involving data analysis, markets, or quantitative modeling is a plus but not required.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is intellectually curious, competitive, numerically strong, and comfortable making decisions with incomplete information. You enjoy solving complex problems, thinking strategically, learning from feedback, and working in a fast-moving environment where performance and precision matter.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Comprehensive training in trading, market structure, risk management, and quantitative strategy development.
  • Mentorship from experienced traders, researchers, and technologists.
  • Exposure to live markets and real-time trading decision-making.
  • A collaborative, high-performance environment that values curiosity, discipline, and continuous learning.
  • Opportunities for rapid growth based on performance, ownership, and impact.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits package.

description:
In Webranking guidiamo la crescita dei maggiori brand nazionali e internazionali trasformando dati, visione strategica ed eccellenza operativa in campagne ad alto impatto.

Stiamo ampliando l’area Digital Advertising e cerchiamo una persona per il ruolo di Senior Digital Advertising.

Cerchiamo un profilo strategico e analitico, capace di orchestrare budget complessi, guidare la relazione con clienti e contribuire all'innovazione delle metodologie del team. Se cerchi un ambiente stimolante, dinamico e con reali opportunità di impatto, questo è il ruolo giusto.

Ruolo

Come Senior Digital Advertising avrai la responsabilità end-to-end della strategia media sui clienti presidiati, agendo da consulente di fiducia e punto di riferimento tecnico per il team. In particolare ti occuperai di:

  • Media Strategy & Budget Management: Gestione di strategie di investimento omnicanale complesse, ottimizzando l'allocazione dei budget in logica di massimizzazione dei Kpi chiave.
  • Eccellenza Operativa & Avanzata: Gestione e ottimizzazione avanzata di campagne Search e Social Advertising (in particolare su Google Ads, Meta Ads, Tik Tok Ads).
  • Advanced Measurement & Frameworks: Progettazione e implementazione di studi di misurazione complessi (Incrementality test, Geo-Lift, Causal Impact) e supporto nell'analisi tramite Marketing Mix Model (MMM) per valutare l'efficacia causale del media sulle performance.
  • Advanced Analytics & Attribution: Analisi approfondita dei dati (anche incrociando metriche online e offline), interpretazione di modelli di attribuzione, misurazione dei KPI avanzati e trasformazione dei numeri in insight ad alto valore strategico per il top management del cliente.
  • AI Adoption & Automation: Guidare la sperimentazione e l'adozione strategica di strumenti di Intelligenza Artificiale Generativa e Predittiva nel workflow di Media Planning, creative testing e analisi avanzata dei dati.
  • Consulting & Client Leadership: Presentazione periodica delle performance, raccomandazioni strategiche e roadmap di crescita ai clienti assegnati.
  • Innovazione e Mentoring: Test di nuove funzionalità/piattaforme adv e supporto nella crescita tecnica dei profili più junior del team.

Requirements

Sei la persona che stiamo cercando se hai:

  • Almeno 4-5 anni di esperienza nel ruolo di Digital Advertising / Paid Media Specialist, maturati idealmente all’interno di Centri Media o Agenzie di Digital Marketing strutturate.
  • Padronanza avanzata delle principali piattaforme ADV (Google Ads, Meta Ads) e solida autonomia nell'utilizzo di strumenti di Web Analytics (GA4, Adobe Analytics) e di Data Visualization (Looker Studio, PowerBi).
  • Solide competenze in ambito Data Analysis, con ottima padronanza di MS Excel e un forte background in ambito test & misurazione (es. approcci data-driven per misurare causalità e incrementalità).
  • Dimostrata capacità di gestire clienti complessi, budget importanti e relazioni con stakeholder di livello medio-alto.
  • Ottima conoscenza della lingua inglese (almeno B2/C1), per la gestione di clienti internazionali.

Caratteristiche Personali

  • Eccellenti capacità di data storytelling: capacità di sintesi qualitativa del dato, per tradurre metriche tattiche in visioni strategiche chiare per i referenti aziendali di alto livello.
  • AI Mindset: piena predisposizione e forte interesse verso i tool di AI. Conoscenza (o grande motivazione all'esplorazione) dell'ecosistema di strumenti di Intelligenza Artificiale applicati al MarTech e al Performance Marketing, per efficientare processi e massimizzare i risultati.
  • Visione strategica, spiccata attitudine al problem solving e forte orientamento ai risultati di business.
  • Autonomia nella gestione delle priorità, precisione e capacità di lavorare su più progetti complessi contemporaneamente.
  • Doti di leadership, comunicazione efficace e propensione al mentoring e al lavoro di squadra.

Nice to Have

  • Esperienza pregressa nella progettazione di logiche di allocazione budget avanzate (es. GeoBidding o GeoBoost).
  • Esperienza su piattaforme avanzate di Bid Management (es. Search Ads 360, DoubleClick/SA360).
  • Conoscenza e operatività su verticali ADV aggiuntivi (TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Microsoft Ads, Pinterest, Snapchat).
  • Certificazioni attive sulle principali piattaforme adv (Google, Meta, ecc.).

Benefits

Avrai la possibilità di entrare a far parte di un team affiatato a cui offriamo:

  • Smart Working libero
  • Contributo Smart Working Station: un’attrezzatura a tua scelta per lavorare meglio da casa
  • Flessibilità oraria
  • Buoni Pasto elettronici cumulabili (anche quando sei in smart working!)

  • Piano di sviluppo concordato con il proprio responsabile
  • Formazione interna e esterna con tempi e budget dedicati con occasioni di partecipazione a eventi in Italia e all’estero
  • Accesso illimitato ad Upskill for Webrankers, la nostra piattaforma interna di corsi e-learning.
  • Welcome kit: zaino, laptop e postazione di lavoro dedicata

  • Spazi di relax e svago, dove rilassarsi e divertirsi con i colleghi (a Correggio avrai a tua disposizione una palestra e, nei mesi estivi, la piscina)

Cosa offriamo

Are you passionate about helping students succeed in the classroom and beyond? As a family-owned organization, we believe in a person-centered approach that empowers students, supports school staff, and creates meaningful, lasting change. title: Real Estate Investment Associate
location: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa
description:
Roseau Ford is building a portfolio of residential-scale senior living communities — senior coliving and cohousing — designed for upper-income residents who want connection, autonomy, and community at home. We’re a small, high-trust team at an early stage of growth, and this is a foundational role. You’ll touch every part of the business — from sourcing and underwriting acquisition targets to structuring deals with lenders, and from coordinating architects and contractors to managing resident experience and community programming. As the portfolio scales, you’ll have the opportunity to grow into the function that best fits your strengths, whether that’s on the investment and capital side or the property and community side. Both are strategic to what we’re building. You’ll work directly with the principal and senior partners across multiple projects simultaneously.

What you’ll do

Acquisitions & deal sourcing

  • Source acquisition opportunities against a defined buy box using MLS, off-market channels, and direct outreach
  • Conduct preliminary property analysis and filter candidates against investment criteria
  • Initiate and manage seller communications to gather preliminary information, rent rolls, and expense history
  • Draft letters of intent for principal review and signature

Financial analysis & deal structuring

  • Build and maintain pro formas for acquisition and development projects
  • Track NOI, DSCR, and returns assumptions across the portfolio
  • Structure loan terms with lenders and prepare lender packages
  • Coordinate due diligence, manage third-party reporting timelines, and support closing execution from accepted LOI through funding

Project coordination

  • Serve as a coordination point between architects, contractors, and vendors across active projects
  • Track schedules and deliverables; flag issues early
  • Manage document flow and approvals across active projects

Property management support

  • Support day-to-day rental operations including lease tracking and resident communications
  • Coordinate vendors and triage maintenance issues
  • Help evaluate and interface with third-party operators

Resident experience & programming

  • Help design and coordinate community programming and activities for senior residents
  • Develop resident onboarding materials, community agreements, and engagement touchpoints
  • Think holistically about what makes a home feel like a community

Operations & process building

  • Help create SOPs, workflows, and playbooks as the portfolio grows
  • Document what works; identify gaps
  • Build systems that allow the team to scale without adding complexity

Requirements

Experience

2–5 years across real estate, property management, development, or hospitality. Direct experience building pro formas, working with lenders, or evaluating acquisition targets is a strong plus.

People skills

Warm, professional communicator. Comfortable interfacing with sellers, residents, vendors, and lenders — often in the same day. Discretion and care matter here, especially with senior residents.

Generalist mindset

Equally comfortable with a deal spreadsheet and a community calendar. Doesn’t need a narrow lane. Enjoys variety and can prioritize across competing tasks without losing things.

Self-directed

This is a remote role on a small team. You’ll need to manage your own workload, surface issues proactively, and work without close supervision most of the time.

Systems thinking

When you do a task twice, you write it down the third time. Interested in building processes, not just completing them. Comfortable with ambiguity in a growing organization.

Nice to have

Background in senior living, aging services, or community development. Familiarity with RAL-scale or residential assisted living concepts. Experience evaluating your own real estate deals or managing your own portfolio. Interest in the coliving movement.

Working at Roseau Ford

Small team, high trust, direct access to leadership. This is not a siloed role — you’ll see the full picture of how investment projects come together, from deal sourcing through resident move-in. As the portfolio grows, the natural evolution of this role is a split between the investment and capital function and the property and community function. We don’t need you to have chosen a lane yet. We value people who are honest about what they don’t know, curious enough to figure it out, and reliable enough that things don’t fall through the cracks.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with experience ($1500 - $1900 monthly)
  • Opportunity for performance-based bonuses as the company grows
  • Direct mentorship from the founder and CEO
  • 21 days of paid time off
  • Health benefits

title: MORROW Experience Executive
description:
MORROW HEALTH

MORROW Health is Singapore’s largest integrated fitness and recovery destination, designed to help individuals build healthier, more resilient lives through intentional daily habits. Grounded in lifestyle medicine, MORROW Health brings together physical activity, nutrition, restorative sleep, stress management, avoidance of risky substances, and social connection through structured programmes and purpose-built environments that make sustainable lifestyle change achievable. Supported by evidence-informed practice and data from wearables and lifestyle inputs, MORROW Health helps members recognise patterns, build consistency, and stay accountable—turning insight into everyday action that supports long-term vitality, strength, and clarity, without medical diagnosis or treatment.

Location: Singapore
Reports To: Membership Experience Manager

Role Overview

As a MORROW Experience Executive, you will be the first point of contact for our members and guests, playing a critical role in shaping their journey with us. You will manage daily queries, provide exceptional service recovery, and ensure every interaction reflects our brand values of care, wellness, and excellence.

This role goes beyond standard customer service — you will act as a brand ambassador, guiding members through our service offerings, resolving feedback promptly, and creating meaningful experiences that foster loyalty and retention.

Key Responsibilities

  • Handle customer feedback, complaints, compliments, and inquiries with professionalism and empathy.
  • Provide accurate information on all service offerings (wellness, recovery, nutrition, and lifestyle facilities) to members and guests.
  • Manage and maintain merchandise inventory: monitor stock levels, ensure timely replenishment, oversee visual-merchandising standards and presentation of retail displays to uphold our brand experience.
  • Support the daily operations of the membership desk, including rostering coverage, queue management, and appointment scheduling.
  • Log, escalate, and follow up on service issues in line with SOPs, ensuring timely resolution and service recovery.
  • Maintain up-to-date knowledge of promotions, membership packages, and new service launches.
  • Collect and relay member feedback to the Manager for continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Assist in the execution of member engagement activities, workshops, or events.
  • Ensure data accuracy when updating member records in the CRM system.
  • Uphold confidentiality, service consistency, and compliance with organisational standards.

Requirements

  • Diploma/Certificate in Hospitality, Business, Customer Service, or related field.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of experience in customer-facing roles, preferably in hospitality, healthcare, fitness, spa, or wellness environments.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a natural customer-first mindset.
  • Ability to remain calm under pressure and resolve conflicts with professionalism.
  • Tech-savvy with experience using CRM or booking systems.
  • Team player who is adaptable, proactive, and comfortable working in a startup environment.
  • Bonus: Prior experience in wellness-focused settings such as gyms, spas, recovery facilities, or health & lifestyle clubs.

Benefits

This is a career-defining opportunity to shape the future of longevity medicine while working alongside world-class clinicians and technologists. You will contribute to initiatives that directly lead to extending human healthspan while establishing Singapore as the global hub for longevity innovation.

At MORROW, you will not only help define operational excellence but also build the culture, rhythm, and future of interventions. You won't just be joining a team. You will be co-creating tomorrow.

title: Technician
description:
Laboratory Technician

At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve transitioned quantum computing from an academic ambition into a commercial reality—and we’re just getting started.

The Purpose

Keep OQC’s laboratory environments safe, well supplied and ready for the engineers developing our quantum computers.

As a Laboratory Technician, you’ll help maintain critical cryogenic equipment, complete practical engineering work orders and support the assembly and upkeep of the systems that enable our technical teams to deliver their objectives.

The Role

Working within Engineering Operations and reporting to the Laboratory Supervisor, you’ll provide hands-on support across OQC’s laboratories, workshops and other technical spaces.

You’ll monitor equipment, respond to incidents, maintain stock and safety records, and work closely with Quantum Engineers, hardware teams, deployment teams and other Laboratory Technicians. The role includes acting as a first responder during scheduled shifts and agreed on-call periods, with occasional travel to support OQC’s globally deployed devices.

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Maintain the availability and performance of cryogenic equipment, coordinating servicing, resolving faults and escalating complex issues when required.
  • Complete work orders involving electronic, electrical and mechanical assemblies, alongside general maintenance activities supporting the development of OQC’s quantum computers.
  • Support the set-up, assembly, disassembly and maintenance of quantum computers and associated scientific equipment.
  • Help maintain day-to-day health and safety standards across laboratories and workshops, including preparing and documenting risk assessments under appropriate supervision.
  • Respond to alerts and technical incidents, assess immediate risks, troubleshoot issues such as dilution refrigerator faults or chemical spills, and escalate where necessary.
  • Monitor laboratory resources, stock and liquid nitrogen levels, working with the Stores Controller to coordinate checks, orders and approved requisitions.
  • Record incidents and technical issues accurately on agreed platforms, maintaining clear logs and communicating relevant updates to the wider organisation.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience working in a technical or industrial environment.
  • Experience following health and safety procedures and preparing or documenting risk assessments.
  • Practical electrical measurement skills.
  • Hands-on experience assembling and fitting mechanical components, ideally involving scientific or technical equipment.
  • Experience operating water systems and manifolds.
  • A technical apprenticeship, BTEC or relevant engineering degree, supported by industry experience.
  • An adaptable and practical approach, with strong communication, creativity and problem-solving skills.

The ‘Nice-to-Haves’

  • Experience supporting project-management activities or coordinating technical work.
  • Experience working with vendors or external service providers.
  • Familiarity with cryogens, cryogenic equipment or dilution refrigerator systems.
  • Knowledge of vacuum systems, quantum computers or high-pressure cylinders and manifolds.
  • Additional technical qualifications in a mechanical or electrical discipline.
  • Strong planning and organisational skills, sound decision-making and a commitment to delivering high-quality work.

title: Director of Finance
description:
Director of Finance

Reports to: Chief Financial Officer

Supervises: Controller (who supervises the accounting team)

Status: Full-time, Exempt

Leadership body: Operating Committee

POSITION SUMMARY

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, transparency, and strategic stewardship of the Alaska Community Foundation’s financial operations. Working closely with the Chief Financial Officer, this position oversees fund accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, and regulatory compliance within a complex community foundation structure that includes donor-advised, restricted, endowment, and agency funds. The Director of Finance brings deep technical expertise in nonprofit GAAP and the ability to translate complex financial data into clear, actionable insights for leadership, board members, and stakeholders.

The Director of Finance reviews, analyzes, and reports on the Foundation’s financial activity and supervises the Controller, who owns and executes the monthly and year-end close. The Director supports the CFO above and the Controller below—setting standards, reviewing results, and providing analysis and reporting—without performing the mechanics of the close. Close matters are routed to the Controller for execution.

This position partners closely with executive leadership to ensure that the Foundation’s financial systems, policies, and reporting frameworks support organizational strategy, donor intent, and long-term sustainability. As a member of the Operating Committee, the Director of Finance contributes to cross-functional planning and organizational decision-making, and serves as a key bridge between the finance function and non-finance staff, program teams, and development and donor stewardship partners across the Foundation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Leadership and Strategy

  • Serves as a strategic finance partner to the CFO, providing actionable financial insights to support decision-making and long-term organizational sustainability.
  • Supports the CFO in long-range financial planning, scenario analysis, risk assessment, and organizational sustainability modeling.
  • Contributes to enterprise-wide initiatives, including system implementations, policy development, and operational improvements.
  • Translates technical financial concepts into clear guidance for non-finance staff, leadership, and board audiences.

Fund Accounting and Financial Reporting

  • Provides oversight and technical review of fund accounting across donor-advised funds, restricted and unrestricted funds, endowments (including principal and spendable classifications), and agency and held-for-others funds in accordance with FASB ASC 958-605 and FASB ASC 958-810, with day-to-day execution performed by the Controller and accounting team.
  • Ensures accurate classification and reporting of net assets with and without donor restrictions, including complex transactions such as multi-year pledges, discounting, and contribution revenue recognition.
  • Reviews and analyzes the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements prepared by the Controller, and presents them to the CFO.
  • Delivers timely budget-to-actual reporting at organizational and departmental levels, including year-to-date and period-specific analysis.

Close Process and Financial Operations

  • Sets close standards and continuously improves the month-end and year-end close framework, and reviews the close executed by the Controller with a focus on accuracy, analysis, timeliness, and reporting—rather than performing close mechanics directly.
  • Reviews reconciliations of all key accounts—including cash, investments, pledges receivable, and liabilities—completed by the accounting team under the Controller.
  • Oversees cash management, including banking relationships and treasury functions.
  • Maintains oversight of accounts payable, accounts receivable, and disbursement cycles, including grantmaking disbursements.

Internal Controls and Compliance

  • Designs, implements, and monitors a robust internal control environment aligned with nonprofit best practices and audit requirements, with control execution carried out by the Controller and accounting team.
  • Ensures compliance with nonprofit GAAP, federal and state regulations, and organizational policy across all finance functions.
  • Develops and maintains finance policies covering expenditure authority, credit card and expense management, grant approval workflows, and revenue recognition and pledge accounting.
  • Partners with external auditors and oversees audit preparation, which is coordinated operationally by the Controller on behalf of the finance team.

Systems and Process Optimization

  • Serves as the finance lead for core systems including Community Suite (fund accounting), grant management and reporting platforms, and banking and credit card platforms.
  • Drives system enhancements, integrations, and process automation to improve efficiency and reduce manual effort.
  • Develops scalable processes that support organizational growth and increasing operational complexity.

Grantmaking and Financial Oversight

  • Oversees financial controls and workflows related to grant voucher approvals and disbursements.
  • Ensures compliance with donor intent, fund restrictions, and organizational policies across all grantmaking activity.
  • Partners with program and development teams to support accurate, compliant, and timely grant financial activity.

Team and Operational Leadership

  • Supervise and develop the Controller, and through the Controller support the growth, performance, and continuous improvement of the accounting team.
  • Develop and manage departmental budgets, work plans, and performance metrics in alignment with organizational goals and financial oversight responsibilities.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement across the finance function.
  • Work across departments to ensure finance operations align with ACF’s strategic priorities and organizational values.

Operating Committee Participation

  • Serve as an active member of the Operating Committee, contributing to cross-functional planning and organizational decision-making.
  • Bring a financial stewardship and risk management lens to foundation-wide initiatives and ensure consistent fiscal positioning across the organization.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or a related field required; CPA or advanced degree preferred.
  • Eight to twelve or more years of progressive accounting and finance experience, with significant experience in nonprofit accounting, preferably within a community foundation or similar philanthropic organization.
  • Demonstrated expertise in fund accounting and complex revenue recognition, including pledges, restricted gifts, and endowments.
  • Deep knowledge of U.S. GAAP, specifically nonprofit standards under FASB ASC 958, including net asset classifications, endowment accounting, and agency versus owned fund structures.
  • Experience working with auditors and leading financial statement preparation and audit processes.
  • Experience with fund accounting systems such as Community Suite or similar platforms; advanced Excel and financial modeling skills.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to present financial information clearly to executive leadership, finance committees, and board members.
  • A commitment to Alaska, its communities, and the mission of the Alaska Community Foundation.

CORE COMPETENCIES

  • Strategic financial leadership
  • Technical expertise and accuracy
  • Complexity management
  • Systems and process orientation
  • Cross-functional communication
  • Integrity and mission alignment

WORK ENVIRONMENT AND ACCESSIBILITY

We are committed to creating an inclusive and accessible workplace. The physical, sensory, and environmental requirements described here represent the general nature of the role and are not intended to exclude individuals who can perform the essential functions of the position with or without reasonable accommodation.

This role may involve a combination of desk-based and active work in a professional office or field environment. The position requires the ability to effectively engage in communication, operate standard office technology or job-related equipment, and perform the core responsibilities of the role.

Reasonable accommodations will be provided in accordance with applicable laws to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

title: Rehabilitation Technical Officer - Tawilah, North Darfur
description:
Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organization working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organization works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organization. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview. For more information about the organisation.

JOB CONTEXT:
Since January 2024, HI has been responding to Sudan’s crisis. HI’s joint multisectoral response in Gedaref State, implemented with a Sudanese partner NGO, is already providing physical and functional rehabilitation services in healthcare centers and at community level, as well as MHPSS services, including individual and group counselling. HI is further engaged at the humanitarian coordination level to mainstream disability inclusion throughout the humanitarian response.

HI is scaling up its response from both geographic and modalities/sectorial perspectives. In particular, HI has deployed emergency response teams in Darfur, to setup its operations and initiate its response in the western parts of Sudan. Since 2026, HI team is also active in other sectors such as Functional and Physical rehabilitation, and mutualized logistics. The advertised vacancy is to be part of that team.

The main office is currently in Tawila, North Darfur, but HI is also operational in Geneina, West Darfur, and exploring having an operational presence in Nyala, South Darfur.

YOUR MISSION:

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, as Stimulation therapy Technical Officer you are responsible for overseeing the implementation of project’ stimulation therapy activities for under five malnourished children.

Your role involves providing technical expertise and ensuring strict adherence to HI’s established stimulation therapy protocols by the project’s physiotherapists.

You lead the stimulation therapy for malnourished children initial training for the project’s rehabilitation professionals and ensure their continuous follow up and mentorship.

You are responsible for fostering a culture of continuous child development stimulation among parents and caregivers, and for guiding the physiotherapists in educating parents/caregivers on age appropriate and needs based stimulation techniques. You work closely with nutritional actors targeted by the project.

In this framework, your main missions are :


Mission 1: Providing guidance and technical support to project in accordance with the technical frameworks and general standards of your sectoral scope

a. Provide appropriate technical guidance and support to project leaders and/or specialists.

b. Ensure project(s) Stimulation therapy of malnourished children activities are implemented in accordance with quality and established protocols and propose adjustments or improvements as necessary.

c. Adapt project documentation as required, in accordance with Stimulation therapy of malnourished children technical standards and norms.

d. Develop stimulation therapy tools and ensure their availability

e. Contribute to the regular reporting of stimulation therapy of malnourished children activities (collection and analysis of stimulation therapy data collected) in conjunction with the project team and the MEAL team.

f. Coordinate and collaborate with the nutrition actors as delegated by the Project Manager.

Mission 2: Providing project-based technical learning

a. Ensure global and field technical specialists get the information they need and collaborate with technical divisions as needed.

b. Collect the elements necessary for capitalization exercises or scientific documentation.

c. Contribute to technical learning under the responsibility of the specialist or project manager, based on best practices.

d. Responsible for the technical learning of projects based on lessons learned and good practices

e. Adjust activities to audit recommendations as appropriate.

f. Implement recommendations to improve the technical quality of projects.

g. Ensure the technical quality and relevance of project activities implemented within their area of expertise; conduct self-evaluation of their project and participate in evaluation cycles under the supervision of the PM.

h. Taking ownership of norms and standards anticipates and prepares for nexus adjustments.

i. Propose research and study topics.

j. Oversee data collection for research activities.

k. Contribute to the terms of reference for evaluations.

Mission 3: Contributing to the animation of your sector

a. Contribute to technical recruitment.

b. Lead the stimulation therapy initial training

c. Contribute to the skills upgrading plan for professionals in its sector and may be a third-party assessor.

d. May contribute to the development of a local talent pool within his/her sector (conducts technical interviews of candidates and makes recommendations, identifies training and coaching needs).

e. Assists in coordinating technical professional development and facilitating a community of practice, in collaboration with the technical division. Conducts technical trainings for staff as appropriate.

f. Contribute to the design and collection of operational data to ensure adequate monitoring of activities or ad hoc data collection activities, and ensure appropriate measurement of project completion in his/her area of expertise.

g. Ensure that data processing is established and carried out in accordance with the rules and principles set by the IM/MEAL and by the technical councils of the sector of expertise.

Mission 4: Contribute to ensure the technical influence of HI on its perimeter

a. Contribute to the outreach of HI expertise: Represent HI Stimulation therapy technical expertise by delegation in relevant local, regional and international networks and with local nutrition partners.

b. Where appropriate, coordinate and collaborate with the project's technical partners as delegated by the Specialist or Project Manager.

c. Relay and contribute to advocacy messages within its scope of work.

d. Write new project content for the continuity or expansion of the project within its technical scope.

e. Contribute to the writing of new proposals for new opportunities within its technical scope.

Mission 5: Emergency Preparedness and Response Responsibilities

Contribute to the support or implementation of emergency preparedness actions of the program(s) and, during an emergency, adapts his/her work modality in order to contribute to an effective HI humanitarian response.

CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:

The situation in Tawilah is relatively calm. There is no conflict at present. The town is relatively isolated; it takes two days by car to reach the Sudanese town near the border with Chad. There are risks of waterborne diseases. The entire security package is up to date and there is a HAS (Security) and a liaison officer present on the base. The route to reach the base goes via: N'djamena (international flight) then NDJ to Adré via UNHAS flights and finally by car to the Geneina’s base (west Darfur). Then, 2 days by road to reach Tawilah. In terms of conditions, the teams are housed in a collective guesthouse, in the same building as our offices.

Requirements

  • You hold a Bachelor’s degree in physiotherapy with Minimum of 2 years of clinical experience in pediatric or physical rehabilitation care;
  • You have a good knowledge of stimulation therapy approach developed by HI;
  • You have a good knowledge of stimulation therapy protocols and national and international nutrition rehabilitation guidelines;
  • You have experience in a humanitarian organization; an experience in working with hospitals and rehabilitation center setting is desirable;
  • You have experience in training trainers’ certification in childhood development stimulation including stimulation therapy;
  • Knowledge of English is essential; Arabic will be an asset;
  • You are able to work in a multidisciplinary team.

Benefits

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission: Join the team

  • 12 months International contract starting from November 1st 2026;
  • The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
    • Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
    • Pension scheme;
    • Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
    • Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
  • Salary from 2345 € gross/month upon experience;
  • Perdiem: 706 € net/month - paid in the field;
  • Hardship: 500 € net/month paid with your salary;
  • Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
  • R&R: 5 days every 8 weeks + possible transport/package support;
  • Position unaccompanied:
    • Payment for travel costs (air ticket & visa) and transport of your personal effects; (from 12 months of mission);
    • Mission of more than 12 months: a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child) paid in the field;
  • Housing: Collective taken in charge by HI;
  • If you are resident in the country: local package.

TO APPLY:

Applications will be processed on an ongoing basis, don’t wait for applying!
Only successful candidates will be contacted.

title: Lead Research Advisor - Conseiller principal en recherche
description:
About the Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages (OCIL)

The Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages is dedicated to promoting and championing Indigenous languages by supporting the efforts of Indigenous Peoples across Canada to reclaim, revitalize, maintain, and strengthen their languages.

Our national team is passionate about our work, and the difference we make with the research, resources and innovation we develop collaboratively with partners and share with Indigenous communities. We have policies in place to ensure a welcoming, safe and respectful workplace, as well as rigorous standards for transparency and accountability.

Our Vision: All Indigenous languages in Canada are safe, vibrant, and thriving.

Our Guiding Principles

  1. There is an urgent need for concerted efforts and investments toward the revitalization of Indigenous languages to arrest and reverse the erosion that has already occurred. Research shows that no Indigenous language in Canada is safe and that all are in varying stages of endangerment.
  2. Indigenous languages are fundamental to the identities, cultures, spirituality, relationships to the land, worldviews, and self-determination of Indigenous peoples.
  3. Indigenous languages have and continue to contribute to the strength of Canada as a whole, including biodiversity and the richness of linguistic and cultural heritage. The Commission is committed to protecting the vitality of all Indigenous languages, including sign languages and sleeping languages.

We welcome interest by qualified candidates as we expand our national team to launch new, exciting projects and to meet growing organizational needs.

About the Role

Reporting to the Manager of the Knowledge Hub, the Lead Research Advisor provides strategic research leadership for the Indigenous Languages Knowledge Hub and supports OCIL's mandate to advance Indigenous language preservation, revitalization, reclamation, and promotion across Canada. The position leads complex research initiatives, develops research frameworks and methodologies, coordinates partnerships, and ensures excellence in support of organizational priorities and legislative obligations.

The Lead Research Advisor works closely with Indigenous communities, governments, academics, language experts, and partners to generate evidence, identify emerging trends, and produce high-quality research that informs policy, programs, and Indigenous language revitalization efforts..

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Research Leadership

  • Lead the design and implementation of national research projects and initiatives.
  • Develop research frameworks, methodologies, standards, and work plans.
  • Provide strategic advice on Indigenous language research trends, priorities, and opportunities.
  • Identify research gaps and emerging issues affecting Indigenous languages and language revitalization.
  • Contribute to the development of annual and multi-year research agendas.
  • Works effectively across teams and contributes to Knowledge Hub and organizational priorities.

Research Project Management



  • Lead and oversee multiple research projects from planning through completion.
  • Coordinate internal and external researchers, consultants, contractors, and partners.
  • Monitor project timelines, budgets, deliverables, and performance measures.
  • Ensure projects align with OCIL priorities, strategic plans, and Indigenous community needs.
  • Support the development of project charters and partnership agreements.

Indigenous Language Research and Analysis

  • Conduct and oversee qualitative, quantitative, and Indigenous methodologies.
  • Synthesize evidence from multiple sources into actionable findings.
  • Analyze trends related to language vitality, demographics, language documentation, mapping, and emerging technologies.
  • Support research related to Indigenous Languages Act reporting requirements.
  • Develop reports, briefing materials, position papers, and recommendations.

Indigenous Data Sovereignty and Governance



  • Promote and apply principles of Indigenous data sovereignty, ownership, access, control, and stewardship.
  • Ensure ethical, culturally appropriate, and community-centered research practices.
  • Advise on research governance frameworks and protocols.
  • Support the respectful collection, management, sharing, and use of Indigenous language data.

Partnerships and Engagement



  • Build and maintain relationships with Indigenous governments, organizations, communities, academic institutions, and research networks.
  • Facilitate collaborative research initiatives and partnerships.
  • Support engagement activities, advisory committees, and knowledge-sharing forums.
  • Represent OCIL at meetings, conferences, and working groups.

Knowledge Mobilization



  • Translate research findings into accessible products for diverse audiences.
  • Support the development of reports, fact sheets, toolkits, dashboards, and knowledge resources.
  • Contribute to public awareness and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
  • Provide strategic advice to support evidence-informed decision-making throughout the organization.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Master's degree in Indigenous Studies, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Linguistics Education, Research Methodology, or a related field.
  • Significant involvement (3 - 5+ years) of progressively responsible experience conducting and leading research initiatives.
  • Experience working alongside Indigenous communities, organizations, governments, or language revitalization initiatives.
  • Experience managing complex projects involving multiple stakeholders and partners.
  • Experience developing research methodologies and leading evidence-based analysis.

Knowledge and Expertise

  • Strong understanding of Indigenous language revitalization, documentation, reclamation, or language policy, including the Indigenous Languages Act and the TRC Calls to Action.
  • Experience with geographic information systems (GIS), digital knowledge repositories, archival research, or emerging technologies.
  • Knowledge of Indigenous data sovereignty frameworks and ethical research standards.

Skills and Competencies

  • Knowledge of Indigenous research methodologies and ethical research practices.
  • Advanced qualitative and quantitative research and analytical skills.
  • Excellent strategic thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Excellent written communication, report writing, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships across diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong facilitation, consultation, and engagement skills.
  • High degree of cultural competency, humility, and respect when working with Indigenous Peoples and communities.

Assets

  • Doctoral degree in a related discipline is an asset.
  • Proficiency in an Indigenous language and bilingualism (English/French).

What We Offer

The Commission offers a competitive benefits package, including medical and dental benefits and a pension plan. The Commission offers a wonderful, supportive work environment, with opportunities for career development, mentorship, and professional development.

The Commission recognizes that our success requires us to have a workforce that reflects the community we serve, and diversity in its widest context, one where all people, regardless of difference, are valued and respected.

Preference will be given to Indigenous applicants in accordance with section 16(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act. Candidates are encouraged to self-identify in their cover letter.

À propos du Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones (OCIL)

Le Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones s'engage à promouvoir et défendre les langues autochtones en soutenant les efforts des peuples autochtones à travers le Canada pour reconquérir, revitaliser, maintenir et renforcer leurs langues.

Notre équipe nationale est passionnée par notre travail et par la différence que nous faisons grâce à la recherche, aux ressources et à l'innovation que nous développons en collaboration avec des partenaires et que nous partageons avec les communautés autochtones. Nous avons mis en place des politiques pour garantir un milieu de travail accueillant, sécuritaire et respectueux, ainsi que des normes rigoureuses de transparence et de responsabilité.

Notre vision : Toutes les langues autochtones au Canada sont sécuritaires, vibrantes et florissantes.

Nos principes directeurs

  1. Il est urgent d'efforts concertés et d'investissements pour la revitalisation des langues autochtones afin d'arrêter et d'inverser l'érosion déjà survenue. Les recherches démontrent qu'aucune langue autochtone au Canada n'est sécuritaire et que toutes sont à différents stades de danger.
  2. Les langues autochtones sont fondamentales pour les identités, les cultures, la spiritualité, les relations avec la terre, les visions du monde et l'autodétermination des peuples autochtones.
  3. Les langues autochtones ont contribué et continuent de contribuer à la force du Canada dans son ensemble, y compris la biodiversité et la richesse du patrimoine linguistique et culturel. La Commission s'engage à protéger la vitalité de toutes les langues autochtones, y compris les langues des signes et les langues du sommeil.

Nous accueillons l'intérêt des candidats qualifiés alors que nous élargissons notre équipe nationale pour lancer de nouveaux projets passionnants et répondre aux besoins organisationnels croissants.

À propos du rôle

Relevant du gestionnaire du Knowledge Hub, le conseiller principal en recherche assure la direction stratégique de la recherche pour les langues autochtones et soutient le mandat de l'OCIL visant à promouvoir la préservation, la revitalisation, la réhabilitation et la promotion des langues autochtones à travers le Canada. Ce poste dirige des initiatives de recherche complexes, développe des cadres et méthodologies de recherche, coordonne les partenariats et assure l'excellence en appui aux priorités organisationnelles et aux obligations législatives.

Le conseiller principal en recherche travaille en étroite collaboration avec les communautés autochtones, les gouvernements, les universitaires, les experts en langues et les partenaires pour générer des preuves, identifier les tendances émergentes et produire des recherches de haute qualité qui éclairent les politiques, les programmes et les efforts de revitalisation des langues autochtones.

Responsabilités clés

Leadership stratégique en recherche

  • Diriger la conception et la mise en œuvre de projets et d'initiatives de recherche nationaux.
  • Développer des cadres de recherche, des méthodologies, des normes et des plans de travail.
  • Fournir des conseils stratégiques sur les tendances, priorités et opportunités de recherche en langues autochtones.
  • Identifier les lacunes en recherche et les enjeux émergents affectant les langues autochtones et la revitalisation des langues.
  • Contribuer à l'élaboration d'agendas de recherche annuels et pluriannuels.
  • Travaille efficacement entre équipes et contribue aux priorités du Knowledge Hub et de l'organisation.

Gestion de projet de recherche



  • Diriger et superviser plusieurs projets de recherche, de la planification à l'achèvement.
  • Coordonnez les chercheurs, consultants, entrepreneurs et partenaires internes et externes.
  • Surveillez les échéanciers du projet, les budgets, les livrables et les mesures de performance.
  • Assurez-vous que les projets sont alignés avec les priorités de l'OCIL, les plans stratégiques et les besoins des communautés autochtones.
  • Soutenez l'élaboration de chartes de projet et d'ententes de partenariat.

Recherche et analyse des langues autochtones

  • Mener et superviser les méthodologies qualitatives, quantitatives et autochtones.
  • Synthétiser des preuves provenant de multiples sources en résultats exploitables.
  • Analyser les tendances liées à la vitalité linguistique, à la démographie, à la documentation linguistique, à la cartographie et aux technologies émergentes.
  • Soutenez la recherche liée aux exigences de déclaration en vertu de la Loi sur les langues autochtones.
  • Élaborez des rapports, des documents d'information, des documents de position et des recommandations.

Souveraineté et gouvernance des données autochtones



  • Promouvoir et appliquer les principes de souveraineté, de propriété, d'accès, de contrôle et de gestion des données autochtones.
  • Assurer des pratiques de recherche éthiques, culturellement appropriées et centrées sur la communauté.
  • Conseiller sur les cadres et protocoles de gouvernance de la recherche.
  • Soutenez la collecte, la gestion, le partage et l'utilisation respectueux des données sur les langues autochtones.

Partenariats et engagement



  • Bâtir et maintenir des relations avec les gouvernements, organisations, communautés, institutions académiques et réseaux de recherche autochtones.
  • Faciliter des initiatives de recherche collaborative et des partenariats.
  • Soutenir les activités d'engagement, les comités consultatifs et les forums de partage des connaissances.
  • Représenter l'OCIL lors de réunions, conférences et groupes de travail.

Mobilisation des connaissances



  • Traduire les résultats de la recherche en produits accessibles pour des publics diversifiés.
  • Soutenir le développement de rapports, fiches d'information, trousses d'outils, tableaux de bord et ressources de connaissances.
  • Contribuer à la sensibilisation du public et aux initiatives de partage des connaissances.
  • Fournir des conseils stratégiques pour soutenir la prise de décision fondée sur des preuves à travers l'organisation.

Qualifications

Éducation et expérience

  • Maîtrise en études autochtones, sciences sociales, politiques publiques, éducation linguistique, méthodologie de recherche ou domaine connexe.
  • Une implication significative (3 à 5+ ans) d'une expérience de plus en plus responsable dans la conduite et la direction d'initiatives de recherche.
  • Expérience de travail aux côtés de communautés autochtones, d'organisations, de gouvernements ou d'initiatives de revitalisation linguistique.
  • Expérience de la gestion de projets complexes impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes et partenaires.
  • Expérience dans le développement de méthodologies de recherche et la direction d'analyses fondées sur des preuves.

Connaissances et expertise

  • Une solide compréhension de la revitalisation, de la documentation, de la réhabilitation ou de la politique linguistique des langues autochtones, y compris la Loi sur les langues autochtones et les appels à l'action de la CVR.
  • Expérience avec les systèmes d'information géographique (SIG), les dépôts de connaissances numériques, la recherche archivistique ou les technologies émergentes.
  • Connaissance des cadres de souveraineté des données autochtones et des normes éthiques de recherche.

Compétences et aptitudes

  • Connaissance des méthodologies de recherche autochtones et des pratiques éthiques de recherche.
  • Compétences avancées en recherche qualitative et quantitative ainsi qu'en analyse.
  • Excellentes capacités de pensée stratégique et de résolution de problèmes.
  • Solides compétences en gestion de projet et organisationnelle.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite, en rédaction de rapports et en présentation.
  • Capacité à bâtir des relations collaboratives entre divers groupes de parties prenantes.
  • Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités dans un environnement rapide.
  • Solides compétences en facilitation, consultation et engagement.
  • Un haut degré de compétence culturelle, d'humilité et de respect lorsqu'il s'agit de travailler avec les peuples autochtones et les communautés.

Actifs

  • Un doctorat dans une discipline connexe est un atout.
  • Maîtrise d'une langue autochtone et bilinguisme (anglais/français).

Ce que nous offrons

La Commission offre un ensemble d'avantages sociaux compétitif, incluant des prestations médicales et dentaires ainsi qu'un régime de pension. La Commission offre un environnement de travail merveilleux et bienveillant, avec des occasions de développement de carrière, de mentorat et de développement professionnel.

La Commission reconnaît que notre succès exige que nous ayons une main-d'œuvre qui reflète la communauté que nous servons, et la diversité dans son contexte le plus large, où toutes les personnes, peu importe leurs différences, sont valorisées et respectées.

La préférence sera accordée aux demandeurs autochtones conformément à l'article 16(1) de la Loi canadienne sur les droits de la personne. Les candidats sont encouragés à s'identifier dans leur lettre de motivation.

title: F&B Crew
description:
MORROW HEALTH

MORROW Health is Singapore’s largest integrated fitness and recovery destination, designed to help individuals build healthier, more resilient lives through intentional daily habits. Grounded in lifestyle medicine, MORROW Health brings together physical activity, nutrition, restorative sleep, stress management, avoidance of risky substances, and social connection through structured programmes and purpose-built environments that make sustainable lifestyle change achievable. Supported by evidence-informed practice and data from wearables and lifestyle inputs, MORROW Health helps members recognise patterns, build consistency, and stay accountable—turning insight into everyday action that supports long-term vitality, strength, and clarity, without medical diagnosis or treatment.

Location: Singapore
Reports To: F&B Manager

Role Summary

At MORROW, service is both a privilege and a calling. As a Nutrition Ambassador, you are not just part of the service team — you are the storyteller of our food philosophy, the connector between our nutrition pillars and our members’ daily choices. Every dish and drink is thoughtfully curated, and your role is to bring that ethos to life through excellent service, authentic engagement, and deep knowledge of what we offer.

This role requires ownership, collaboration, and agility. You will play a key part in creating memorable dining experiences while also stepping into other guest-facing roles as needed, ensuring seamless support across MORROW’s member journey.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide warm, attentive, and professional service, ensuring members feel welcomed and supported.
  • Act as a spokesperson for MORROW’s nutrition pillars, explaining how dishes and drinks are curated to support health and lifestyle goals.
  • Represent F&B offerings in cooking classes, demonstrations, or educational touchpoints, inspiring members through knowledge and engagement.
  • Take and deliver orders with accuracy and consistency, always mindful of dietary preferences.
  • Maintain hygiene, cleanliness, and operational standards of the highest quality.
  • Manage guest flow, reservations, and service recovery with professionalism.
  • Collaborate closely with teammates across all zones to ensure a seamless and integrated member experience.
  • Support other customer service functions when needed, demonstrating agility and teamwork.
  • Embody MORROW’s values by showing up with excellence, taking ownership, and uplifting the team culture.

Requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in hospitality, restaurants, or member clubs.
  • Valid food hygiene certification.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills with an ability to engage and educate guests.
  • Passion for wellness, nutrition, and service.
  • Knowledge (or willingness to learn) of MORROW’s full offerings and the role F&B plays in supporting the nutrition pillar.
  • Collaborative spirit and agility to adapt to changing guest traffic and operational needs.

Benefits

This is a career-defining opportunity to shape the future of longevity medicine while working alongside world-class clinicians and technologists. You will contribute to initiatives that directly lead to extending human healthspan while establishing Singapore as the global hub for longevity innovation.


At MORROW, you will not only help define operational excellence but also build the culture, rhythm, and future of interventions. You won't just be joining a team. You will be co-creating tomorrow.

MORROW Health Pte Ltd is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

title: Principal Engineer, Signal and Power Integrity
location: San Diego, California, United States of America
description:
Company:

Qualcomm Technologies, Inc.

Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Packaging Engineering

General Summary:

As a Qualcomm Package System Design and Technology Engineer, you will drive new advanced package technology development, concept design architecture analysis from package to system, new generation product package structure selection, package system design by multi-physics simulation analysis, multi-physics lab validation/correlation of package to system models, and the manufacturing qualification for new product introduction (NPI). Package System Design and Technology Engineers collaborate with multi-disciplinary teams to achieve optimized performance of mechanical, electrical, and thermal package systems for various end market applications. This role interfaces with internal/external IP teams, industry standards, and vendors to set package to system design and technology specifications; enabling product designs to achieve high performance, high reliability, low cost, and easy to implement system with integrated component attaches for end customers.

The candidate will work in a team-oriented, professional engineering environment to perform a variety of signal and power integrity tasks and collaborate with package and IC designers to optimize the overall package design. Electrical model extraction and signal and power integrity simulations will constitute the majority of the tasks. This engineer must interface with a variety of board, package, and IC designers. Working effectively across organizational boundaries is essential, as is effective documentation and presentation of results. This candidate will work on high-speed memory interfaces for electrical model extraction and system-level simulation.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform various IO analyses using established methodologies, potentially from model extraction through simulation and reporting of conclusions. IO types include a variety of memory interfaces.
  • Apply established methodologies to analyze IO power distribution in product development and reference systems.
  • Perform package extraction for time domain and frequency domain analysis and provide design guidelines for the package design.
  • Create clear and complete documentation of results.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in DDR in Package/PCB/System Design related to compute/server standards.
  • Experience in electromagnetics and a solid background in transmission line theory and crosstalk.
  • Proficiency in field solvers such as HFSS, Q3D, Sentinel-PSI, and Clarity, and SPICE transient simulation (ADS, Hspice), including use of IBIS and IBIS AMI models.
  • Experience in DDR design specifications such as DDR and LPDDR
  • Experience in Matlab to automate existing simulation flow.
  • Experience in programming languages (C/C++) or scripting languages (Perl/Python) is a plus.
  • Master’s or Ph.D. degree with 3+ years of industry experience.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field and 8+ years of System/Package Design/Technology Engineering or related work experience.
OR
Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field and 7+ years of System/Package Design/Technology Engineering or related work experience.
OR
PhD in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field and 6+ year of System/Package Design/Technology Engineering or related work experience.

title: GROUNDS MAINTENANCE
description:
Landscapes Golf Management and Settler's Hill Golf Course are seeking a Grounds Maintenance team members for the upcoming golf season. These are seasonal positions with full time hours available during the season.


The present location of Settler's Hill Golf Course is on the site of the old County Farm and Home. The Home site itself had several buildings, the home, administration building, power plant, maintenance building, corn crib and dairy barn, plus other out-structures such as machine sheds and animal shed, but the only ones that still exist are the power house, maintenance building, corn crib and the dairy barn. The dairy barn was remodeled and is currently used as a club house. The corn crib and the maintenance building are used to store equipment for use on the course.

Our Values Bring Us Together; Our Expertise Sets Us Apart. We at LGM believe these values are instrumental to our daily operations.

LGM Values: Do the Right Thing, Take Care of Each Other, Find a Way, Lead, Be the Best


JOB SUMMARY

Responsible for performing the tasks associated with the daily maintenance of the golf course, associated grounds, and project implementation.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

The essential functions include, but are not limited to the following:

  1. Promotes, works and acts in a manner consistent with the values of LGM.
  2. Operates mowing equipment; mows greens, tees, fairways, rough, bunker banks and native grass.
  3. Performs bunker maintenance; rakes and moves sand, edges, and pulls weeds.
  4. Ensures that all areas around trees, bunkers, cart paths, signs and other golf course features are maintained and edged.
  5. Installs and maintains landscaping plant material and performs all associated landscaping duties.
  6. Assists with the repairs and maintenance of the irrigation system features.
  7. Performs golf course set up; cup cutting, tee cleanup, divot filling, ball mark repair, trash and debris removal, and golf ball washer maintenance.
  8. Cleans, fuels, and stores equipment after each use. Refreshes oil and other lubricants as directed by the equipment technician. Reports equipment problems promptly to the appropriate supervisor.
  9. Possesses an understanding of the equipment and how to best maintain it for maximum life and minimum downtime.
  10. Complies with golf course etiquette rules.
  11. Must be well mannered, display a smile at all times, greet guests, member and fellow employees when encountered, show appreciation to the guests and the members, and demonstrate a willingness to help guests and members at all times.
  12. Possesses and understanding of the importance of safety and sees that safe operation procedures are observed in all daily activities. Adheres to the safety program.
  13. Demonstrates a commitment to the work and success of the club and the Company by being service- and solution-oriented, having positive interactions with all club staff and members/guests, and meeting established quality, service and safety expectations.
  14. Performs additional assignments per the direction of club or Company managers.
  15. Regular and punctual attendance on site for all scheduled shifts is required.

WORK HOURS AND CONDITIONS

Work hours may include early mornings and evenings on weekdays, weekends and holidays. Subject to inside and outside environmental conditions. May be exposed to inclement (non-threatening) weather, plant protection products, fertilizers, misdirected golf balls, and sharp and rapid equipment movement on a daily basis. Injury may result as a result of exposure to the above if safety policies and practices are not properly followed.

  • Lead construction operations for multiple residential rowhome rehabilitation projects across West Baltimore.
  • Manage, mentor, and grow a diverse construction team while fostering a collaborative culture.

  • Competitive salary in the range of $100,000 to $150,000, depending on experience.
