title: Senior RF Engineer
description:
At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve successfully transitioned quantum computing from an academic dream into a commercial reality. The most exciting thing is that we’re just getting started.

The Mission

As a Senior RF Engineer, you will design, develop, and optimise the RF systems that underpin OQC’s quantum computing platform. Working at the intersection of cutting-edge hardware, systems engineering, and quantum technology, you'll solve complex RF challenges that improve the performance, reliability, and scalability of our quantum computers.

The Role

You'll be a technical specialist within our Advanced Product Development team, leading the design and validation of RF and microwave solutions that enable quantum control and readout. Working closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams, you'll take ownership of RF hardware development from concept through to deployment, helping shape the future of commercially viable quantum computing.

What You'll Be Working On

  • Architecting and delivering RF control, readout, and packaging solutions that meet demanding system performance requirements.
  • Designing, simulating, testing, and optimising RF and microwave circuitry using modelling tools and laboratory-based experimentation.
  • Leading RF characterisation activities, including microwave I/O analysis, filtering design, signal-to-noise optimisation, and performance validation.
  • Investigating complex technical issues, driving root-cause analysis, and implementing data-led design improvements.
  • Collaborating with hardware, systems, and cryogenic engineering teams to ensure successful integration across the quantum computing stack.
  • Managing technical engagement with RF suppliers, evaluating components, and supporting hardware quality assurance activities.
  • Providing technical leadership, mentoring engineers, and contributing to roadmap planning, delivery forecasting, and engineering best practices.

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience developing RF and microwave hardware solutions.
  • Strong RF design, simulation, and modelling expertise.
  • Experience with RF laboratory testing, validation, and characterisation methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to solve complex technical and system integration challenges independently.
  • Experience working across multidisciplinary engineering environments.
  • Strong data analysis, stakeholder communication, and technical documentation skills.
  • Ability to balance technical trade-offs, risk, manufacturability, and performance requirements.
  • Experience engaging with suppliers and technical partners.
  • Technical leadership capability, including project ownership and mentoring of engineers.
  • Degree in Electronics, Physics, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

The 'Nice-to-Haves'

  • Postgraduate qualification in RF Engineering, Microwave Engineering, Electronics, Physics, or a related discipline.
  • Experience leading complex technical projects or work packages.
  • Experience within advanced technology, research, or highly regulated environments.
  • Knowledge of project planning, risk analysis, and process improvement methodologies.
  • Python scripting experience.
  • Strong influencing, adaptability, creativity, and leadership skills.

Why Join OQC

You will join a world-class team at the forefront of the next computational era. We offer a culture of bold innovation, the chance to work with unique lab infrastructure, and the opportunity to see your work redefine the limits of computation.

Learn more about our benefits and positive work culture here:

Interviews will commence from the 18th June.

READ Foundation is a UK based registered charity working to provide access to quality education to vulnerable children in our regions of work. title: Customer Logistics Co-ordinator
description:
Build your career in logistics with Highland Spring

Are you organised, comfortable working with customers and colleagues, and interested in developing a career in logistics or supply chain?

We’re looking for a Customer Logistics Coordinator to join our Supply Chain team at our Blackford site. This is a great opportunity for someone relatively early in their career who wants to build practical experience across customer service, logistics and supply chain within Highland Spring.

You don’t need to have spent years working in logistics. You may already have some experience in customer service, administration, order processing, transport or supply chain, or you may be looking for an opportunity to take your next step into the sector.

You’ll be at the centre of our day-to-day logistics operation, helping to make sure Highland Spring products get from our warehouses to our customers accurately and on time. The role offers a salary of £28,615.59 and is based at our Blackford site, working 37.5 hours per week as part of our Supply Chain team.

What you’ll be doing

Working closely with our Customer Supply Chain Coordinators, hauliers and third-party logistics partners, you’ll help keep orders moving and make sure our customers receive the service they expect.

You’ll coordinate customer orders, making sure they are allocated and ready for collection and delivery at the right time. You’ll work with our hauliers and third-party warehouses to arrange and monitor deliveries, check that orders have been processed accurately through our systems, and investigate any shipping or delivery issues that arise.

You’ll also support the team with haulage information, purchase orders and invoices, keep customer service and logistics trackers up to date, and help monitor our On Time In Full (OTIF) performance.

As you develop in the role, you’ll gain experience of the systems, processes and relationships that help keep a busy supply chain running smoothly.

What we’re looking for

We’re not expecting you to know everything from day one.

What matters most is that you’re organised, dependable and keen to learn. You’ll enjoy working with different people, communicate clearly and take pride in getting the details right.

You should be comfortable using Microsoft Office and confident learning new systems as part of the role. You’ll also need to be able to manage different priorities, solve problems and work well as part of a team.

Experience within FMCG, logistics or working with hauliers would be useful, but it isn’t essential. A background in customer service or administration could give you many of the transferable skills you need to succeed here.

How we work

At Highland Spring, how we work together matters just as much as what we deliver.

We’re a Team – we help each other, listen to others and work together to solve problems.

We’re Proud – we take ownership of our work, do what we say we will do and look for ways to keep improving.

We Care – we treat people fairly and respectfully, support our customers and colleagues, and recognise that everyone has a voice.

If you’re looking for a role where you can learn, build your experience and develop a career in logistics and supply chain, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is seeking a hands‑on Sr. Software Engineer to drive end‑to‑end solution delivery for major retail platforms.

In this role, you will own hands‑on implementation (feature development, technical design, code reviews), engagement leadership (client‑facing technical lead, trade‑off decisions, mentoring), and operational ownership (delivery sign‑off, post‑release support) of high‑impact solutions, translating business requirements into working software you help build.

You will drive Dual‑Track Agile processes, contributing to the Discovery Track through rapid prototyping and feasibility validation, and leading the Delivery Track to ensure quality, traceability, and measurable outcomes. The ideal candidate is a senior software engineer who codes daily, prototypes proactively, and integrates AI/agent workflows across the software lifecycle—from analysis and design to testing, documentation, and code generation—while bringing the technical leadership to drive client engagements forward. You will mentor teams, make critical technical trade‑offs, and take full accountability for delivery sign‑off and post‑release support. This role requires strong retail platform domain knowledge (POS systems, store operations), cloud‑native development experience, and fluency with generative and agentic AI tools to accelerate delivery while preserving code quality and architectural integrity. You will be a key driver of engineering excellence, ensuring solutions are both innovative and operationally robust.

Key Responsibilities

Instrument and leverage AI/agentic workflows in your daily development to accelerate design, prototyping, code generation, test‑case creation, specification drafting, and automated validation across the software lifecycle. Apply AI‑assisted development practices in your own work, model best practices for the team, and ensure ethical compliance and responsible integration of generative AI tools. Own end‑to‑end solution delivery across Discovery and Delivery Tracks, personally building validated prototypes, contributing to formal designs, decomposing work into deliverables, and shipping accepted technical implementations. Drive the Discovery Track under Dual‑Track Agile by writing working prototypes and demoing solutions to validate feasibility and align stakeholders before full implementation. Translate discovery outcomes into delivery backlog items and partner with implementation teams to ensure design intent, code quality standards, and non‑functional requirements are preserved throughout delivery. Contribute to technical design across products and integrations: produce ADRs, interface contracts, data models, sequencing diagrams, migration/rollback plans, and traceability matrices, partnering with architects on broader governance. Serve as the primary technical lead in client engagements: facilitate workshops, present technical solutions, make trade‑off decisions, drive approvals, and act as a subject‑matter expert for assigned platform areas. Personally implement critical components and complex features in modern retail platform stacks, set the bar for code quality through your own work, and review and approve deliverables from implementation teams. Apply and reinforce engineering standards, reusable integration patterns, and non‑functional requirements (security, scalability, observability) across client solutions. Mentor and upskill engineers on AI‑assisted development, Dual‑Track workflows, specification‑driven design, and platform best practices, primarily through pair programming, code reviews, and example‑driven leadership. Contribute to platform and product strategy, identifying reusable assets, API‑first designs, and technical gaps requiring investment. Own risk analysis and mitigation for technical decisions, including backward compatibility, data integrity, and compliance constraints.

Must‑Have Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience. Applying and utilizing AI‑assisted tools and workflows (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) for design, coding, test generation, and documentation. 8+ years of professional software development experience with current, daily hands‑on coding and prototyping in modern technology stacks.

5+ years building cloud‑native, microservices, or event‑driven systems, with experience in Azure or equivalent cloud platforms. Strong proficiency in technology stacks such as Java/Spring Boot, TypeScript, React/Vue.

Proven experience owning end‑to‑end solution delivery, including design, implementation, and post‑release operational accountability for medium‑to‑large projects. Track record of building production code, prototypes, and reference implementations to validate solutionfeasibility. Strong experience with REST/OpenAPI, messaging platforms, and relational/non‑relational databases (SQL/NoSQL).

Hands‑on proficiency with CI/CD, containerization, Docker, Kubernetes, deployment tooling, automated testing, and AI/agentic workflows to accelerate the software lifecycle. Practical experience with generative AI and AI‑assisted development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor) with measurable impact on delivery. Excellent stakeholder communication skills, able to facilitate workshops, present technical solutions, and collaborate across business and engineering teams. Proven leadership in mentoring engineers, conducting thorough code reviews, and championing engineering best practices across teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Strong retail platform domain knowledge (POS systems, store operations) is highly desirable. Certifications such as Azure Developer Associate, Azure Solutions Architect, or equivalent cloud credentials.

Strong understanding of advanced security best practices and compliance requirements in enterprise systems. Experience leading Dual‑Track Agile processes, managing both Discovery and Delivery Tracks, and translating discovery outcomes into actionable backlog items.

Experience contributing to platform strategy, reusable assets, and API‑first designs. Expertise in formal or machine‑readable specifications (Open API, UML+OCL, TLA+, or equivalent) to guide implementation and enable automated validation.

About Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions

Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions is a dynamic billion‑dollar global company based in Research Triangle Park, NC, providing retail store solutions to your favorite brands.

As set forth in Toshiba Global Commerce Solutions - External’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy,we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

If you believe you belong to any of the categories of protected veterans listed below, please indicate by making the appropriate selection.As a government contractor subject to the Vietnam Era Veterans Readjustment Assistance Act (VEVRAA), we request this information in order to measurethe effectiveness of the outreach and positive recruitment efforts we undertake pursuant to VEVRAA. Classification of protected categoriesis as follows:

A "disabled veteran" is one of the following: a veteran of the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service who is entitled to compensation (or who but for the receipt of military retired pay would be entitled to compensation) under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs; or a person who was discharged or released from active duty because of a service‑connected disability.

A "recently separated veteran" means any veteran during the three‑year period beginning on the date of such veteran's discharge or release from active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval, or air service.

An "active duty wartime or campaign badge veteran" means a veteran who served on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service during a war, or in a campaign or expedition for which a campaign badge has been authorized under the laws administered by the Department of Defense.

An "Armed forces service medal veteran" means a veteran who, while serving on active duty in the U.S. military, ground, naval or air service, participated in a United States military operation for which an Armed Forces service medal was awarded pursuant to Executive Order 12985.

We are a federal contractor or subcontractor. The law requires us to provide equal employment opportunity to qualified people with disabilities. We have a goal of having at least 7% of our workers as people with disabilities. The law says we must measure our progress towards this goal. To do this, we must ask applicants and employees if they have a disability or have ever had one. People can become disabled, so we need to ask this question at least every five years.

Completing this form is voluntary, and we hope that you will choose to do so. Your answer is confidential. No one who makes hiring decisions will see it. Your decision to complete the form and your answer will not harm you in any way. If you want to learn more about the law or this form, visit the U.S. Department of Labor’s Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) website at www.dol.gov/ofccp .

How do you know if you have a disability?

A disability is a condition that substantially limits one or more of your “major life activities.” If you have or have ever had such a condition, you are a person with a disability. Disabilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Alcohol or other substance use disorder (not currently using drugs illegally)
  • Autoimmune disorder, for example, lupus, fibromyalgia, rheumatoid arthritis, HIV/AIDS
  • Blind or low vision
  • Cancer (past or present)
  • Cardiovascular or heart disease
  • Celiac disease
  • Cerebral palsy

  • Diabetes

  • Gastrointestinal disorders, for example, Crohn's Disease, irritable bowel syndrome
  • Intellectual or developmental disability
  • Mental health conditions, for example, depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorder, schizophrenia, PTSD
  • Missing limbs or partially missing limbs
  • Mobility impairment, benefiting from the use of a wheelchair, scooter, walker, leg brace(s) and/or other supports
  • Nervous system condition, for example, migraine headaches, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis (MS)
  • Neurodivergence, for example, attention‑deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), autism spectrum disorder, dyslexia, dyspraxia, other learning disabilities
  • Partial or complete paralysis (any cause)

title: New Grad Full-Time Quantitative Trader

description:

Proprietary trading firm based in New York City is seeking a highly motivated New Graduate Quantitative Trader to join the team full-time. In this role, you will apply analytical thinking and market intuition to pricing, execution, and risk decisions as part of the firm's quantitative trading team.

- Reason through pricing, risk, and execution decisions.

title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
description:
MORROW Health

MORROW Health is Singapore’s largest integrated fitness and recovery destination, designed to help individuals build healthier, more resilient lives through intentional daily habits. Grounded in lifestyle medicine, MORROW Health brings together physical activity, nutrition, restorative sleep, stress management, avoidance of risky substances, and social connection through structured programmes and purpose-built environments that make sustainable lifestyle change achievable.   • Leverage AI-assisted development tools (such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor or similar) as a core part of the daily workflow, from code generation and refactoring to test writing and documentation.
  • Apply sound judgment over AI-generated code: review, validate and take full ownership of everything shipped to production.
  • Contribute to architecture decisions, technical design reviews and the long-term health of the codebase.
  • Write automated tests (unit, integration, end-to-end) and maintain high standards of code quality through code reviews and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Deploy, monitor and troubleshoot services in cloud environments (AWS/Azure/GCP), including containerised workloads.

  • Optimise application performance, reliability and scalability as the user base grows.
  • Integrate third-party services, devices and data sources (such as payments, wearables and messaging) as required by the product roadmap.
  • Collaborate closely with the Product Manager and Designer from discovery through delivery, providing effort estimates and technical input on feasibility.
  • Support production operations, including participation in incident response and on-call arrangements where needed.
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to engineering standards, documentation and best practices as the team grows.
  • Stay current with emerging technologies, frameworks and AI coding workflows, and bring practical improvements to the team.

Requirements

  • At least 7 years of professional software development experience, including production experience across the full stack.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and modern JavaScript/TypeScript.
  • Strong hands-on experience with React and modern frontend development practices.
  • Solid experience with both relational and NoSQL databases, ideally MySQL and MongoDB, including schema design and query optimisation.
  • Demonstrated fluency with AI-assisted coding tools and workflows in daily development, with the judgment to review and own AI-generated code.
  • Experience designing and consuming APIs (REST or GraphQL).
  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure or GCP), Docker and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Good understanding of software security fundamentals; familiarity with healthcare data privacy requirements (PDPA or equivalent) is an advantage.
  • Experience with automated testing and maintaining quality in a fast-moving codebase.
  • Experience in healthtech, digital health or another regulated space is an advantage.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills across technical and non-technical teams.

Benefits

Why Join Us
This is a career-defining opportunity to shape the future of longevity medicine while working alongside world-class clinicians and technologists. You will contribute to initiatives that directly lead to extending human healthspan while establishing Singapore as the global hub for longevity innovation.

At MORROW, you will not only help define operational excellence but also build the culture, rhythm, and future of interventions. You won't just be joining a team. You will be co-creating tomorrow.

MORROW Health Pte Ltd is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.

title: Local Content Associate
description:
Company Background

Tetra Maritime is the Nigerian operating platform of Union Maritime Limited, an international shipping group established in 2006 with offices across four continents. Union Maritime operates a diversified fleet of circa 100 vessels across the tanker and dry bulk sectors, with a strong presence in the clean products and light chemical markets. Tetra serves as the group’s principal presence in Nigeria, supporting its vessels and cargoes across Nigerian and West African trades. This role is based in Abuja to keep Tetra close to the government bodies, regulators and agencies that are central to its activities in the country.

The Position

We are looking for a proactive and well-connected Local Content Associate to represent Tetra Maritime and the wider Union Maritime group on the ground in Abuja. Working closely with the operations and documentation teams in Lagos and the commercial team in London, the role is hands-on and mobile: meeting government officials, keeping document approvals and permits on track, building and maintaining relationships across the sector, and keeping the group informed of developments in the Nigerian oil and gas market. It will suit an energetic and personable individual who is comfortable moving between government offices and agencies to get things done, and who can represent the group credibly and professionally in-country.

Key responsibilities will include:

· Act as Tetra Maritime’s local point of contact in Abuja, meeting regularly with government officials, regulators and authorities – including bodies such as NIMASA, the Nigerian Ports Authority and Nigerian Customs – as well as agencies, oil majors, terminals, agents and local partners.

· Prepare, submit and follow up on documentation, permits and approvals, making sure they are progressed and completed on time and that the group stays compliant with Nigerian maritime and trade regulation, including Cabotage, Local Content and customs requirements.

· Develop and maintain strong relationships across government bodies, partners and stakeholders in Nigeria, representing the group’s interests credibly and professionally in-country.

· Monitor developments in the Nigerian oil and gas sector and keep the group updated on new opportunities, regulatory changes and market developments.

Requirements

The successful candidate will be expected to demonstrate the following:

· A good working knowledge of Nigerian government processes, approvals and Local Content requirements, and confidence navigating the relevant authorities and agencies.

· An established network among Nigerian authorities, agencies, oil and gas and industry contacts, or the proven ability to build one quickly.

· Willingness to travel frequently and move between government offices and agencies across Abuja and the wider country.

· A relevant degree or equivalent practical experience, ideally with a background in government liaison, regulatory affairs, documentation or compliance within shipping, oil and gas, logistics or a related sector.

Skills:

· Strong relationship-building, communication and negotiation skills, able to build trust with regulators, authorities, partners and internal group functions.

· Good organisation and time management, with the ability to keep multiple approvals, deadlines and priorities on track at once.

· Clear, credible written and verbal communication, with proficiency in Microsoft Office.

Qualities:

· Proactive, resourceful and comfortable working independently and solving problems on the ground.

· Reliable, with exceptional attention to detail and high standards of accuracy across documentation and reporting.

· Resilient and adaptable, staying composed amid the unpredictability of the industry and the local operating context.

· Honest, professional and trustworthy, demonstrating integrity and ethical conduct in all dealings with officials and partners.

title: Program Assistant
description:
About Mission Bit

Mission Bit is a San Francisco-based nonprofit that equips youth with hands-on computer science and AI education that builds confidence, technical skills, and pathways to meaningful careers in technology. We serve public high school students who've historically had limited access to tech and tech careers through semester-long coding courses, self-paced learning, workshops, and more.

The role

The Program Assistant of Tech Start and Alumni Initiatives supports program coordination, participant case management, and community engagement. This role helps organize workshops and events, manage participant communications and records, connect young people with career-development resources, and engage alumni. This role reports directly to the Director of Programs.

We’re looking for someone who is highly organized, proactive, dependable, and a clear communicator. The ideal candidate is comfortable working with data, learning new tools, and supporting young people as they pursue education and careers in technology.

This is a hybrid, temporary, part-time role based in San Francisco, CA, starting from date of hire through June 30, 2027. In-person work is required at least two times a week, depending on the program schedule. In-person work will include travel to the office and around the Bay Area.

Schedule

  • 20 hours/week
  • Monday through Thursday, some Fridays, evenings, or weekends occasionally required
  • Typically 5-7 hour shifts, between the business hours of 9:00 AM - 7:00 PM
    • Hours may vary based on the semester and organizational needs. Flexibility to adjust the schedule as needed.

Duration

  • Date of hire through June 30, 2027

What you’ll be doing

Program Coordination

  • Assist the Director of Programs in scheduling, coordinating, and executing workshops, events, and program activities
  • Prepare program materials, including agendas, slide decks, and handouts, in advance of each session
  • Draft and send routine communications such as participant reminders, surveys, and partner updates
  • Track program materials and office inventory, and assist with supply prep and distribution
  • Participate in and support Mission Bit activities and events as needed

Tech Start Program Support

  • Coordinate participant recruitment, enrollment, and onboarding for each Tech Start cohort, including collecting forms, communicating logistics, and supporting orientation
  • Moderate virtual and in-person workshops and events, supporting smooth facilitation, day-of setup, troubleshooting, and coordination with external partners at Mission Bit HQ
  • Liaise with industry volunteers, panelists, and mentor matches to confirm availability, share logistics, and support a positive participant experience across all workshops
  • Coordinate distribution of participant benefits (e.g., LinkedIn Premium and Vercel Premium access) for each enrolled cohort
  • Track and maintain accurate participant records, including Individual Employment Plans, attendance, and survey responses, and enter data into required systems no later than the 10th of each month
  • Monitor cohort progress toward completion and placement targets, flag updates to the Director of Programs, and assist in collecting program metrics — including attendance trends and participant demographics — to support quarterly grant reporting and continuous improvement

Case Management

  • Conduct regular check-in calls with Tech Start participants to monitor their progress, address barriers, and ensure they remain on track toward program completion and placement goals
  • Maintain detailed case notes for each participant, documenting phone calls, key updates, and any follow-up actions taken
  • Flag participants who are at risk of dropping off to the Director of Programs and coordinate appropriate support or interventions
  • Track participant milestones and outcomes post-program, including placement in employment, education, or training, and document accordingly
  • Serve as a consistent point of contact for participants throughout their time in the program and during the alumni transition
  • Support participants and alumni in accessing career development resources, including internship and job opportunities, skill building, and ongoing career guidance
  • Work closely with the Programs team to build and maintain career partnerships

Alumni Initiatives

  • Maintain and grow the Mission Bit Alumni Network by identifying and curating events, opportunities, internships, and resources to share via the alumni newsletter and LinkedIn group
  • Draft and schedule regular alumni communications, including newsletters, event announcements, and engagement check-ins
  • Support coordination of the Student Ambassador Board, including scheduling meetings and maintaining follow-up communications
  • Assist in connecting alumni to Tech Start programming as mentors, panelists, or volunteers

Requirements

We’d love to hear from you if you have…

  • Demonstrated interest or experience in education, workforce development, or youth-serving programs
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple deadlines
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication skills
  • Comfortable working with data and keeping detailed records
  • Experience with Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Calendar) and comfort learning new tools
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team
  • Familiarity with communities Mission Bit serves, underrepresented young people in San Francisco, is a plus

It’s not required, but it’s a nice bonus if you…

  • Experience with Salesforce, Notion, and Slack
  • Experience with WorkForce Central
  • Prior experience supporting workshops, events, or program coordination

Benefits

Compensation

  • $25/hr

Benefits

  • Accrued sick time-off

Mission Bit is an equal opportunity employer that does not discriminate on the basis of actual or perceived race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, pregnancy, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, familial status, domestic violence victim status, veteran or military status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

title: Real Estate Investment Associate
description:
Roseau Ford is building a portfolio of residential-scale senior living communities — senior coliving and cohousing — designed for upper-income residents who want connection, autonomy, and community at home. We’re a small, high-trust team at an early stage of growth, and this is a foundational role. You’ll touch every part of the business — from sourcing and underwriting acquisition targets to structuring deals with lenders, and from coordinating architects and contractors to managing resident experience and community programming. As the portfolio scales, you’ll have the opportunity to grow into the function that best fits your strengths, whether that’s on the investment and capital side or the property and community side. Both are strategic to what we’re building. You’ll work directly with the principal and senior partners across multiple projects simultaneously.

What you’ll do

Acquisitions & deal sourcing

  • Source acquisition opportunities against a defined buy box using MLS, off-market channels, and direct outreach
  • Conduct preliminary property analysis and filter candidates against investment criteria
  • Initiate and manage seller communications to gather preliminary information, rent rolls, and expense history
  • Draft letters of intent for principal review and signature

Financial analysis & deal structuring

  • Build and maintain pro formas for acquisition and development projects
  • Track NOI, DSCR, and returns assumptions across the portfolio
  • Structure loan terms with lenders and prepare lender packages
  • Coordinate due diligence, manage third-party reporting timelines, and support closing execution from accepted LOI through funding

Project coordination

  • Serve as a coordination point between architects, contractors, and vendors across active projects
  • Track schedules and deliverables; flag issues early
  • Manage document flow and approvals across active projects

Property management support

  • Support day-to-day rental operations including lease tracking and resident communications
  • Coordinate vendors and triage maintenance issues
  • Help evaluate and interface with third-party operators

Resident experience & programming

  • Help design and coordinate community programming and activities for senior residents
  • Develop resident onboarding materials, community agreements, and engagement touchpoints
  • Think holistically about what makes a home feel like a community

Operations & process building

  • Help create SOPs, workflows, and playbooks as the portfolio grows
  • Document what works; identify gaps
  • Build systems that allow the team to scale without adding complexity

Requirements

Experience

2–5 years across real estate, property management, development, or hospitality. Direct experience building pro formas, working with lenders, or evaluating acquisition targets is a strong plus.

People skills

Warm, professional communicator. Comfortable interfacing with sellers, residents, vendors, and lenders — often in the same day. Discretion and care matter here, especially with senior residents.

Generalist mindset

Equally comfortable with a deal spreadsheet and a community calendar. Doesn’t need a narrow lane. Enjoys variety and can prioritize across competing tasks without losing things.

Self-directed

This is a remote role on a small team. You’ll need to manage your own workload, surface issues proactively, and work without close supervision most of the time.

Systems thinking

When you do a task twice, you write it down the third time. Interested in building processes, not just completing them. Comfortable with ambiguity in a growing organization.

Nice to have

Background in senior living, aging services, or community development. Familiarity with RAL-scale or residential assisted living concepts. Experience evaluating your own real estate deals or managing your own portfolio. Interest in the coliving movement.

Working at Roseau Ford

Small team, high trust, direct access to leadership. This is not a siloed role — you’ll see the full picture of how investment projects come together, from deal sourcing through resident move-in. As the portfolio grows, the natural evolution of this role is a split between the investment and capital function and the property and community function. We don’t need you to have chosen a lane yet. We value people who are honest about what they don’t know, curious enough to figure it out, and reliable enough that things don’t fall through the cracks.

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation commensurate with experience ($1500 - $1800 monthly)
  • Opportunity for performance-based bonuses as the company grows
  • Direct mentorship from the founder and CEO
  • 21 days of paid time off
  • Health benefits

title: Research Analyst - Analyste de recherche
description:
About the Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages (OCIL)

The Office of the Commissioner of Indigenous Languages is dedicated to promoting and championing Indigenous languages by supporting the efforts of Indigenous Peoples across Canada to reclaim, revitalize, maintain, and strengthen their languages.

Our national team is passionate about our work, and the difference we make with the research, resources and innovation we develop collaboratively with partners and share with Indigenous communities. We have policies in place to ensure a welcoming, safe and respectful workplace, as well as rigorous standards for transparency and accountability.

Our Vision: All Indigenous languages in Canada are safe, vibrant, and thriving.

Our Guiding Principles

  1. There is an urgent need for concerted efforts and investments toward the revitalization of Indigenous languages to arrest and reverse the erosion that has already occurred. Research shows that no Indigenous language in Canada is safe and that all are in varying stages of endangerment.
  2. Indigenous languages are fundamental to the identities, cultures, spirituality, relationships to the land, worldviews, and self-determination of Indigenous peoples.
  3. Indigenous languages have and continue to contribute to the strength of Canada as a whole, including biodiversity and the richness of linguistic and cultural heritage. The Commission is committed to protecting the vitality of all Indigenous languages, including sign languages and sleeping languages.

We welcome interest by qualified candidates as we expand our national team to launch new, exciting projects and to meet growing organizational needs.



About the Role

Reporting to the Knowledge Hub Manager, the Research Analyst supports the planning, coordination, implementation, and documentation of research projects that advance Indigenous language revitalization, preservation, and promotion. The position contributes to research activities by organizing project information, conducting research and environmental scans, tracking deliverables, supporting committees and partnerships, and preparing research products and reports.

The Research Analyst plays an important role in ensuring research activities are well coordinated, timelines are maintained, and knowledge generated through research initiatives is documented and accessible for use by Indigenous communities, partners, and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

Research Coordination and Support

  • Coordinate research activities, project schedules, and deliverables across multiple initiatives.
  • Support the implementation of research work plans and project timelines.
  • Assist with the administration and coordination of research committees, advisory groups, and working groups.
  • Monitor project milestones and support reporting requirements.
  • Maintain project documentation, records, and research files.
  • Coordinate meetings, consultations, and engagement activities with partners and stakeholders.
  • Works effectively across teams and contributes to Knowledge Hub and organizational priorities.

Research Analysis

  • Conduct literature reviews, environmental scans, and jurisdictional analyses.
  • Compile, organize, and analyze qualitative and quantitative data.
  • Support the development of research reports, discussion papers, briefing notes, and presentations.
  • Summarize research findings and identify key themes, trends, and opportunities.
  • Assist in developing evidence-based recommendations to support organizational priorities

Stakeholder and Partnership Support

  • Support relationships with Indigenous communities, organizations, researchers, academic institutions, and partner organizations.
  • Coordinate information requests and facilitate communication between project partners.
  • Assist in planning and delivering workshops, meetings, and engagement sessions.
  • Contribute to collaborative research initiatives and knowledge-sharing activities.

Knowledge Management

  • Maintain research databases, repositories, and project records.
  • Ensure research materials are properly catalogued, organized, and accessible.
  • Support the development of knowledge products including research summaries, fact sheets, and briefing materials.
  • Contribute to the dissemination of research findings through reports, presentations, and digital resources.

Indigenous Research and Data Governance

  • Support research activities in accordance with Indigenous data sovereignty principles, OCAP® principles, and ethical research practices.
  • Assist with data collection, documentation, and management processes.
  • Ensure research activities respect community protocols and Indigenous ways of knowing.

Knowledge Mobilization



  • Translate research findings into accessible products for diverse audiences.
  • Support the development of reports, fact sheets, toolkits, dashboards, and knowledge resources.
  • Contribute to public awareness and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
  • Provide strategic advice to support evidence-informed decision-making throughout the organization.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Indigenous Studies, Public Policy, Social Sciences, Linguistics, Education, Information Studies, Research Methods, or a related field.
  • Minimum three years of experience supporting research, policy, program, or knowledge management initiatives.
  • Experience working with Indigenous communities, organizations, governments, or research environments is considered an asset.
  • Equivalent combination of education lived experience, and professional experience will be considered.

Knowledge Skills and Competencies

  • Strong research, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Knowledge of qualitative and quantitative research methods.
  • Experience conducting literature reviews and environmental scans.
  • Strong organizational and project coordination skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and competing deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, SharePoint, Teams, and research databases.
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships with diverse partners and stakeholders.
  • Understanding of Indigenous languages, cultures, histories, and communities.
  • Knowledge of Indigenous research methodologies and data governance principles.



Assets

  • Knowledge of one or more Indigenous languages.
  • Proficiency in an Indigenous language and bilingualism (English/French).



What We Offer

The Commission offers a competitive benefits package, including medical and dental benefits and a pension plan, three weeks paid holidays to begin, plus additional paid days off through the year, including federal and provincial holidays. The Commission offers a wonderful, supportive work environment, with opportunities for career development, mentorship, and professional development.

The Commission recognizes that our success requires us to have a workforce that reflects the community we serve, and diversity in its widest context, one where all people, regardless of difference, are valued and respected.

Preference will be given to Indigenous applicants in accordance with section 16(1) of the Canadian Human Rights Act. Candidates are encouraged to self-identify in their cover letter.

À propos du Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones (OCIL)

Le Bureau du Commissaire aux langues autochtones s'engage à promouvoir et défendre les langues autochtones en soutenant les efforts des peuples autochtones à travers le Canada pour reconquérir, revitaliser, maintenir et renforcer leurs langues.

Notre équipe nationale est passionnée par notre travail et par la différence que nous faisons grâce à la recherche, aux ressources et à l'innovation que nous développons en collaboration avec des partenaires et partageons avec les communautés autochtones. Nous avons mis en place des politiques pour assurer un milieu de travail accueillant, sécuritaire et respectueux, ainsi que des normes rigoureuses de transparence et de responsabilité.

Notre vision : Toutes les langues autochtones au Canada sont sécuritaires, vibrantes et florissantes.

Nos principes directeurs

  1. Il est urgent de déployer des efforts et des investissements concertés pour la revitalisation des langues autochtones afin d'arrêter et d'inverser l'érosion déjà survenue. La recherche démontre qu'aucune langue autochtone au Canada n'est sécuritaire et que toutes sont à différents stades de danger.
  2. Les langues autochtones sont fondamentales pour les identités, les cultures, la spiritualité, les relations avec la terre, les visions du monde et l'autodétermination des peuples autochtones.
  3. Les langues autochtones ont contribué et continuent de contribuer à la force du Canada dans son ensemble, y compris la biodiversité et la richesse du patrimoine linguistique et culturel. La Commission s'engage à protéger la vitalité de toutes les langues autochtones, y compris les langues des signes et les langues du sommeil.

Nous accueillons l'intérêt des candidats qualifiés alors que nous élargissons notre équipe nationale pour lancer de nouveaux projets passionnants et répondre aux besoins organisationnels croissants.



À propos du rôle

Relevant du gestionnaire du Knowledge Hub, l'analyste de recherche soutient la planification, la coordination, la mise en œuvre et la documentation des projets de recherche qui font progresser la revitalisation, la préservation et la promotion des langues autochtones. Le poste contribue aux activités de recherche en organisant l'information des projets, en réalisant des analyses de recherche et environnementales, en suivant les livrables, en soutenant les comités et partenariats, et en préparant des produits et rapports de recherche.

L'analyste de recherche joue un rôle important pour s'assurer que les activités de recherche sont bien coordonnées, que les échéanciers sont respectés et que les connaissances générées par les initiatives de recherche sont documentées et accessibles pour les communautés autochtones, les partenaires et les parties prenantes.

Responsabilités clés

Coordination et soutien à la recherche

  • Coordonnez les activités de recherche, les calendriers de projets et les livrables à travers plusieurs initiatives.
  • Soutenir la mise en œuvre des plans de recherche et des échéanciers des projets.
  • Aider à l'administration et à la coordination des comités de recherche, des groupes consultatifs et des groupes de travail.
  • Surveillez les jalons du projet et soutenez les exigences de rapport.
  • Maintenir la documentation, les dossiers et les dossiers de recherche du projet.
  • Coordonner des rencontres, des consultations et des activités d'engagement avec les partenaires et les parties prenantes.
  • Travaille efficacement entre équipes et contribue aux priorités du Knowledge Hub et de l'organisation.

Analyse de la recherche

  • Effectuer des revues de littérature, des analyses environnementales et des analyses juridictionnelles.
  • Compiler, organiser et analyser des données qualitatives et quantitatives.
  • Soutenir le développement de rapports de recherche, de documents de discussion, de notes d'information et de présentations.
  • Résumez les résultats de la recherche et identifiez les thèmes clés, les tendances et les opportunités.
  • Aider à élaborer des recommandations fondées sur des preuves pour soutenir les priorités organisationnelles

Soutien aux parties prenantes et aux partenariats

  • Soutenir les relations avec les communautés autochtones, les organisations, les chercheurs, les institutions académiques et les organisations partenaires.
  • Coordonnez les demandes d'information et facilitez la communication entre les partenaires du projet.
  • Aider à la planification et à la présentation d'ateliers, de réunions et de séances d'engagement.
  • Contribuer à des initiatives de recherche collaborative et à des activités de partage des connaissances.

Gestion des connaissances

  • Maintenir les bases de données de recherche, les dépôts et les dossiers de projets.
  • Assurez-vous que les documents de recherche sont correctement catalogués, organisés et accessibles.
  • Soutenir le développement de produits de connaissances, y compris des résumés de recherche, des fiches d'information et des documents d'information.
  • Contribuer à la diffusion des résultats de recherche par le biais de rapports, présentations et ressources numériques.

Recherche autochtone et gouvernance des données

  • Soutenir les activités de recherche conformément aux principes de souveraineté des données autochtones, aux principes de l'OCAP® et aux pratiques de recherche éthiques.
  • Aider à la collecte des données, à la documentation et aux processus de gestion.
  • Assurez-vous que les activités de recherche respectent les protocoles communautaires et les modes de connaissance autochtones.

Mobilisation des connaissances



  • Traduire les résultats de la recherche en produits accessibles pour des publics diversifiés.
  • Soutenir le développement de rapports, fiches d'information, trousses d'outils, tableaux de bord et ressources de connaissances.
  • Contribuer à la sensibilisation du public et aux initiatives de partage des connaissances.
  • Fournir des conseils stratégiques pour soutenir la prise de décision fondée sur des preuves à travers l'organisation.

Qualifications

Éducation et expérience

  • Baccalauréat en études autochtones, politiques publiques, sciences sociales, linguistique, éducation, études de l'information, méthodes de recherche ou domaine connexe.
  • Minimum trois ans d'expérience en soutien à la recherche, aux politiques, aux initiatives de gestion des connaissances ou en matière de programmes.
  • L'expérience de travail avec les communautés, organisations, gouvernements ou environnements de recherche autochtones est considérée comme un atout.
  • Une combinaison équivalente d'éducation, d'expérience vécue et d'expérience professionnelle sera prise en compte.

Connaissances et compétences

  • Solides compétences en recherche, en analyse et en résolution de problèmes.
  • Connaissance des méthodes de recherche qualitative et quantitative.
  • Expérience dans la réalisation de revues de littérature et d'analyses environnementales.
  • Solides compétences organisationnelles et de coordination de projets.
  • Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités et des échéances concurrentes.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale.
  • Maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office, SharePoint, Teams et des bases de données de recherche.
  • Capacité à bâtir des relations collaboratives avec des partenaires et parties prenantes diversifiées.
  • Compréhension des langues, cultures, histoires et communautés autochtones.
  • Connaissance des méthodologies de recherche autochtones et des principes de gouvernance des données.



Actifs

  • Connaissance d'une ou plusieurs langues autochtones.
  • Maîtrise d'une langue autochtone et bilinguisme (anglais/français).



Ce que nous offrons

La Commission offre un ensemble d'avantages compétitifs, incluant des prestations médicales et dentaires ainsi qu'un régime de retraite, trois semaines de congés payés pour commencer, plus des congés payés supplémentaires au cours de l'année, y compris les jours fériés fédéraux et provinciaux. La Commission offre un environnement de travail formidable et bienveillant, avec des occasions de développement de carrière, de mentorat et de développement professionnel.

La Commission reconnaît que notre succès exige que nous ayons une main-d'œuvre qui reflète la communauté que nous servons, et la diversité dans son contexte le plus large, où toutes les personnes, peu importe leurs différences, sont valorisées et respectées.

La préférence sera accordée aux demandeurs autochtones conformément à l'article 16(1) de la Loi canadienne sur les droits de la personne. Les candidats sont encouragés à s'identifier dans leur lettre de motivation.

title: 12-Month Intake Specialist
description:
New Mexico Immigrant Law Center (NMILC) is seeking a 12-Month Bilingual Intake Specialist


NMILC is a social justice organization whose mission is to advance equity and justice by empowering low-income immigrant communities through collaborative legal services, advocacy, and education. Each year we provide direct legal representation and assistance in immigration matters to thousands of immigrants and advocate for laws and policies that respect the rights of immigrants. NMILC’s model focuses on establishing relationships with local, state and national organizations and governmental institutions to expand access to legal services for historically marginalized immigrant communities.


Job Summary: The Intake Specialist serves immigrants residing in New Mexico by providing screening, information, and referrals to callers, by working directly with immigrant clients to prepare their immigration cases, by assisting legal representatives in case preparation, and by supporting the administrative functions of a busy non-profit organization. Applicants for this position must be able to handle a fast-paced, dynamic work environment and be able to work closely with other staff members and volunteers who provide back-up support. This position is meant for an individual who is organized and detail-oriented, who is compassionate and patient, and who enjoys working directly with clients.



Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Provide initial screening, information and referrals to immigrants in need of assistance (phone and in-person)
  • Gather information and data to verify eligibility for services, summarize prospective client’s legal problems, and document requests for services.
  • Apply NMILC eligibility guidelines, priorities, and current case acceptance availability to evaluate what level of assistance can be offered.
  • Work directly with immigrant clients and NMILC’s legal representatives to prepare immigration cases.
  • Enter required client data in our case management system (Legal Server).
  • Assist Remote Workshop Team to provide assistance to community members in varying immigration matters, including citizenship, green card renewals, and DACA.
    • Respond to incoming telephone calls related to the Remote Workshop Program. Make outgoing telephone calls as needed by the Remote Workshop Program.
    • In collaboration with the Remote Workshop Managerial Team, support the maintenance of systems for legal files. This includes files maintenance through Legal Server, Dropbox, and paper files.
    • Provide large-scale print, mailing and filling assistance to Remote Workshop program legal staff to ensure such jobs are completed and executed in a timely manner.
    • Provide file maintenance, storage and retrieval assistance to Remote Workshop program staff. Such assistance includes, but is not limited to, in-office physical file maintenance and storage as well as electric file maintenance.
  • Perform legal program administrative tasks to support the efficiency of a vibrant non-profit, including:
    • Provide support services to staff including logging incoming client mail, sending packets when requested, and returning calls from clients under supervision.

Qualifications:

  • Must be Bilingual (Spanish and English) and have excellent written and oral communication skills in both languages.
  • Strong interviewing skills and desire to interact with many people on a daily basis.
  • Understanding and familiarity with immigration law and processes is a plus.

  • Ability to prioritize workload to manage time, tasks, and meet deadlines in a dynamic environment.
  • Excellent client centered customer service skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Commitment to working in a diverse environment.
  • Ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Must be resilient and patient with a high level of personal integrity.

  • Must be detailed oriented, able to efficiently manage multiple tasks, work well under stress, and anticipate quickly changing needs.
  • Demonstrated commitment to immigrant rights and willingness to support NMILC’s mission, vision and values, which can be found at

Compensation and Benefits

  • Starting Rate: $21.50/hour (full-time, non-exempt), with upward adjustments for additional relevant experience.

title: Data Scientist
description:
About us

Food waste is a $1 trillion problem – costing the world over 1% of global GDP. We’re dead set on solving the problem and looking for people to help us achieve our mission. We, at Winnow, believe that food is far too valuable to waste, and that technology can transform the way we produce food. Our team is made of people who all share a passion for food and technology.

Winnow was founded in London in 2013 to help the hospitality industry prevent food waste through internet of things tools in the kitchen. We have worked with thousands of sites and are operating in over 90 countries around the world supported by our offices in London, Dubai, Singapore, Cluj-Napoca (Romania) and Chicago. We are a scale-up stage company with a strong base of clients who are rolling out our system globally. We have blue-chip customers including Accor Hotels, IKEA, IHG, Marriott, Compass Group and many others.

Winnow’s clients on average reduce waste by over 50% by value and sustain savings. Winnow works with hotels, universities and schools, staff restaurants, event/hospitality kitchens, buffets, pubs, and high street restaurants. Where the system is permanently adopted, pre-consumer waste value is reduced by 50% - 70% with no detrimental impact to the perceived quality or value of the offer to their customers. This represents a typical improvement of food cost savings of 3% to 8%, commonly a 40%+ increase in profitability for operations.

As the global leader in addressing food waste, we are committed to continue pushing the envelope on what technology can do to solve this problem. Winnow Vision, our new artificial intelligence-based technology, is trained to automatically track all food waste thrown away. It has won awards at the World Economic Forum and has received tremendous enthusiasm from our clients and the industry. You can read more about it on our website.

Winnow has recently been ranked #4 in the Global FoodTech 500 for 2025, recognising our position among the world’s leading innovators at the intersection of food, technology, and sustainability. We have also consistently been recognised in the FoodTech 500, the world’s first definitive list of global entrepreneurial talent in this space, further reinforcing our impact in the industry. Other recent accolades include being listed in the 2025 Sunday Times Best Places to Work, a recognition based on feedback from our UK team. While this award is UK-based, it reflects something global: a culture built on purpose, collaboration, and the belief that businesses can - and should - tackle real-world problems while being great places to work. Winnow was also named among Impact 50’s most impactful companies to work for. You can read more about it here.

We are passionate about living our values and place them at the centre of everything we do. We are excited about like minded talent who share these values, joining us in our mission:

Equal parts head and heart. We’re both passionate and measured. We carefully balance the need for quick solutions and pragmatism with the ability to step back, take in the bigger picture and build for the long term.

Bravely honest. With each other, that means we’re a transparent organisation where healthy, respectful debate is encouraged. With our customers, we challenge them if we don’t think they’re achieving their goals, whether they be environmental or financial.

People of action. Done is better than perfect, and we learn by boldly doing then rapidly improving. We’re breaking new ground, so we know things might go wrong. But we judge ourselves and each other on our reaction and our resilience.

Bound by food. We’re a diverse bunch, but our belief in the value of food is the common thread in everything we do. With each other, we celebrate through our love and respect for food. With our customers, it means we work hard to develop creative tools to make it easy for chefs to value food.

Hungry and humble. Our product is revolutionary, our people are impressive, and we’re hungry for change. But, we’re just the catalyst for a bigger movement. We stay humble regardless of our success, and make chefs the heroes in this journey.

People and planet positive. We’re caretakers of the planet, helping to preserve and support it for now and the future. Our work already minimises the impact that the hospitality industry has on the planet, and we’re also committed to actively reducing our own footprint while doing so. We’re leaving the planet and its people better off than we found them.

This is an opportunity to join an exciting organisation and help us propel our growth at what are truly the most exciting and dynamic points in time in our business. You will work alongside a driven team who are motivated by building an exciting business and leaving the world a better place than we found it.

About the team

The Data team plays a critical role in the continuous improvement of our flagship product - Winnow Vision. We've collected millions of images of food items already, and keep collecting thousands every day from the kitchens we operate in. Those images need to be processed, curated and structured to optimise the quality and accuracy of our AI models. Managing this big data pipeline is no easy task: we operate across the world, in a wide variety of industries and our model needs to recognize food ranging from the Malay Nasi Goreng to the American fried chicken, and everything else in between.

We have come a long way - from long data collection time and training small AI models for very specific clients, we have now managed to generalise our approach and can now deploy AI models to almost any kitchen in the world in a matter of a couple of weeks. However, there are still many challenges ahead - today we present a top selection of items to our clients and they confirm the right one - our ambition is to become completely touch less. How can we make our models more confident and more accurate, that is the question!

We are investing in developing new products and services, and this role is responsible for leading data analysis for these innovations.

About the role:

As a Data Scientist, you will be reporting to the Data Scientist Lead and will have a wide range of responsibilities which includes:

  • Use your data skills to enhance the confidence and accuracy for our AI models
  • Developing and refining complex queries and reports to help other team members execute their roles
  • Performing ongoing data analysis to present back insights to clients
  • Shape our data processes to optimize efficiency while reducing costs
  • Imagine and deliver insightful analysis aiming at improving our user experience
  • Monitor and manage the existing fleet of models in the field, and ensure new clients benefit from AI no less than 1 month after installation
  • Produce and track key performance indicators
  • Take on more complex data analysis problems

Requirements

Excellent numerical and analytical skills

  • Strong knowledge in SQL and Python required and willingness to learn more
  • Experience handling large data sets
  • Experience visualising large datasets
  • Experience with AWS
  • Experience using Claude to simplify and streamline tasks
  • Comfortable using macros and formulas such as vlookups, sumifs, and pivot tables
  • Experience with Grafana, JupyterHub, postgreSQL is a plus
  • A willingness to learn and suggest machine learning approaches to solving data problems

Effective verbal and written communication skills

  • Ability to turn data into insights and present these insights effectively
  • Ability to adapt communication style to suit different audiences
  • Ability to facilitate group discussions
  • Attention to detail. Ability to develop accurate written materials
  • Action oriented. Ability to follow-up on feedback to ensure positive outcomes
  • Comfortable training others to develop data skills

Pro-active and critical thinker

  • Ability to think out of the box and not afraid to speak up
  • Ability to create new processes from scratch
  • Ability to influence others to follow best practices
  • Flexible and willing to take on new challenges as they emerge

Benefits

  • Company stock options package
  • Meal tickets - 40 RON per working day
  • 2 Wellness hours per month plus a 274 RON gross monthly wellness allowance or the option to swap the wellness allowance for a 7Card subscription
  • 25 days of paid vacation time in addition to national holidays, plus the option to buy a further 5 days annual leave
  • Company part-funded private health insurance and eye care allowance
  • Life insurance (3 times base salary)
  • Employee Assistance Programme - 24/7 helpline for your wellbeing
  • Learning and development allowance of 1,730 RON annually
  • Hybrid way of working - we’re all in the office on Wednesdays and Thursdays
  • Company provided breakfast & snacks on office days
  • Early Finish Fridays - log off at 3 PM on a Friday if you have completed your tasks by then
  • Our own office space with a great working environment
  • You will love what you do – waking up every day solving one of the biggest social problems of our generation - food waste
  • Committed team members with broad experience who share a common passion to build a world class business

title: Configuration Engineer - PLM
description:
Configuration Engineer

At OQC, we aren’t just theorising about the future; we’re building it. Born from a philosophy of bold innovation, we’ve transitioned quantum computing from an academic ambition into a commercial reality—and we’re just getting started.

The Purpose

Ensure the hardware information behind OQC’s quantum computers is accurate, controlled and fully traceable throughout the engineering lifecycle.

As a Configuration Engineer, you’ll own day-to-day configuration data, engineering Bills of Materials and hardware release records. You’ll support effective design governance and change control while helping mature and standardise the PLM and PDM processes that enable our engineering teams to release hardware information efficiently and reliably.

The Role

Working within Engineering Operations and reporting to the Head of Design Engineering, you’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering, Operations and Supply Chain. You’ll manage the information that defines released hardware configurations, ensuring product structures, drawings, specifications and revisions remain complete, consistent and traceable.

You’ll work across Arena PLM, SolidWorks PDM, CAD data and downstream systems, resolving discrepancies and supporting Engineering Change Request and Engineering Change Order workflows. You’ll also spend regular time in laboratory and workshop environments to understand physical hardware builds and ensure deviations, part usage and configuration changes are reflected accurately in released records.

What You’ll Be Working On

  • Structure and maintain accurate multi-level engineering Bills of Materials, ensuring product structures reflect released engineering intent.
  • Maintain hardware release records and configuration data across components, assemblies and product revisions.
  • Facilitate Engineering Change Request and Engineering Change Order workflows, ensuring changes are properly recorded, progressed and traceable.
  • Review technical release packages for completeness and configuration accuracy before drawings, specifications and engineering data are released.
  • Administer Arena PLM and SolidWorks PDM workflows, including lifecycle states, routing, permissions and configuration data.
  • Maintain alignment across CAD, PDM, PLM and downstream systems, working with functional owners to resolve data and configuration discrepancies.
  • Improve configuration-management, engineering-change and hardware-release processes by developing clearer workflows, guidance and conventions.

What We’re Looking For

  • Experience managing engineering product data, configuration information or Bills of Materials.
  • Experience working with formal engineering change-control processes.
  • Hands-on experience using PLM or PDM systems for day-to-day engineering-data management.
  • Experience identifying and resolving BOM, release-data or configuration discrepancies across multiple teams.
  • Strong technical-document and release-management skills.
  • A clear understanding of data accuracy, revision control and configuration traceability.
  • Strong problem-solving, planning and organisational skills.
  • The ability to communicate effectively with engineering, operations and supply-chain stakeholders.
  • Excellent attention to detail, adaptability and a willingness to share knowledge with colleagues.
  • Strong hands-on technical experience within engineering operations, configuration management or a related environment. A relevant engineering or operations degree would be beneficial.

The ‘Nice-to-Haves’

  • Experience administering PLM or PDM workflows, lifecycle states, user permissions or release processes.
  • Hands-on experience with Arena PLM and SolidWorks PDM.
  • Knowledge of CAD-to-PDM or PLM integrations and engineering-data relationships.
  • Familiarity with ERP integration or downstream manufacturing-data flows.
  • Experience maintaining or contributing to manufacturing Bills of Materials.
  • Experience configuring PLM or PDM workflows and supporting CAD, ERP or manufacturing-system integrations.

Why Join OQC

You’ll join an Engineering Operations team supporting the development and release of highly complex quantum-computing hardware. This is an opportunity to work closely with both engineering data and physical products, improving the controls that connect design intent with real-world hardware builds.

You’ll have the chance to shape and mature OQC’s configuration-management processes, improve consistency across multiple engineering systems and help create the reliable product information needed to develop and scale our quantum technology.

title: Assessment Center Lead Youth Care Specialist
description:
Position Function:

The Primary function of a Lead Youth Care Specialist is to provide direct care, youth behavior support and ensure smooth daily routines. The Lead Youth Care Specialist will serve as the on-shift leader who provides structure, models best practices, supports frontline staff, and ensures youth receive high-quality care and supervision. The position should be on the floor working with youth and modeling for YCS at least 90% of their shift.


Requirements:

Education: High School Diploma or GED required; bachelor’s degree in a human service field preferred. One year of direct care experience required. One year experience in TBRI or other similar models of care preferred. Must possess a valid Texas driver’s license and be willing to transport clients.


Program & Shift Operations:

  • Serve as the on-shift point person, coordinating staff assignments, responsibilities, transportation needs and youth supervision needs.
  • Ensure staff follow all daily routines, schedules, treatment guidelines, and care plans.
  • Monitor household operations to maintain a welcoming, clean, safe, and trauma-informed environment at all times.
  • Lead shift change meetings in the absence of the Shift Supervisor.
  • Communicate shift concerns, incidents, patterns, or safety updates to the Shift Supervisor promptly.
  • Ensure staff are informed and ready to execute safety plans, Attachment A information, and youth-specific needs before beginning the shift.
  • Support the completion of all required program paperwork and documentation.
  • Administer medications according to agency protocols and maintain accurate medication logs.
  • Ensure compliance with DFPS minimum standards, licensing expectations, and agency protocols during each shift.


Client Care & Youth Support:

  • Provide direct supervision, care, and TBRI-aligned engagement with youth during daily routines and activities
  • Model TBRI-aligned appropriate supervision, engagement, emotional support, and behavioral expectations for all youth.
  • Directly support clients who are exhibiting behavioral challenges, as needed, modeling interventions for staff.
  • Participate in and ensure appropriate implementation of structured programming, life-skills development, recreational activities, and therapeutic routines in collaboration with the clinical team.
  • Ensure all youth basic needs are met, including meals, hygiene, clothing, sleep, transportation, and medication routines.
  • Respond to youth behaviors using trauma-informed strategies, providing de-escalation and crisis support as needed.
  • Build consistent, trust-based relationships with youth that promote safety, respect, and accountability.
  • Promote normalcy by helping youth access everyday opportunities, such as hobbies, peer interactions, and community activities, to build confidence and support healthy development aligned with their individual therapeutic treatment needs.


Staff Guidance & Teamwork:

Documentation & Communication:

Collaboration & Community Relations:
